children.text: Vaidya 1
Suvikrāntavikrāmiparipṛcchā nāma
children.translated_text: The Inquiry of <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, namely

children.text: sārdhadvisāhasrikā prajñāpāramitā /
children.translated_text: the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) in Two Thousand Five Hundred Lines.

children.text: START Svp 1
children.translated_text: [START Svp 1]

children.text: 1 nidānaparivartaḥ /
children.translated_text: 1. The <s>Nidāna</s> Chapter (Introduction).

children.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣuśataiḥ, aprameyāsaṃkhyaiśca bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ nānābuddhakṣetrasaṃnipatitairekajātipratibaddhaiḥ / tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavānanekaśatasahasrayā parṣadā parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto dharmaṃ deśayati sma //
children.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrels' Feeding Ground), together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), twelve hundred and fifty <s>bhikṣus</s>, and with immeasurable and countless <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who had assembled from various <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) and were bound to one more birth. At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded and honored by an assembly of many hundreds of thousands, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: atha khalu tasyāmeva parṣadi suvikrāntavikrāmī nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ saṃnipatito 'bhūtsaṃniṣaṇṇaḥ / sa utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - pṛccheyamahaṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kaṃcideva pradeśam, saced bhagavānavakāśaṃ kuryāt pṛṣṭaśca praśnavyākaraṇāya / evamukte bhagavān suvikrāntavikrāmiṇaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - pṛccha tvaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmiṃstathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ yadyadevākāṅkṣasi / ahaṃ te tasya tasyaiva praśna(sya) vyākaraṇena cittamārādhayiṣyāmi //
children.translated_text: Then, in that very assembly, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> had assembled and was seated. He rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'I would ask the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, about a certain matter, if the <s>Bhagavān</s> would grant me the opportunity to answer the question asked.' Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>: 'Ask, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, whatever you wish. I shall satisfy your mind with an answer to each and every question.'

children.text: evamukte suvikrāntavikrāmī bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - prajñāpāramitā prajñāpāramiteti bhagavannucyate / kiyatā bhagavan bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitā prajñāpāramitetyucyate? kathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati? kathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ prajñāpāramitābhāvanā paripūriṃ gacchati? kathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayato māraḥ pāpīyānavatāraṃ (na) labhate, sarvamārakarmāṇi cāvabudhyate? kīdṛgrūpaiśva bhagavan prajñāpāramitāvihārairviharan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṣipraṃ sarvajñatādharmaparipūrimadhigacchati?
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, it is said, <s>Bhagavān</s>. To what extent, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? How, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> practice <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? How, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> reach fulfillment for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? How, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does <s>Māra</s> the Evil One fail to find an opening against a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who cultivates <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and how does he see through all the works of <s>Māra</s>? And with what kind of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> practices, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> quickly attain the fulfillment of all qualities of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>)?'

children.text: evamukte bhagavān suvikrāntavikrāmiṇaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - sādhu sādhu suvikrāntavikrāmin, yastvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ paripṛcchasi bodhisattvānāṃ (
Vaidya 2
children.translated_text: [Vaidya 2]

children.text: ) mahāsattvānāmarthāya, yathāpi nāma tvaṃ bahujanahitāya pratipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca, etarhyanāgatānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmālokaṃ kartukāma iti //
children.translated_text: ) <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. It is indeed as though you have set out for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of beings, of gods and humans, and that you wish to create illumination for <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> of the present and the future.'

Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>: 'Well done, well done, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, that you ask the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One about <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for the benefit of <s>Bodhisattva</s> (

children.text: atha khalu bhagavān jānanneva suvikrāntavikrāmiṇaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ paripṛcchati sma - kiṃ tvaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin arthavaśaṃ saṃpaśyaṃstathāgatametadarthaṃ paripṛcchasi? evamukte suvikrāntavikrāmī bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - sarvasattvānāṃ vayaṃ bhagavannarthāya tathāgatametamarthaṃ paripṛcchāmaḥ sarvasattvahitāya sarvasattvānukampāyai / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prajñāpāramitā bhagavan sarvadharmāṇāṃ grāhikā yaduta śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvasamyaksaṃbuddhadharmāṇām / ato bhagavaṃstathāgataviṣayaṃ tathāgatajñānaṃ ca nirdiśatu / tatra ye sattvā niyatāḥ śrāvakayāne bhaviṣyanti, te kṣipramanāsravāṃ bhūmiṃ sākṣātkariṣyanti / ye pratyekabuddhayāne niyatā bhaviṣyanti, te kṣipraṃ pratyekabuddhayānena niryāsyanti / ye anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ saṃprasthitāḥ, te kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante / ye ca anavakrāntasamyaktvaniyāmā aniyatāstisṛṣu bhūmiṣu, te śrutvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayiṣyanti / sarvasattvānāṃ ca bhagavan kuśalamūlasaṃjananaṃ kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati tathāgatena imaṃ prajñāpāramitāpraśnaṃ visarjayatā / na ca vayaṃ bhagavan hīnādhimuktikānāṃ sattvānāṃ kṛtaśastathāgataṃ paripṛcchāmaḥ, na daridracittānām, na daridramānasasamanvāgatānām, na kusīdānām, na kausīdyābhibhūtānām, na dṛṣṭipaṅkāvasannānām, na mārapāśabaddhānām, nānapatrapāṇām, nāsaṃlekhasamanvāgatānām, na muṣitasmṛtīnām, na bhrāntacittānām, na kāmapaṅkamagnānām, na śaṭhānām, na māyāvinām, nākṛtajñānām, na pāpecchānām, na pāpasamācārāṇām, na śīlavipannānām, nāpariśuddhaśīlānām, na dṛṣṭivipannānām, na māragocaracāriṇām, nātmotkarṣakāṇām, na parapaṃsakānām, na lābhasatkāragurukāṇām, na pātracīvarādhyavasitānām, na kuhakānām, na lapakānām, na naimittikānām, na naiṣpeṣikāṇām, na lābhena lābhacikīrṣukāṇām / na vayaṃ bhagavan evaṃrūpāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ kṛtaśastathāgataṃ paripṛcchāmaḥ / ye punarbhagavan sattvāḥ sarvajñajñānaṃ prārthayanti, asaṅgajñānaṃ svayaṃbhūjñānamasamajñānamanuttarajñānaṃ prārthayante, ye nātmānamupalabhante na param, kutaḥ punarātmānamutkarṣayiṣyanti paraṃ vā pasaṃyiṣyanti, teṣāṃ nihatamānānāṃ vayaṃ bhagavaṃśchinnaviṣāṇavṛṣabhopamānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmāvrīḍhaśalyānāṃ nīcamānasānāṃ caṇḍālakumārakopamacittānāṃ pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśasamacitānāṃ bhagavan sattvānāmarthāya tathāgataṃ paripṛcchāmo bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām / ye dharmamapi nopalabhante nābhiniviśante kutaḥ punaradharmam, teṣāṃ vayaṃ bhagavannarthāya tathāgataṃ paripṛcchāmo bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmāśayaśuddhānāmaśaṭhānāmamāyāvināmṛjukānāṃ samacittānāṃ sarvasattvahitāmukampakānāṃ samādāpakānāṃ samuttejakānāṃ saṃpraharṣakāṇāṃ mahābhāravāhikānāṃ mahāyānasamārūḍhānāṃ mahākṛtyena pratyupasthitānāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ sarvasattvahitasukhāvahānāṃ nāyakānāṃ vināyakānāṃ pariṇāyakānāṃ sarvadharmāniśritavihārikāṇāṃ sarvopapattyāyatanānarthikānāṃ sarvamārapāśavinirmuktānāṃ (
Vaidya 3
children.translated_text: [Vaidya 3]

children.text: ) chandikānāṃ vīryavatāmapramattānāṃ sarvadharmaparamapāramiprāptānāṃ sarvasaṃśayacchedanakuśalānām / (teṣāṃ) vayaṃ bhagavan sattvānāṃ kṛtaśastathāgataṃ paripṛcchāmo bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām / ye te bhagavan sattvā bodhijñānamapi na manyante nābhiniviśante nādhyavasāya tiṣṭhanti, sarvamanyanāsamatikrāntā mārgasthitā mārgapratipannā mārgadaiśikāḥ, teṣāṃ vayaṃ bhagavan sattvānāṃ kṛtaśastathāgataṃ paripṛcchāmo bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ ca / sarvasattvānāṃ vayaṃ bhagavannarthāya hitāya sukhāya yogakṣemāya tathāgataṃ paripṛcchāmaḥ, sarvasattvānāṃ vayaṃ bhagavan sukhamupasaṃhartukāmā anuttarasukhaṃ niruttarasukhaṃ nirvāṇasukhaṃ buddhasukhamasaṃskṛtasukham / tena vayaṃ bhagavan sarvasattvānāṃ saṃśayacchittyarthaṃ tathāgataṃ paripṛcchāmaḥ / niḥsaṃśayā vayaṃ bhagavan bhavitukāmāḥ, niḥsaṃśayāśca bhagavan sarvasattvebhyaḥ saṃśayaprahāṇāya dharmaṃ deśayitukāmāḥ / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? sarvasattvā hi bhagavan sukhakāmā duḥkhapratikūlāḥ, sarvasattvāḥ sukhenārthikāḥ / na ca vayaṃ bhagavan sarvasattvānāṃ kiṃcidanyatsukhaṃ samanupaśyāmo 'nyatra prajñātaḥ / na cānyatkiṃcidbhagavan sarvasattvānāṃ sukhamasti anyatra bodhisattvayānānmahāyānāt / tena vayaṃ bhagavan imamarthavaśaṃ saṃpaśyantaḥ sattvānāṃ sukhamupasaṃhartukāmāḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ paripṛcchāmaḥ / bodhisattvānāṃ caitamarthaṃ bhagavan samanupaśyadbhirasmābhistathāgata etamarthaṃ paripṛṣṭaḥ //
children.translated_text: ) of those who are heroic, energetic, vigilant, who have attained the supreme perfection of all <s>dharmas</s>, who are skilled in cutting through all doubts. On behalf of those beings, Blessed One, we ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> about the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>. Those beings, Blessed One, who do not conceive of even <s>bodhi</s>-knowledge, do not cling to it, do not abide in attachment to it, who have transcended all conceiving, who stand on the path, follow the path, and are guides on the path — on behalf of those beings, Blessed One, we ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> about the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>. For the sake of all beings, Blessed One — for their welfare, benefit, happiness, and security — we ask the <s>Tathāgata</s>. We wish to bring happiness to all beings, Blessed One — unsurpassed happiness, supreme happiness, the happiness of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the happiness of Buddhahood, unconditioned happiness. Therefore, Blessed One, for the sake of cutting through the doubts of all beings, we ask the <s>Tathāgata</s>. We wish to become free from doubt, Blessed One, and being free from doubt, Blessed One, we wish to teach the <s>Dharma</s> to all beings for the abandonment of doubt. Why is that? For all beings, Blessed One, desire happiness and are averse to suffering; all beings seek happiness. And we do not see, Blessed One, any other happiness for all beings apart from <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom). Nor is there, Blessed One, any other happiness for all beings apart from the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle, the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Therefore, Blessed One, seeing this purpose, wishing to bring happiness to beings, we ask about the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). And seeing this purpose for the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, Blessed One, we have asked the <s>Tathāgata</s> about this matter.

Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, although already knowing, questioned the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>: 'Do you, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, perceiving a purpose, ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> about this matter?' Thus addressed, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'We, <s>Bhagavān</s>, ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> about this matter for the benefit of all beings, for the welfare of all beings, out of compassion for all beings. For what reason? <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, encompasses all <s>dharmas</s>, namely the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and Perfectly Awakened Ones. Therefore, <s>Bhagavān</s>, let the <s>Tathāgata</s> expound the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Those beings who are determined upon the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle shall quickly realize the stage free from defilements. Those who are determined upon the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle shall quickly progress through the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle. Those who have set out for supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) shall quickly attain supreme perfect awakening. And those who have not yet entered the certainty of the correct path and are undetermined in the three stages, upon hearing this, shall generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening. And for all beings, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the generation of roots of merit will have been accomplished by the <s>Tathāgata</s> through answering this question on <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. We do not, <s>Bhagavān</s>, ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> for the sake of beings of inferior aspiration, nor for those of impoverished minds, nor for those endowed with impoverished mentality, nor for the lazy, nor for those overcome by sloth, nor for those sunk in the mire of wrong views, nor for those bound by the snares of <s>Māra</s>, nor for the shameless, nor for those lacking self-discipline, nor for those whose mindfulness is stolen, nor for those of deluded minds, nor for those sunk in the mire of sense-desires, nor for the deceitful, nor for the fraudulent, nor for the ungrateful, nor for those of evil wishes, nor for those of evil conduct, nor for those whose morality is broken, nor for those whose morality is impure, nor for those of broken views, nor for those who range in <s>Māra</s>'s domain, nor for those who exalt themselves, nor for those who disparage others, nor for those who value gain and honor, nor for those preoccupied with bowl and robes, nor for the hypocritical, nor for the garrulous, nor for those who seek omens, nor for the presumptuous, nor for those who seek gain through gain. We do not, <s>Bhagavān</s>, ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> for the sake of beings of such character. Rather, <s>Bhagavān</s>, for those beings who aspire to omniscient knowledge, who aspire to unattached knowledge, self-born knowledge, unequaled knowledge, unsurpassed knowledge, who do not apprehend self or other — how much less would they exalt themselves or disparage others! — for the sake of those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> whose pride is destroyed, who are like bulls with broken horns, whose thorn of shame is extracted, who are of humble mind, whose minds are like those of <s>caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) children, whose minds are equal to earth, water, fire, wind, and space, <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the sake of such beings we ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> about <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> — those who do not apprehend even <s>dharma</s>, much less non-<s>dharma</s>. For the sake of those, <s>Bhagavān</s>, we ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> about <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> whose intentions are pure, who are without deceit, without fraud, who are upright, even-minded, compassionate toward the welfare of all beings, who encourage, rouse, and delight others, who bear great burdens, who have mounted the great vehicle (<s>Mahāyāna</s>), who are engaged in the great task, who are greatly compassionate, who bring welfare and happiness to all beings, who are leaders, guides, and conductors, who dwell without relying on any <s>dharmas</s>, who have no desire for any realm of rebirth, who are completely freed from all the snares of <s>Māra</s> (

children.text: evamukte bhagavām suvikrāntavikrāmiṇaṃ bodhisattvāṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - sādhu sādhu suvikrāntavikrāmin / guṇānāṃ te na sukaraḥ paryanto 'dhigantum, yastvaṃ tathāgataṃ mahato janakāyasyānukampayā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ paripṛcchasi / tena hi tvaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru, bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti suvikrāntavikrāmī bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ////
children.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One spoke to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>: 'Well done, well done, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>! The limit of your virtues is not easy to reach, in that you, out of compassion for the great multitude of beings, ask about this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Therefore, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, listen well and carefully attend; I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One' — the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> assented to the Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavānetadavocat - yattvaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin evaṃ vadasi - prajñāpāramitā prajñāpāramiteti bhagavannucyate, kiyatā bhagavan bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitetyucyata iti, na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin kenaciddharmeṇa prajñāpāramitā vacanīyā / sarvavacanātikrāntā hi prajñāpāramitā / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā śakyate vaktum - iyaṃ sā prajñāpāramitā, asya vā prajñāpāramitā, anena vā prajñāpāramitā, asmādvā prajñāpāramitā / apāramitaiṣā suvikrāntavikrāmin sarvadharmāṇām, tenocyate prajñāpāramiteti / prajñaiva suvikrāntavikrāmiṃstathāgatena na labdhā, nopalabdhā, kutaḥ punaḥ prajñāpāramitāmupalapsyate? prajñeti suvikrāntavikrāmin ajñaiṣā sarvadharmāṇām, ajānanaiṣā sarvadharmāṇām, tenocyate prajñeti / katamā ca suvikrāntavikrāmin ajānanā sarvadharmāṇām? anyathaite sarvadharmā anyathābhilapyante, na cābhilāpavinirmuktāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / yā ca ajñā sarvadharmāṇām, yā ca ajānanā sarvadharmāṇām, na sā śakyā vācā vaktum / api tu yathā sattvā ajānanāḥ, tenocyate prajñeti / prajñāptirityevocyate, tenocyate prajñeti / sarvadharmāśca suvikrāntavikrāmin aprajñapanīyāḥ, apravartyāḥ, anirdeśyāḥ adṛśyāśca / yaivamajānanā, iyamucyate ajānaneti / prajñeti suvikrāntavikrāmin naiṣā ajñā nāpyanajñā, nāpyajñānajñā, tatastenocyate prajñeti / (
Vaidya 4
children.translated_text: [<s>Vaidya</s> 4]

children.text: ) [na]) jñānagocara eṣa suvikrāntavikrāmin, nājñānagocaraḥ / nājñānaviṣayo nāpi jñānaviṣayaḥ / aviṣayo hi jñānam / sacedajñānaviṣayaḥ syāta, ajñānaṃ syāt / na jñānamajñānataḥ, nāpi jñānato 'jñānam, nāpi jñānamajñānam, nāpyajñānaṃ jñānam / nājñānena jñānamityucyate, nāpi jñānena jñānamityucyate / ajñānena hi jñānamityucyate, na tu tatra kiṃcidajñānaṃ yacchakyamādarśayitum - idaṃ tajjñānam, asya vā tajjñānam, anena vā tajjñānam / tena tajjñānaṃ jñānatvena na saṃvidyate, nāpi tajjñānaṃ tattvenāvasthitam, nāpyajñānaṃ jñānamityucyate / sacedajñānena jñānamityucyeta, tataḥ sarve bālapṛthagjanā jñānino bhaveyuḥ / api tu jñānājñānānupalabdhito jñānājñānaṃ yathābhūtaparijñā / tadeva jñānamityucyate, na punaryathocyate tathā tajjñānam / tatkasmāt? na hi jñānaṃ vacanīyam, nāpi jñānaṃ kasyacidviṣayaḥ / sarvaviṣayavyatikrāntaṃ hi jñānam, na ca jñānaṃ viṣayam (yaḥ?) / ayaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin jñānanirdeśaḥ, adeśo 'pradeśaḥ, yena jñānenāsau jñānināṃ jñānīti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / yaivaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin prajānanā anubodhanā ajānanā, iyamucyate prajñeti / ya evaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin abhisamayaḥ, sākṣātkriyā, iyamucyate lokottarā prajñeti, na punaryathocyate lokottarā prajñeti / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? loka eva nopalabhyate, kutaḥ punarlokottarā prajñā? kaḥ punarvādo yo lokān samanuttariṣyati lokottarayā prajñayā? tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi sā lokamupalabhate, tena na kiṃciduttārayati, tenocyate lokottarā prajñeti / loka iti suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñaptirlokasamatikramaḥ / sarvaprajñaptisamatikrāntaṃ lokottaramityucyate / na ca punarlokottaramuttaraṇam, anuttaraṇaṃ lokottaram / tatkasya hetoḥ? aṇurapi tatra dharmo na saṃvidyate ya uttartavyo yena cottartavyaḥ / tenocyate lokottaramiti / lokottare hi na loko vidyate na lokottaram, anuttarasyānuttara(ṇa) miti, tenocyate lokottaramiti / ayamucyate suvikrāntavikrāmin lokottarāyāḥ prajñāyā nirdeśaḥ, na punaryathocyate lokottarā prajñeti / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi yā lokottarā sā vacanīyā, uttīrṇā sā / na tatra bhūyaḥ kiṃciduttartavyam, tenocyate lokottarā prajñeti //
children.translated_text: ) This is not the domain of knowledge, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, nor is it the domain of non-knowledge. It is not the object of non-knowledge, nor is it the object of knowledge. For knowledge is without object. If it were the object of non-knowledge, it would be non-knowledge. Knowledge does not come from non-knowledge, nor does non-knowledge come from knowledge; knowledge is not non-knowledge, nor is non-knowledge knowledge. It is not by non-knowledge that knowledge is called 'knowledge,' nor by knowledge that knowledge is called 'knowledge.' It is by non-knowledge that knowledge is called 'knowledge,' but therein no non-knowledge can be pointed out — 'This is that knowledge,' or 'It is of this,' or 'It is by this.' Therefore that knowledge is not found as knowledge, nor does that knowledge abide in reality, nor is non-knowledge called 'knowledge.' If knowledge were called 'knowledge' by non-knowledge, then all foolish ordinary people would be knowers. Rather, through the non-apprehension of both knowledge and non-knowledge, the true comprehension of knowledge and non-knowledge — that itself is called knowledge; but knowledge is not as it is spoken of. Why? For knowledge is beyond expression, nor is knowledge the object of anything. Knowledge transcends all objects, and knowledge is not an object. This, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the teaching of knowledge — a non-teaching, a non-indication — by which knowledge the knower is reckoned among knowers as 'a knower.' This very knowing, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, this awakening, this non-cognizing — this is called <s>Prajñā</s>. This very realization, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, this direct experience — this is called supramundane <s>Prajñā</s>; but it is not as it is called 'supramundane <s>Prajñā</s>.' Why? The world itself is not apprehended — how then supramundane <s>Prajñā</s>? And who would speak of one who would transcend the world by supramundane <s>Prajñā</s>? Why? For it does not apprehend the world; therefore it does not transcend anything — therefore it is called 'supramundane <s>Prajñā</s>.' 'World,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is a designation; 'transcendence of the world' — what transcends all designation is called 'supramundane.' But the supramundane is not transcendence; non-transcendence is the supramundane. Why? Not even the slightest <s>dharma</s> exists there that is to be transcended or by which one would transcend. Therefore it is called 'supramundane.' In the supramundane, neither the world exists nor the supramundane — the non-transcendence of the non-transcendent — therefore it is called 'supramundane.' This is called, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the teaching of supramundane <s>Prajñā</s>; but it is not as it is called 'supramundane <s>Prajñā</s>.' Why? For what is supramundane cannot be expressed — it has been transcended. There is nothing further to transcend — therefore it is called 'supramundane <s>Prajñā</s>.'

The Blessed One spoke thus: '<s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, you say "<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — thus it is called, Blessed One. In what sense, Blessed One, is it called the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>?" Indeed, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> cannot be expressed by any <s>dharma</s>. For <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> transcends all expression. It cannot be said, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>: "This is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>," or "It is of this," or "It is by this," or "It is from this." This is the non-perfection (<s>apāramitā</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> — therefore it is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. <s>Prajñā</s> itself, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, has not been found or apprehended by the <s>Tathāgata</s> — how then would one apprehend the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? "<s>Prajñā</s>," <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the non-knowing (<s>ajñā</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>, the non-cognizing of all <s>dharmas</s> — therefore it is called <s>Prajñā</s>. And what, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the non-cognizing of all <s>dharmas</s>? All these <s>dharmas</s> are one way but are expressed otherwise, yet all <s>dharmas</s> are not free from expression. That which is the non-knowing and non-cognizing of all <s>dharmas</s> cannot be spoken by words. Rather, just as beings are non-cognizing, therefore it is called <s>Prajñā</s>. It is called designation (<s>prajñapti</s>) — therefore it is called <s>Prajñā</s>. All <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, are beyond designation, beyond occurrence, beyond description, and invisible. This very non-cognizing — this is called non-cognizing. "<s>Prajñā</s>," <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> — this is neither non-knowing nor not non-knowing, nor the non-knowing of non-knowing — therefore it is called <s>Prajñā</s>. (

children.text: tatra suvikrāntavikrāmin yā nirvedhikā prajñā, kiṃ sā prajñā nirvidhyati? nātra kiṃcinnirveddhavyam / sacetkiṃcinnirveddhavyamabhaviṣyat, prajñapyeta - iyaṃ sā prajñā yā nirvidhyatīti / na kenacidvidhyate nāvidhyate, na kasyaciduttaramupalabhyate yadvidhyeta / nirvidhyatīti nātra kiṃcidvidhyati nāvidhyati, nātra kiṃcidvidhyate nāvidhyate, tenocyate nirvidhyatīti / nātra kaścidantaṃ prayāti nāpi madhyam, tenocyate nirvidhyatīti / nirvidhyati nirvedhikā prajñetyucyate nirvidhyati na kvaciddhāvati, na vidhāvati, na saṃdhāvati, tenocyate nirvedhiketi / api tu suvikrāntavikrāmin nirvedhikā prajñeti kiṃ nirvidhyati? yatkiṃciddarśanam, tatsarvaṃ nirvidhyati / kena nirvidhyati? prajñayā nirvidhyati / kimiti prajñayā nirvidhyati? prajñaptilakṣaṇamiti nirvidhyati / yatkiṃcitprajñaptilakṣaṇam, tatsarvamalakṣaṇamiti, alakṣaṇaṃ prajñaptilakṣaṇamiti / yaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin evaṃrūpayā prajñayā samanvāgato vidhyati, sa traidhātukaṃ (
Vaidya 5
children.translated_text: [<s>Vaidya</s> 5]

children.text: ) vidhyati / kathaṃ vidhyati? adhātukaṃ traidhātukamiti nirvidhyati / na hyatra kaściddhātuṃ vidhyati, sa traidhātukamadhātukamiti nirvidhyati / yenaivaṃ traidhātukaṃ nirviddham, ayamucyate nairvedhikyā prajñayā samanvāgata iti / kathaṃ ca nairvedhikyā prajñayā samanvāgataḥ? na hi kiṃcinnirveddhavyamakuśalam, sa sarvaṃ kuśalamiti nirvidhyati, nairvedhikyā prajñayā atikrāmati / sa evaṃ nairvedhikyā prajñyā samanvāgato yatkiṃcitpaśyati śṛṇoti jighrati āsvādayati spṛśati vijānīte vā, tatsarvaṃ nirvidhyati / kathaṃ nirvidhyati? anityato duḥkhato gaṇḍato rogataḥ śalyataḥ śūnyato aghata āghātataḥ parataḥ (pralopataḥ) pralopadharmataścalataḥ prabhaṅgurato 'nātmato 'nutpādato 'nirodhato 'lakṣaṇata iti / ayamucyate suvikrāntavikrāmin śītībhūtoviśalya iti / tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin viśalyā nāma bhaiṣajyajātiḥ / sā yasmin sthāpyate tataḥ sarvaśalyānyapanayati nirvidhyati, evameva evaṃrūpairdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bhikṣurviśalyaḥ śītībhūto nairvedhikyā prajñayā samanvāgataḥ saṃsārātyantavihārī nairvedhikaprajñoviraktaḥ sarvatraidhātukāt, atikrāntaḥ sarvamārapāśebhyaḥ / tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin vajraṃ yasminneva nikṣipyate nirvedhanārtham, tattadeva nirvidhyati, evameva bhikṣurvajropamasamādhinairvedhikyā prajñayā parigṛhītaṃ (cittaṃ?) yatra sthāpayati yeṣu ca pracārayati, tān sarvānnirvidhyati / sa nairvedhikyā prajñayā samanvāgato lokottarayā samyagduḥkhakṣayagāminyānuliptastravidya ityucyate / vidyeti suvikrāntavikrāmin avidyopaśamasyaitadadhivacanam, avidyāparijñeti duḥkhaskandhavyupaśamasyaitadadhivacanam / tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin vaidyaḥ paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī tantraupayikayā mīmāṃsayā samanvāgataḥ syāt sarvabhaiṣajyakuśalaḥ sarvavyādhyutpattikuśalaḥ sarvaduḥkhapramocanakaḥ / sa yaṃ yameva glānaṃ cikitsati taṃ tameva mocayat / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi sa sarvabhaiṣajyakuśalaḥ sarvavyādhyutpattikuśalaḥ sarvarogavimocanakaḥ / evameva suvikrāntavikrāmin tṛtīyā vidyā sarvāvidyopaśamāya saṃvartate, sarvaduḥkhaniryātanāya saṃvartate, sarvajarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsānāmupaśamāya saṃvartate / iyamucyate suvikrāntavikrāmin lokottarā prajñā nirvedhagāminīti //
children.translated_text: penetrates. How does one penetrate? One penetrates the triple world as being without essential elements (adhātuka). For no one here penetrates any element; one penetrates the triple world as without essential elements. When one has thus penetrated the triple world, one is said to be endowed with penetrating wisdom (<s>nairvedhikī prajñā</s>). And how is one endowed with penetrating wisdom? For there is nothing unwholesome to be penetrated; one penetrates all as wholesome, and transcends through penetrating wisdom. One so endowed with penetrating wisdom — whatever one sees, hears, smells, tastes, touches, or cognizes — all that one penetrates. How does one penetrate? As impermanent, as suffering, as a boil, as a disease, as a thorn, as empty, as misfortune, as affliction, as other, as subject to dissolution, as having the nature of dissolution, as unstable, as fragile, as without self, as unborn, as unceasing, as without characteristics. This is called, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, "cooled and free from thorns." Just as, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is a medicinal herb called <s>Viśalyā</s> — wherever it is applied, it removes all thorns and penetrates them — so too a monk endowed with such qualities is free from thorns, cooled, endowed with penetrating wisdom, dwelling perpetually beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>, dispassionate through penetrating wisdom toward the entire triple world, having transcended all the snares of <s>Māra</s>. Just as, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a diamond — wherever it is placed for the purpose of piercing, it pierces that very thing — so too a monk whose mind is grasped by the penetrating wisdom of the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s>, wherever he places it and upon whatever he directs it, he penetrates all of them. One endowed with penetrating wisdom, with the supramundane [wisdom] rightly leading to the cessation of suffering, is called "one possessed of the three knowledges" (<s>traividyā</s>). "Knowledge" (<s>vidyā</s>), O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is a designation for the pacification of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>); the full comprehension of ignorance is a designation for the pacification of the aggregate of suffering. Just as, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a physician who is learned, skilled, intelligent, endowed with investigation appropriate to the treatises, expert in all medicines, expert in the origin of all diseases, capable of releasing from all suffering — whichever patient he treats, that very one he liberates. Why is that? Because he is expert in all medicines, expert in the origin of all diseases, capable of releasing from all ailments. In the same way, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the third knowledge conduces to the pacification of all ignorance, conduces to the release from all suffering, conduces to the pacification of all old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and affliction. This is called, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the supramundane wisdom leading to penetration.

Now, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, as for penetrating <s>Prajñā</s> (<s>nirvedhikā prajñā</s>) — does that <s>Prajñā</s> penetrate? There is nothing here to be penetrated. If there were something to be penetrated, it could be designated: 'This is that <s>Prajñā</s> which penetrates.' It is not penetrated by anything, nor is it not penetrated; no further [object] is apprehended that would be penetrated. 'It penetrates' — yet nothing here penetrates or does not penetrate, nothing here is penetrated or is not penetrated — therefore it is called 'it penetrates.' No one here reaches the end or the middle — therefore it is called 'it penetrates.' 'It penetrates' — penetrating <s>Prajñā</s> is so called — 'it penetrates' means it does not run anywhere, does not run about, does not run together — therefore it is called 'penetrating.' But, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, as for 'penetrating <s>Prajñā</s>' — what does it penetrate? Whatever view there is — all that it penetrates. By what does it penetrate? It penetrates by <s>Prajñā</s>. How does it penetrate by <s>Prajñā</s>? It penetrates the nature of designation (<s>prajñapti-lakṣaṇa</s>). Whatever has the nature of designation — all that is without characteristics (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>); what is without characteristics has the nature of designation. One who, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, endowed with such <s>Prajñā</s>, penetrates — he [penetrates] the triple world (

children.text: idaṃ ca me suvikrāntavikrāmin saṃghāya bhāṣitam -
children.translated_text: And this, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, I have spoken to the <s>Saṃgha</s>:

children.text: prajñā śreṣṭhā hi lokasya yeyaṃ nirvedhagāminī /
children.translated_text: Wisdom is supreme in the world — this which leads to penetration,

children.text: yayā samyak prajānāti bhavajātiparikṣayam //
children.translated_text: by which one rightly knows the exhaustion of becoming and birth.

children.text: iti /
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: bhavajātiparikṣaya iti suvikrāntavikrāmin kasyaitadadhivacanam? udayāstaṃgamaprativedhasyaitadadhivacanam / katamaśca udayāstaṃgamaprativedhaḥ? yatkiṃcitsamudayadharmi, tatsarvaṃ nirodhadharmi ityevaṃ samudayāstaṃgamaṃ pratividhyati / samudaya iti suvikrāmin utpādasyaitadadhivacanam, astaṃgama iti nirodhasyaitadadhivacanam, na punaryathocyate tathodayāstaṃgamaḥ / yaḥ kaścitsuvikrāntavikrāmin samudayaḥ, na sa udayadharmaḥ / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin samasya kaścidudayaḥ, nāpi tatsamudāgacchati / samatānuyātameva tat / tenocyate samudaya iti / samatānuyātamiti (
Vaidya 6
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 6)

children.text: ) suvikrāntavikrāmin nātra kaścidudayati na samudāgacchati / na tasya yaḥ svabhāvaḥ sa svayaṃ saṃbhavaḥ, sa nirodhaḥ / tatra ca na kasyacinnirodhaḥ, samudayānantaranirodhaḥ / yatrotpādo nāsti, na tatra nirodhaḥ, sa nirodhaḥ / evaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin yaḥ samudayāstaṃgamaprativedhaḥ anutpādāya anirodhāya, so 'staṃgamaprativedhaḥ / tenocyate udayāstaṃgamaprativedha iti ////
children.translated_text: O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, herein nothing arises nor comes into being. That which is its own nature, that is self-arising, that is cessation. And therein there is no cessation of anything — cessation follows immediately upon arising. Where there is no origination, there is no cessation — that is cessation. Thus, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the penetration of arising and cessation is for the sake of non-arising and non-cessation — that is the penetration of cessation. Therefore it is called "the penetration of arising and cessation."

"The exhaustion of becoming and birth" — O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, of what is this a designation? This is a designation for the penetration of arising and cessation. And what is the penetration of arising and cessation? Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of cessation — thus one penetrates arising and cessation. "Arising" (<s>samudaya</s>), O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is a designation for origination (<s>utpāda</s>); "cessation" (<s>astaṃgama</s>) is a designation for cessation (<s>nirodha</s>); but arising and cessation are not as they are spoken of. Whatever arising there is, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, it does not have the nature of arising. For in evenness (<s>samatā</s>), O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is no arising, nor does it come into being. It is simply conforming to evenness. Therefore it is called "arising." "Conforming to evenness" —

children.text: prativedha iti suvikrāntavikrāmin pratītyasamutpādasyaiṣā parijñā / yaṃ pratītya yo dharma utpadyate, tameva pratītya sa dharmo na saṃvidyate / ayamucyate pratītyasamutpādaprativedhaḥ / saiṣā suvikrāntavikrāmin pratītyasamutpādasya parijñā yathābhūtatā anutpādena sūcyate / anutpādo hi pratītyasamutpādaḥ / samo 'nutpādaḥ / tenocyate pratītyasamutpāda iti / yatra nāstyutpādaḥ, tatra kuto nirodhaḥ? anirodho nirodhaḥ pratītyasamutpādasyāvabodhaḥ / asamutpādaḥ pratītyasamutpāda ityucyate / yo 'samutpādaḥ so 'nutpādaḥ / yo 'nutpādaḥ, sa nātīto na anāgato na pratyutpannaḥ / tasya nirodho na saṃvidyate / yasya nirodho na saṃvidyate, taducyate 'nutpādajñānamiti / yena ca anutpādo jñātaḥ, sa na bhūya utpādayati, na ca nirodhaṃ sākṣātkaroti / yo notpādayati, sa na nirodhayati / utpādasya hi sato nirodhaḥ prajñāyate / yenotpādayati, tena niruddhā eva sarvadharmā jñātā dṛṣṭāḥ pratividdhāḥ sākṣātkṛtāḥ / tenocyate nirodhaḥ sākṣātkṛta iti ////
children.translated_text: "Penetration," O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the full comprehension of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). A <s>dharma</s> that arises dependent on something — dependent on that very thing, that <s>dharma</s> is not found. This is called the penetration of dependent origination. This, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the full comprehension of dependent origination: its true nature is indicated by non-arising. For non-arising is dependent origination. Non-arising is evenness. Therefore it is called "dependent origination." Where there is no arising, how can there be cessation? Non-cessation is cessation — the understanding of dependent origination. Non-arising is called "dependent origination." What is non-arising is non-origination. What is non-origination is neither past, nor future, nor present. Its cessation is not found. That whose cessation is not found is called "the knowledge of non-arising." And by whom non-arising is known, that one does not further produce, nor does one realize cessation directly. One who does not produce does not cause to cease. For cessation is recognized only when there is origination. By what one would produce, by that very thing all <s>dharma</s>s are known, seen, penetrated, and directly realized as already ceased. Therefore it is called "cessation directly realized."

children.text: kṣayajñānamiti suvikrāntavikrāmin kṣīṇamajñānam / tenocyate kṣayajñānamiti / kena kṣīṇam? akṣayatayā kṣīṇam / kṣayamasya na samanupaśyati / ajñānavigama eṣa suvikrāntavikrāmin / tenocyate kṣayajñānamiti / ajñānaparijñaiṣā suvikrāntavikrāmin / tenocyate ajñānakṣayaḥ kṣayajñānamiti / na hi ajñānaṃ kṣayo vā akṣayo vā / vigama eṣa suvikrāntavikrāmin jñāsyate / tenocyate kṣayajñānamiti / yathābhūtaparijñaiṣā suvikrāntavikrāmin / tenocyate vigama iti / na kiṃcidanyadupalabhyate idaṃ tajjñānavigama iti / jñānameva nopalabhyate, kutaḥ punarajñānam / yasya kasyavidvimukti, tenocyate kṣayajñānamiti, na punaryathocyate / yasya punaḥ kṣayajñānam, tasya na kaścidvyavahāraḥ / api tu nirdeśa eṣaḥ ajñānakṣaya iti vā kṣaya(jñāna)miti / iyaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin akṣayakṣayajñānaparīkṣā sarvadharmāṇāṃ yenāvabuddhā sa kṣayajñānavigataḥ, akṣayakoṭimanuprāptaḥ / akoṭirnivāṇakoṭiḥ, na punaryathocyate / avacanīyaṃ nirvāṇaṃ sarvavyavahārasamucchinnam / ayaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin nirvāṇadhātunirdeśaḥ, na punaryathā nirdiṣṭaḥ / anirdeśyo hi nirvāṇadhātuḥ sarvanirdeśasamatikrāntaḥ sarvanirdeśasamucchinno nirvāṇadhātuḥ / ayamucyate lokottarāyā nirvedhikāyāḥ prajñāyā nirdeśaḥ, yo 'yaṃ nirvāṇadhāturiti / na ca suvikrāntavikrāmin nirvāṇadhāturdeśastho na pradeśasthaḥ / eṣo 'sya nirdeśa iti //
children.translated_text: "The knowledge of exhaustion" (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>), O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>: ignorance has been exhausted. Therefore it is called "the knowledge of exhaustion." By what is it exhausted? It is exhausted through inexhaustibility. One does not perceive its exhaustion. This, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the departure of ignorance. Therefore it is called "the knowledge of exhaustion." This, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the full comprehension of ignorance. Therefore it is called "the exhaustion of ignorance is the knowledge of exhaustion." For ignorance is neither exhaustible nor inexhaustible. This, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is to be known as departure. Therefore it is called "the knowledge of exhaustion." This, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the full comprehension of things as they truly are. Therefore it is called "departure." Nothing else is apprehended as "this is the departure of that knowledge." Knowledge itself is not apprehended — how much less then ignorance? From whatever one is liberated — therefore it is called "the knowledge of exhaustion," but not as it is literally spoken. For one who has the knowledge of exhaustion, there is no conventional activity whatsoever. Rather, this is merely a designation: "the exhaustion of ignorance" or "the knowledge of exhaustion." This, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the examination of the knowledge of inexhaustible-exhaustion of all <s>dharma</s>s. By which [knowledge] one has awakened, one has departed from the knowledge of exhaustion and has reached the limit of the inexhaustible. The non-limit is the limit of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, but not as it is literally spoken. <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is inexpressible, with all conventional activity cut off. This, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the exposition of the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-element, but not as it has been expounded. For the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-element is beyond all exposition, with all exposition cut off. This is called the exposition of the supramundane penetrating wisdom — which is the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-element. And, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-element is not located in any place nor in any region. This is its exposition.

children.text: Vaidya 7

tatra katamā suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā? na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitāyāḥ kiṃcidāraṃ vā pāraṃ vā / sacetsuvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitāyā āraṃ vā pāraṃ vā upalabhyeta, nirdiśettathāgataḥ prajñāyā āraṃ vā pāraṃ vā / na ca suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitāyā āramupalabhyate, tenāsyāḥ pāraṃ na nirdiśyate / api tu suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramiteti pārametatsarvadharmāṇāṃ jñānakarmaṇām, tenocyate prajñāpāramiteti, na punaryathocyate / na hi vācā na karmaṇā prajñāpāramitā pratyupasthitā / anirdeśyā hi suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā / sarvadharmāṇāmeṣo 'nubodhaḥ / yaścānubodhaḥ, so 'virodhaḥ / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi tatra kiṃcidanubuddham, na pratividdham / anubodhaprativedhasamatā hi bodhiḥ sarvadharmānubodhādbodhirityucyate / kathaṃ ca sarvadharmānubodhaḥ? nātra kācidbodhirnāpyatra kaści(danu)bodhaḥ / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? sacet suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhirupalabhyeta, labdhā syādbodhau bodhiḥ / na ca suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhau bodhiḥ saṃvidyate / evameṣā bodhirabhisaṃboddhavyā / ananubodhādaprativedhādanubudhyetyucyate, na punaryathocyate sarvadharmā hyananubuddhā apratividdhāḥ / na ca punardharmo dharmasvabhāvena saṃvidyate anenānubodhena / iyamucyate bodhiriti / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmiṃstathāgatena bodhirupalabdhā, nāpi tathāgatena bodhirvijñaptā / avijñapanīyā aprajñapanīyā bodhiḥ / na ca tathāgatena bodhirjñātā na janitā / ajātā anabhinirvṛttā hi bodhiḥ / na ca bodhiḥ kasyavidviṣayaḥ, na ca bodhau kaścitsattvo vā sattvaprajñaptirvā / yatra nasti sattvo vā sattvaprajñaptirvā, kathaṃ vaktavyo 'yaṃ bodhisattvaḥ, iyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramiteti? na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhau bodhiḥ, na ca bodhau kaścitsattvaḥ / atikrāntā hyeṣā bodhiḥ, anutpannaiṣā bodhiḥ, anabhisaṃvṛttaiṣā bodhiḥ, alakṣaṇaiṣā bodhiḥ / na cāsyāṃ sattvaḥ saṃvidyate, nopalabhyate / na bodhiḥ sattvatayā prajñaptā / niḥsattvānubodho hi bodhirityucyate / bodhi(ra)sattvateti yena jñātā, sa ucyate bodhisattva iti / tatkamāddhetoḥ? na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaḥ sattvasaṃjñāprabhāvitaḥ / sattvasaṃjñāvibhāvanādbodhisattva ityucyate, na punaryathocyate / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? avacanīyo hi bodhisattvaḥ, sattvasvabhāvavigato hi bodhisattvaḥ, sattvasaṃjñāvigatā hi bodhiḥ / yenaivaṃ bodhirjñātā, sa bodhisattva ityucyate / kimiti bodhirjñātā? atikrāntaiṣā bodhiḥ, akaraṇīyaiṣā bodhiḥ, anutpādānirodho hyeṣā bodhiḥ / na bodhirbodhiṃ vijñāpayati, nāpi bodhirvijñāpanīyā / avijñāpanīyā aprajñapanīyā anabhinirvartanīyā bodhirityucyate / yena ca anubuddhā pratibuddhā avikalpā kalpasamucchedāya, tenocyate bodhisattva iti, na punaryathocyate / tatkasmāt? niḥsattvatvāt / yadi bodhisattvaḥ samupalabhyeta, labdhā syādbodhiḥ - iyaṃ sā bodhiḥ, asyāmayaṃ sattvā iti / asattvaniḥsattvasattvāvagamānubodhādbodhisattva ityucyate / niḥsattvatayā sattvasaṃjñāvibhāvanatayā asattvasaṃjñāvibhāvanatayā bodhisattva ityucyate / tat (
Vaidya 8
children.translated_text: [Vaidya 8]

children.text: ) kasmāt? sattvadhāturityasattvatāyā etadadhivacanam / na hi sattvaḥ sattve saṃvidyate, asaṃvidyamānatvātsattvadhātoḥ / yadi sattve sattvaḥ syāt, nocyeta sattvadhāturiti / adhātunidarśanametat sattvadhāturiti / adhātuko hi sattvadhātuḥ / yadi sattvadhātau sattvadhāturbhavet, sajīvastaccharīraṃ bhavet / atha sattvadhātunirmukto dhāturbhavet, adhātuko hi sattvadhātuḥ / dhātuḥ saṃketena vyavahārapadaṃ gacchati / na hi sattvadhātau dhātuḥ saṃvidyate, nāpyanyatra sattvadhātoḥ sattvadhātuḥ saṃvidyate / adhātukā hi sarvadharmāḥ / idaṃ ca me saṃdhāya bhāṣitam - na sattvadhātorūnatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vā prajñāyate / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? asattvāt sattvadhātoḥ, viviktatvātsattvadhātoḥ / yathā ca sattvadhātornonatvaṃ na pūrṇatvaṃ prajñāyate, evaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmapi nonatvaṃ na pūrṇatvaṃ prajñāyate / sarvadharmāṇāṃ hi na kācitpariniṣpattiḥ, yenaiṣāmūnatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vā bhavet / ya evaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmanubodhaḥ, sa ucyate sarvadharmānubodha iti / iyaṃ ca mayā saṃdhāya vāgbhāṣitā - yathā sattvadhātornonatvaṃ na pūrṇatvaṃ prajñāyate, evaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmapi nonatvaṃ na pūrṇatvaṃ prajñāyata iti / yacca sarvadharmāṇāmanūnatvamapūrṇatvam, tadapariniṣpattiyogena, tadeva buddhadharmāṇāmapi anūnatvamapūrṇatvam / evaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmanubodhādbuddhadharmāṇāmanūnatvamapūrṇatvam / sarvadharmāṇāmanūnatvādapūrṇatvādbuddhadharmā iti / tena tadbuddhadharmāṇāmadhivacanam / na hi buddhadharmāḥ kenacicchakyā ūnā vā pūrṇā vā kartum / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? sarvadharmānubodha eṣaḥ / yaśca sarvadharmānubodhaḥ, tatra na kasyaciddharmasya ūnatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vā / sarvadharmā iti dharmadhātoretadadhivacanam / na ca dharmadhātorūnatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vā / tatkasya hetoḥ? ananto hi dharmadhātuḥ / na hi sattvadhātośca dharmadhātośca nānātvamupalabhyate, nāpi sattvadhātorvā dharmadhātorvā ūnatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vopalabhyate vā saṃvidyate vā / ya evamanubodhaḥ, iyamucyate bodhiriti / tenocyate - na buddhadharmāṇāmūnatvaṃ vā pūrṇatvaṃ vā prajñāyata iti / anūnatvapūrṇatvamiti suvikrāntavikrāmin yathāvadavikalpasya yathābhūtadarśanasyaitadadhivacanam / na tatra śakyaṃ kenacidutkṣeptuṃ vā prakṣeptuṃ vā / ya evamanubodhaḥ, iyamucyate bodhiriti / (bodhiriti) suvikrāntavikrāmin buddhalakṣaṇametat / kathaṃ buddhalakṣaṇam? sarvadharmalakṣaṇānyalakṣaṇam, etadbuddhalakṣaṇam / alakṣaṇā hi bodhirlakṣaṇasvabhāvavinivṛttā / ya evamanubodhaḥ, iyamucyate bodhiriti, na punaryathocyate / eṣāṃ hi suvikrāntavikrāmin dharmāṇāmanubodhatvādbodhisattva ityucyate / yo hi kaścit suvikrāntavikrāmin imān dharmānaprajānannanavabudhyamāno bodhisattva ityātmānaṃ pratijānīte, dūre tasya bodhisattvasya bodhisattvabhūmiḥ, dūre bodhisattvadharmāḥ, visaṃvādayati sadevamānuṣāsuraṃ lokaṃ bodhisattvanāmnā / sacetpunaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin vāṅmātreṇa bodhisattvo bhavet, tena sarvasattvā api bodhisattvā bhaveyuḥ / naitatsuvikrāntavikrāmin vāṅmātraṃ yaduta bodhisattvabhūmiriti / na ca vācā śakyamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum / na hi vākkarmaṇā bodhiḥ prāpyate, nāpi bodhisattvadharmāḥ / sarvasattvāḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhāya caranti, (
children.translated_text: ) is that? '<s>Sattvadhātu</s>' (the realm of beings) is a designation for the absence of beings. For no being is found in a being; because the <s>sattvadhātu</s> is unfound. If a being were to be found in a being, it would not be called '<s>sattvadhātu</s>.' This '<s>sattvadhātu</s>' is an indication of non-<s>dhātu</s> (non-element). For the <s>sattvadhātu</s> is without <s>dhātu</s>. If there were a <s>sattvadhātu</s> in the <s>sattvadhātu</s>, it would be a living body. But the <s>dhātu</s> is separate from the <s>sattvadhātu</s>; for the <s>sattvadhātu</s> is without <s>dhātu</s>. The word '<s>dhātu</s>' functions as a conventional designation. For no <s>dhātu</s> is found in the <s>sattvadhātu</s>, nor is the <s>sattvadhātu</s> found apart from the <s>sattvadhātu</s>. For all <s>dharmas</s> are without <s>dhātu</s>. And with this in mind I have spoken: 'Neither deficiency nor fullness of the <s>sattvadhātu</s> is perceived.' For what reason? Because the <s>sattvadhātu</s> is without beings; because the <s>sattvadhātu</s> is isolated. Just as neither deficiency nor fullness of the <s>sattvadhātu</s> is perceived, so too neither deficiency nor fullness of all <s>dharmas</s> is perceived. For there is no completion whatsoever of all <s>dharmas</s>, by which there could be deficiency or fullness of them. This awakening to all <s>dharmas</s> is called the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>. And with this in mind have I spoken: 'Just as neither deficiency nor fullness of the <s>sattvadhātu</s> is perceived, so too neither deficiency nor fullness of all <s>dharmas</s> is perceived.' And this non-deficiency and non-fullness of all <s>dharmas</s>, through their non-completion, is itself the non-deficiency and non-fullness of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> as well. Thus, through the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>, there is non-deficiency and non-fullness of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. Through the non-deficiency and non-fullness of all <s>dharmas</s>, they are called '<s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>.' For that is the designation of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. No one is able to make the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> deficient or full. For what reason? This is the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>. And in the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>, there is no deficiency or fullness of any <s>dharma</s>. 'All <s>dharmas</s>' is a designation for the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharmas</s>). And there is no deficiency or fullness of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. For what reason? Because the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is infinite. No difference between the <s>sattvadhātu</s> and the <s>dharmadhātu</s> can be apprehended, nor can deficiency or fullness of the <s>sattvadhātu</s> or <s>dharmadhātu</s> be apprehended or found. This awakening is called <s>bodhi</s>. Therefore it is said: 'Neither deficiency nor fullness of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> is perceived.' 'Non-deficiency and non-fullness,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is a designation for undifferentiated, reality-seeing as it truly is. Nothing therein can be cast away or added. This awakening is called <s>bodhi</s>. '<s>Bodhi</s>,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the mark of the <s>Buddha</s>. How is it the mark of the <s>Buddha</s>? The non-mark of the marks of all <s>dharmas</s> — that is the mark of the <s>Buddha</s>. For <s>bodhi</s> is without marks, having turned away from the intrinsic nature of marks. This awakening is called <s>bodhi</s>, but not as it is literally said. Because, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, one who has awakened to these <s>dharmas</s> is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. But if anyone, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, not knowing these <s>dharmas</s>, not understanding them, claims to be a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, far from that one is the stage of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, far are the qualities of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>; he deceives the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s> with the name '<s>Bodhisattva</s>.' If, moreover, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, one could become a <s>Bodhisattva</s> by mere words, then all beings would also be <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. But, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage is not a matter of mere words. Nor can supreme perfect awakening be awakened to through speech. For <s>bodhi</s> is not attained through verbal action, nor are the <s>Bodhisattva</s> qualities. All beings, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, are practicing toward awakening (

children.text: Vaidya 9
children.translated_text: [Vaidya 9]

children.text: ) na ca jānanti na budhyante / te na bodhisattvā ityucyante / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi sattvā asattvamiti prajānanti / sacedevaṃ te jānīyuḥ, ātmacaritairbodhisatvā bhaveyuḥ / viparyastāḥ punaḥ sattvāḥ svacaryāṃ svaviṣayaṃ svagocaraṃ na prajānanti / sacedātmacaryāṃ prajānīyuḥ, na te bhūyaḥ kasmiṃścidvikalpe careyuḥ / tābhirvikalpacaryābhiḥ sarvabālapṛthagjanā abhūtārambaṇe caranti / te bodhimapi ārambaṇīkṛtya manyante / teṣāmārambaṇacaritānāṃ vikalpacaritānāṃ kuto bodhiḥ, kuto bodhisattvadharmāḥ? ya evaṃ dharmaṃ prajānanti, na te bhūyo 'bhūtārambaṇe caranti / na te bhūyaḥ kaṃciddharmaṃ manyante / tenocyate - acaryā bodhisattvacareti / na bodhisattvāḥ kalpe na vikalpe caranti / yatra ca na kalpo na vikalpaḥ, na tatra kāciccaryā / yatra cāvikalpaḥ, na tatra kasyaciccaryā / buddhabodhisattvānāṃ sarvacaryā avikalpacaryeti / sarvā manyanā asārambaṇā / sa evaṃ sarvadharmān prajānan na bhūya ārambaṇe vā vikalpe vā carati vicarati vā / iyaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ caryā acaryāyogena / evaṃ hi suvikrāntavikrāmin dharmānavabudhyante pratibudhyante, tenocyante bodhisattvā iti ////
children.translated_text: They do not know, they do not understand. They are not called <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. For what reason? Because beings do not understand non-being. If they were to know thus, they would become <s>Bodhisattvas</s> through their own conduct. But deluded beings do not understand their own conduct, their own domain, their own range. If they were to understand their own conduct, they would no longer engage in any conceptual elaboration (<s>vikalpa</s>). Through those conceptual conducts, all ordinary childish persons (<s>bālapṛthagjana</s>) engage in unreal objects (<s>abhūtārambaṇa</s>). They even make <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) an object and think about it. For those engaged in objects, engaged in concepts — where is <s>Bodhi</s>? Where are the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>dharmas</s>? Those who understand <s>dharma</s> thus no longer engage in unreal objects. They no longer think of any <s>dharma</s>. Therefore it is said: the conduct of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is non-conduct. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> do not engage in concepts or non-concepts. Where there is neither concept nor non-concept, there is no conduct whatsoever. Where there is non-conceptuality, there is no one's conduct. All the conduct of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is non-conceptual conduct. All thinking is without object. One who thus understands all <s>dharmas</s> no longer engages in objects or concepts, does not move about. This is the conduct of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> through the yoga of non-conduct. Thus indeed, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, they understand <s>dharmas</s> and awaken to them; therefore they are called <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

Now what, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? Indeed, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is no hither shore or farther shore of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. If, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a hither shore or farther shore of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> could be apprehended, the <s>Tathāgata</s> would point out the hither or farther shore of wisdom. But since, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, no hither shore of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> can be apprehended, therefore no farther shore of it is pointed out. However, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' means the 'going beyond' (<s>pāram</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s> and all acts of knowledge — therefore it is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, but not as it is literally said. For <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not realized through speech nor through action. Indeed, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is inexpressible. This is the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>. And that which is awakening is non-obstruction. For what reason? Because nothing whatsoever is awakened to, nothing penetrated. The equality of awakening and penetration is <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). Because of the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>, it is called <s>bodhi</s>. And how is this awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>? There is no <s>bodhi</s> therein, nor is there any awakening therein. For what reason? If, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>bodhi</s> could be apprehended, then <s>bodhi</s> would be found in <s>bodhi</s>. But <s>bodhi</s> is not found in <s>bodhi</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>. Thus should <s>bodhi</s> be fully awakened to. Because of non-awakening and non-penetration, it is said 'one awakens,' but not as it is literally said, for all <s>dharmas</s> are unawakened and unpenetrated. Nor is any <s>dharma</s> found with the intrinsic nature of a <s>dharma</s> through this awakening. This is called <s>bodhi</s>. For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>bodhi</s> has not been apprehended by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor has <s>bodhi</s> been cognized by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. <s>Bodhi</s> is uncognizable and undesignable. Nor has <s>bodhi</s> been known by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor produced. For <s>bodhi</s> is unborn and unaccomplished. Nor is <s>bodhi</s> anyone's object, nor in <s>bodhi</s> is there any being or designation of a being. Where there is no being or designation of a being, how can one say 'this is a <s>Bodhisattva</s>' or 'this is a <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>'? For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, in <s>bodhi</s> there is no <s>bodhi</s>, nor in <s>bodhi</s> any being. For this <s>bodhi</s> is transcendent, this <s>bodhi</s> is unarisen, this <s>bodhi</s> is unaccomplished, this <s>bodhi</s> is without marks. Nor is any being found or apprehended therein. <s>Bodhi</s> is not designated through 'being-ness.' For <s>bodhi</s> is said to be the awakening to the absence of beings. One who has known <s>bodhi</s> as 'non-being' — that one is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is not dominated by the notion of a being. Through the removal of the notion of a being, one is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, but not as it is literally said. For what reason? Because a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is inexpressible; because a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is devoid of the intrinsic nature of a being; because <s>bodhi</s> is free from the notion of a being. One who has thus known <s>bodhi</s> is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. How is <s>bodhi</s> known? This <s>bodhi</s> is transcendent, this <s>bodhi</s> is beyond action, this <s>bodhi</s> is non-arising and non-cessation. <s>Bodhi</s> does not make <s>bodhi</s> known, nor is <s>bodhi</s> to be made known. <s>Bodhi</s> is said to be uncognizable, undesignable, and unproducible. And one who has awakened to it and understood it — undifferentiated, for the cutting off of conceptual proliferation — that one is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, but not as it is literally said. For what reason? Because of the absence of beings. If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> could be apprehended, then <s>bodhi</s> would be found — 'this is that <s>bodhi</s>, these are the beings in it.' Through awakening to beings as non-being, as absence of beings, as the understanding of beings — one is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Through the absence of beings, through the removal of the notion of a being, through the non-occurrence of the notion of a being — one is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Why (

children.text: asattveti bodhisattvasyaitadadhivacanam / bibhāvitā hi tena sattvāḥ sarvasaṃjñāḥ / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? jñātā hi tena bhūtāḥ sarvasattvāḥ, asattvāḥ sarvasattvāḥ viparyāsasattvāḥ sarvasattvāḥ, parikalpitasattvāḥ sarvasattvāḥ, abhūtārambaṇasattvāḥ sarvasattvāḥ, svacaryāvipranaṣṭasattvāḥ sarvasattvāḥ, avidyāsaṃskārasattvāḥ sarvasattvā iti / tatkasya hetoḥ? ye dharmāḥ sarvasattvānāṃ na saṃvidyante, tān dharmānabhisaṃskurvanti / tenocyate sarvasattvā avidyāsaṃskārasattvā iti / katamo dharmo na saṃvidyate? ahamiti vā mameti vā ahamasmīti vā na kaściddharmo vidyate / sacetkaściddharmaḥ syāt - ahamiti vā mameti vā ahamasmīti vā, tena bhūtāḥ sattvā abhaviṣyan / yasmāttarhi suvikrāntavikrāmin na sa kaściddharmaḥ, yaḥ ahamiti vā mameti vā ahamasmīti vā, tenocyate - abhūtāḥ sarvasattvā iti, avidyāsaṃskārasattvāḥ sarvasattvā iti / na hi kaścit suvikrāntavikrāmin sattvo nāma dharmaḥ saṃvidyate yasya syādahamiti vā mameti vā ahamasmīti vā / yasmācca na saṃvidyate, tasmādabhūtāḥ sattvā ityucyante / abhūtā iti asattvānāmetadadhivacanam / yathā vā punarabhūtāyāṃ sattvasaṃjñāyāmabhiniviṣṭāḥ, tasmāducyate abhūtāḥ sattvā iti / abhūtamiti suvikrāntavikrāmin nātra kiṃcidbhūtaṃ na saṃbhūtam / sarvadharmā hi abhūtā asaṃbhūtāḥ / tatra sattvā abhūtā adhyavasitā vinibadhyante, tenocyante abhūtārambaṇāḥ sattvā iti / tāṃ te svacaryāmaprajānantaḥ abhūtasattvā ityucyante / aparibodhanā punaryasyāścaryāvabodhādbodhisattvā ityucyate //
children.translated_text: 'Non-being' (<s>asattva</s>) is a designation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. For the designation 'being' (<s>sattva</s>) has been analyzed by him. For what reason? Because he has understood that all beings are unreal (<s>abhūta</s>), all beings are non-beings, all beings are perverted beings, all beings are fabricated beings, all beings are beings with unreal objects, all beings are beings whose own conduct is lost, all beings are beings of ignorance and formations (<s>avidyāsaṃskāra</s>). For what reason? Whatever <s>dharmas</s> are not found in all beings, those very <s>dharmas</s> they fabricate. Therefore it is said that all beings are beings of ignorance and formations. What <s>dharma</s> is not found? No <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is found as 'I' or 'mine' or 'I am.' If any <s>dharma</s> were 'I' or 'mine' or 'I am,' then beings would be real. Since, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is no such <s>dharma</s> as 'I' or 'mine' or 'I am,' therefore it is said: all beings are unreal, all beings are beings of ignorance and formations. No <s>dharma</s> called 'being,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is found, to which 'I' or 'mine' or 'I am' would belong. Since it is not found, beings are said to be unreal. 'Unreal' (<s>abhūta</s>) is a designation for non-beings. Or again, since they are attached to the unreal designation 'being,' therefore it is said that beings are unreal. 'Unreal,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> — here nothing is real, nothing has arisen. All <s>dharmas</s> are unreal, unarisen. There, beings determined as unreal are bound; therefore they are called beings with unreal objects. Not understanding their own conduct, they are called unreal beings. And that non-understanding, through whose understanding of conduct they are called <s>Bodhisattvas</s> —

children.text: ya evaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin dharmānavabudhyate, sa ucyate bodhisattva iti / bodhisattva ityanubuddhasattvasyaitadadhivacanam, yena sarvadharmā buddhā jñātāḥ / kathaṃ jñātāḥ? abhūtā (
Vaidya 10
children.translated_text: [Vaidya p. 10]

children.text: ) asaṃbhūtā avitathāḥ, naite tathā yathā bālapṛthagjanaiḥ kalpitāḥ / naite tathā yathā bālapṛthagjanairlabdhāḥ / tenocyante bodhisattvā iti / tatkasya hetoḥ? akalpitā avikalpitā hi bodhiḥ, aviṭhapitā hi bodhiḥ, anupalambhā hi bodhiḥ / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmiṃstathāgatena bodhirlabdhā / alambhātsarvadharmāṇāmanupalambhātsarvadharmāṇāṃ bodhirityucyate / evaṃ buddhabodhirityucyate, na punaryathocyate / yena suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhāya cittamutpādayanti - idaṃ cittaṃ bodhāyotpādayiṣyāma iti bodhiṃ manyante, astyasau bodhiryasyāṃ vayaṃ cittamutpādayiṣyāma iti, na te bodhisattvā ityucyante, utpannasattvāsta ucyante / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi utpādābhiniviṣṭāścittābhiniviṣṭā bodhimabhiniviśante / ye bodhāya cittamutpādayanti, te bodhicittābhiniviṣṭā bodhisattvā ityucyante / yasmādabhisaṃskurvanti, tasmātte bodhāya cittamutpādayanti / tenocyante / abhisaṃskārasattvā iti / na te bodhisattvāḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? utpannasattvāsta ucyante / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin śakyaṃ bodhāya cittamutpādayitum / anutpannā hi bodhiḥ, acittā hi bodhiḥ / utpādameva te suvikrāntavikrāmin abhiniviśante / na te 'nutpādaṃ prajānanti / yā punaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin utpādasamatā, sā bhūtatā / yā ca cittasamatā yā ca bhūtasamatā, yā ca bhūtasamatā yā ca samatā sā bodhiḥ / yatra ca yathābhūtatā, na tatra kaścidvikalpaḥ / te punarvikalpya cittaṃ bodhiṃ cābhiniviśya dvayato bodhāya cittamutpādayanti / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin anyaccittamanyā bodhiḥ, na ca citte bodhiḥ, nāpi bodhau cittam / yā ca bodhiryacca cittam, sā yathābhūtatā yathāvattā / nātra bodhirna ca cittam, na ca bodhirupalabdhā, notpādo nānutpādaḥ / tena sa bodhisattva ityucyate, yathābhūtasattva ityucyate, mahāsattva ityucyate / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? yā hyabhūtatā, sā tena jñātā / katamā ca sā abhūtatā? sa sarvaloko hyabhūtaḥ, abhūtaparyāpanno 'bhūto 'saṃbhūto batāyaṃ lokasaṃniveśaḥ / kimityabhūtasya saṃbhavaḥ? nābhūtasya kaścitsaṃbhavaḥ / asaṃbhūtaṃ hyabhūtam / tenocyate asvabhāvā abhūtāḥ sarvadharmā iti / yenaivaṃ jñātaḥ, sa ucyate yathābhūtasattva iti / na bhūte bhūtamabhiniviśate, tenocyate yathābhūtasattva iti, na punaryathocyate / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi yathābhūte kaścitsattvo vā mahāsattvo vā / yo hi mahāyānamavagāhate, sa ucyate mahāsattva iti //
children.translated_text: unarisen, not distorted — not as conceived by ordinary childish persons, not as apprehended by ordinary childish persons. Therefore they are called <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. For what reason? Because <s>Bodhi</s> is non-conceptual, non-established, non-apprehensible. The <s>Tathāgata</s> did not 'obtain' <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>. Because of the non-obtaining of all <s>dharmas</s>, the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>, it is called <s>Bodhi</s>. Thus it is called <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Bodhi</s>, but not in the way it is spoken of. Those, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, who generate the mind for awakening, thinking 'We shall generate this mind for <s>Bodhi</s>,' and who think of <s>Bodhi</s>, 'There exists that <s>Bodhi</s> for which we shall generate the mind' — they are not called <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; they are called beings of arising (<s>utpannasattva</s>). For what reason? Because being attached to arising, attached to mind, they are attached to <s>Bodhi</s>. Those who generate the mind for <s>Bodhi</s>, attached to the <s>Bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening), are called <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Since they fabricate, they generate the mind for <s>Bodhi</s>. Therefore they are called beings of fabrication (<s>abhisaṃskārasattva</s>). They are not <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. For what reason? They are called beings of arising. For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, it is not possible to generate the mind for <s>Bodhi</s>. For <s>Bodhi</s> is unarisen, and <s>Bodhi</s> is without mind. They, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, are attached to arising. They do not understand the unarisen. But that equality of arising, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is reality (<s>bhūtatā</s>). That equality of mind, that equality of reality, that equality of the real — that is <s>Bodhi</s>. Where there is reality-as-it-is (<s>yathābhūtatā</s>), there is no conceptual elaboration. But they, having conceptualized mind and having clung to <s>Bodhi</s>, generate the mind for <s>Bodhi</s> from both. For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, mind is not one thing and <s>Bodhi</s> another; <s>Bodhi</s> is not in the mind, nor is mind in <s>Bodhi</s>. What is <s>Bodhi</s> and what is mind — that is reality-as-it-is, suchness. Here there is no <s>Bodhi</s> and no mind; <s>Bodhi</s> is not apprehended; there is no arising and no non-arising. Therefore he is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a being-as-it-is (<s>yathābhūtasattva</s>), a <s>Mahāsattva</s> (great being). For what reason? Because unreality has been understood by him. And what is that unreality? This entire world is unreal, encompassed by unreality — unreal, unarisen — alas, this world-arrangement! How can the unreal come into being? There is no coming into being of the unreal. For the unreal is unarisen. Therefore it is said: all <s>dharmas</s> are without self-nature (<s>asvabhāva</s>), unreal. One who has thus understood is called a being-as-it-is. Reality does not cling to the real; therefore he is called a being-as-it-is, but not in the way it is spoken of. For what reason? In reality-as-it-is, there is no being or <s>Mahāsattva</s>. One who enters the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) is called a <s>Mahāsattva</s>.

One who thus understands <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. '<s>Bodhisattva</s>' is a designation for an awakened being — one by whom all <s>dharmas</s> are known as awakened. How are they known? As unreal,

children.text: katamacca mahāyānam? sarvaṃ jñānaṃ mahāyānam / katamacca sarvaṃ jñānam? yatkiṃcitsaṃskṛtaṃ jñānam, laukikaṃ jñānam, tena mahāsattva ityucyate / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? mahatī hi tasya sattvasaṃjñā vigatā, tenocyate mahāsattva iti / mahānasya avidyāskandho vigataḥ, tenocyate mahāsattvaḥ / mahānasya saṃskāraskandho vigataḥ, tenocyate mahāsattvaḥ / mahānasya ajñānaskandho vigataḥ, tenocyate mahāsattvaḥ / mahānasya duḥkhaskandho vigataḥ, (
Vaidya 11
children.translated_text: [Vaidya p. 11]

children.text: ) tenocyate mahāsattva iti / yairhi suvikrāntavikrāmin mahāsattvasaṃjñā vigarhitā, na ca cittamupalabhante na ca caitasikān dharmān, cittaprakṛtiṃ ca prajānanti, na ca bodhimupalabhante, na ca bodhipakṣikān dharmān, bodhiprakṛtiṃ ca prajānanti, te nājñātacittena bodhiṃ ca paśyanti, na cānyatra bodheścittaṃ paśyanti, na bodhau cittaṃ paśyanti, na citte bodhiṃ paśyanti / ya evaṃ vibhāvayanti, na te ca bhāvayanti na vibhāvīkurvanti, te bhāvānapi nopalabhante na manyante nābhiniviśante, te hi bodhāya cittamutpādayanti / ye ca suvikrāntavikrāmin evaṃ bodhāya cittamutpādayanti, te bodhisattvā ityucyante, na ca te bodhervivartante / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? bodhāveva te sthitāḥ, ya evaṃ na bodheḥ, na cittasya, na notpādasya, na nirodhasya nānākaraṇaṃ samanupaśyanti / na hyatra kaścitsamanupaśyati, na kaścidabhiniviśate, na kaścidvikalpamāpadyate / ya evaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin adhimuktivimukticittamutpādayanti, te bhūtā bodhisattvā ityucyante / ye punaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin (cittasaṃjñito) bodhisaṃjñinaśca bodhāya cittamutpādayanti, dūre te bodheḥ, na te 'bhyāsannā bodheḥ / ye punaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhernāpi dūre nābhyāsanne samanupaśyanti, te bodherāsannāḥ, taiśca bodhāya cittamutpāditam / etacca me saṃdhāya bhāṣitam - yo hi advayamātmānaṃ prajānāti, sa buddhaṃ dharmaṃ ca prajānāti / tatkasya hetoḥ? ātmabhāvaṃ sa bhāvayati sarvadharmāṇām, yena advayaparijñayā sarvadharmāḥ parijñātāḥ / ātmasvabhāvaniyatā hi sarvadharmāḥ / yo hi advayadharmaṃ prajānīte, sa buddhadharmān prajānīte / advayadharmaparijñayā buddhadharmaparijñā, ātmaparijñayā sarvatraidhātukaparijñā / ātmaparijñeti suvikrāntavikrāmin pārametatsarvadharmāṇām / katamacca pāraṃ sarvadharmāṇām? yo hi naiva āramupalabhate na pāraṃ manyate na pāramabhiniviśate, tasya parijñayā pāragata ityucyate, na punaryathocyate / evameṣāṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvabhūmiranugantavyā / sā bodhisattvaprajñāpāramitā, yatra aṇvapi na kiṃcidgantavyaṃ vā adhigantavyaṃ vā / na hyatra āgamanaṃ vā gamanaṃ vā prajñāyate / iti ////
children.translated_text: ) therefore they are called <s>mahāsattvas</s> (great beings). Those, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, by whom the notion of 'great being' has been rejected, who do not apprehend mind nor mental factors (<s>caitasika dharmas</s>), yet know the true nature of mind, who do not apprehend <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) nor the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣika dharmas</s>), yet know the true nature of <s>bodhi</s> — they do not see <s>bodhi</s> with an unknowing mind, nor do they see mind apart from <s>bodhi</s>; they do not see mind in <s>bodhi</s>, nor <s>bodhi</s> in mind. Those who discern thus — they neither cultivate nor make manifest; they do not apprehend even mental states, do not conceive of them, do not cling to them — they indeed generate the mind [set on] awakening. Those, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, who thus generate the mind [set on] awakening are called <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and they do not turn back from <s>bodhi</s>. Why? They are established in <s>bodhi</s> itself — those who thus do not see any distinction between <s>bodhi</s>, mind, arising, and cessation. For no one here perceives, no one clings, no one falls into conceptual elaboration. Those, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, who thus generate the mind of conviction and liberation — they are called true <s>bodhisattvas</s>. But those, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, who, conceiving of mind and conceiving of <s>bodhi</s>, generate the mind [set on] awakening — they are far from <s>bodhi</s>, not near to <s>bodhi</s>. Those, however, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, who see neither distance from nor nearness to <s>bodhi</s> — they are near to <s>bodhi</s>, and by them the mind [set on] awakening has been generated. It is with this meaning in mind that I have spoken: 'One who knows the self as non-dual knows the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Dharma</s>.' Why? He cultivates the self-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>; by the comprehension of non-duality all <s>dharmas</s> are comprehended. For all <s>dharmas</s> are determined by their own nature. One who knows the non-dual <s>dharma</s> knows the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. By the comprehension of the non-dual <s>dharma</s>, the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> are comprehended; by the comprehension of the self, the entire triple world is comprehended. 'Comprehension of the self,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> — that is the far shore of all <s>dharmas</s>. And what is the far shore of all <s>dharmas</s>? One who does not apprehend even the near shore, does not conceive of the far shore, does not cling to the far shore — by his comprehension he is called 'gone to the far shore,' but not as it is spoken. Thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the stage of the <s>bodhisattva</s> is to be understood. That is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, wherein not even the slightest thing is to be attained or realized. For neither coming nor going is discerned here.

And what is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>? All knowledge is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. And what is all knowledge? Whatever conditioned knowledge, worldly knowledge — through that he is called a <s>Mahāsattva</s>. For what reason? Because the great designation 'being' has departed from him, therefore he is called a <s>Mahāsattva</s>. The great mass of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) has departed from him, therefore he is called a <s>Mahāsattva</s>. The great mass of formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) has departed from him, therefore he is called a <s>Mahāsattva</s>. The great mass of unknowing (<s>ajñāna</s>) has departed from him, therefore he is called a <s>Mahāsattva</s>. The great mass of suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) has departed from him —

children.text: āryaprajñāpāramitā(yāṃ) nidānaparivartaḥ prathamaḥ ////
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter, the Introduction (<s>Nidānaparivarta</s>), of the Noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
