children.text: Vaidya 12
2 ānandaparivarto dvitīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 2. The <s>Ānanda</s> Chapter (<s>Ānandaparivarta</s>), the second.

children.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat - uttrasiṣyanti bhagavan asminnirdeśe adhimānikā nimittacāriṇa iti / atha khalvāyuṣmān śāradvatīputra āyuṣmantamānandametadavocat - agatiratrāyuṣman ānanda adhimānikānām,aviṣayaḥ / na te punaratrottrasiṣyanti / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? uttrastā ete ye pāpamitrahastagatāḥ / agatisteṣāmatra, aviṣayaḥ / ye punarāyuṣmannānanda adhimānaprahāṇāya pratipannā adhimānaprahāṇāyodyuktāḥ, te hyatra uttrasiṣyanti / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? adhimānaprajñayā niradhimānatāṃ gaveṣante mānaprahāṇaṃ ca gaveṣante / ye punarāyuṣmānnānanda mānaṃ nopalabhante na samanupaśyanti na manyante nābhiniviśante, na te kvaciduttrasiṣyanti, nāpi kvaciduttrāsamāpsyante / na ca āyuṣmānnānanda adhimānikānāmarthāya iyaṃ dharmadeśanā pravṛttā / anavakāśo hyatra āyuṣmannānanda adhimānikānām, ye ca adhimānaprahāṇāyodyuktā vyāvacchante / adhimāna ityāyuṣmannānanda adhikārasamāropasyaitadadhivacanam / ye 'dhimāne caranti, adhikārasamārope te caranti / na te samacāriṇaḥ / samacāriṇo 'pyasmin dharme saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> spoke to the Blessed One: 'Blessed One, the conceited ones who pursue signs will be frightened by this teaching.' Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (<s>Śāriputra</s>) spoke to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'This is not the domain of the conceited, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>; it is beyond their range. They will not be frightened here. Why? Those who have fallen into the hands of evil friends are already frightened. This is not their domain; it is beyond their range. But those, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, who have set out to abandon conceit and are striving to abandon conceit — they will be frightened here. Why? By the wisdom of conceit they seek the state of being free from conceit and they seek the abandonment of conceit. But those, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, who do not apprehend conceit, do not perceive it, do not conceive of it, do not cling to it — they will not be frightened anywhere, nor will they ever experience fright. And, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, this <s>Dharma</s> teaching has not been set forth for the sake of the conceited. For there is no room here, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, for the conceited, nor for those who strive to abandon conceit and make distinctions. "Conceit" (<s>adhimāna</s>), venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, is a designation for the superimposition of a task. Those who engage in conceit engage in the superimposition of a task. They are not practitioners of equanimity. Even for practitioners of equanimity, there is doubt regarding this <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: ye punarāyuṣmannānanda nāpi samamupalabhante na viṣamam, nāpi samaṃ manyante na viṣamam, evaṃ na samamabhiniviśante na viṣamam, na te kvaciduttrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante //
children.translated_text: But those, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, who do not even apprehend the equal or the unequal, do not conceive of the equal or the unequal, and thus do not cling to the equal or the unequal — they will not be frightened anywhere, will not be terrified, will not experience terror.

children.text: agatiratrāyuṣmannānanda sarvabālapṛthagjanānām, aviṣayaḥ / nātra āyuṣmannānanda sarvabālapṛthagjanā gatimapi vindanti / śrāvakayānīyānāmapyānanda agatiratra / ye ca pratyekabuddhayānīyā gambhīreṣu dharmeṣu caranti, teṣāmapyatrāgatiḥ / ye 'pyāyuṣmannānanda bodhisattvayānīyā nimittacāriṇaḥ kalyāṇamitrāparigṛhītāḥ pāpamitrahastagatāḥ, teṣāmapyeṣu dharmeṣu nirupalepeṣu agatiraviṣayaḥ / sthāpayitvā āyuṣmannānanda dṛṣṭasatyaṃ śrāvakayānīyaṃ (bodhisattvayānīyaṃ) ca kalyāṇamitropastabdhaṃ gambhīradharmādhimuktam, ya eṣāṃ dharmāṇāmanulomaṃ caranti, ya eṣāṃ dharmāṇā**mavagāhante 'vataranti ca / ye punarāyuṣmannānanda bodhisattvā nimittāpagatā animittacāriṇo 'nānātvacāriṇo gambhīreṣu dharmeṣvatyantameva niryātāḥ, ye naivaṃ cittamupalabhante na bodhim, na kasyaciddharmasya nānātvaṃ kurvanti, na samanupaśyanti, teṣāmeṣu evaṃrūpeṣu dharmeṣu na dhandhāyitatvaṃ na kāṅkṣāyitatvam / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? sarvadharmāṇāṃ hi te 'nulomaṃ sthitāḥ, na vilomam / te yato yato dharmān pṛcchyante, tatastata eva anulomaṃ visarjayiṣyanti, anulomaṃ ca saṃdhayanti //
children.translated_text: This is not the domain of all foolish ordinary people, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>; it is beyond their range. Foolish ordinary people, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, do not even find a footing here. Even for followers of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle, <s>Ānanda</s>, this is not their domain. Even those who follow the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle and practice in profound <s>dharmas</s> — for them too this is not their domain. Those, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, who follow the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle but pursue signs, who are not guided by spiritual friends and have fallen into the hands of evil friends — for them too, in these <s>dharmas</s> that are free from defilement, this is not their domain or range. Except, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, for a follower of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle who has seen the truths, and a follower of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle who is supported by spiritual friends, who has conviction in profound <s>dharmas</s>, who practices in conformity with these <s>dharmas</s>, who plunges into and enters these <s>dharmas</s>. But those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, who have abandoned signs, who practice without signs, who practice non-duality, who have entered completely into profound <s>dharmas</s>, who do not apprehend mind or <s>bodhi</s>, who do not make any distinction regarding any <s>dharma</s> and do not perceive [distinctions] — for them, in <s>dharmas</s> of this nature, there is no hesitation or doubt. Why? For they stand in conformity with all <s>dharmas</s>, not in opposition. From whatever direction they are questioned about <s>dharmas</s>, from that very direction they will respond in conformity, and they understand in conformity.

children.text: Vaidya 13

atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandametadavocat - evametadānanda yathāyaṃ śāradvatīputro nirdiśati / abhūmirānanda asyāṃ dharmadeśanāyāmadhimānikānām, aviṣayo hi avatartumasyāṃ buddhabodhau / anulomeyamānanda buddhabodhiḥ / na hi ānanda hīnādhimuktikānāṃ sattvānāmudāreṣu dharmeṣu buddhadharmeṣu cittaṃ krāmati / hīnādhimuktikā hi ānanda ābhi(dhi?)mānikāḥ pratilomamavasthitā buddhabodheḥ / te 'dhimānasya vaśena gacchanti / śuddheyamānanda parṣat pūrvajinakṛtādhikārā avaropitakuśalamūlā bahubuddhaparyupāsitā gambhīradharmādhimuktikā gambhīradharmacaritā / viśvasto hi ānanda tathāgato 'syāṃ parṣadi prasahya dharmaṃ deśayati, na ca kaṃcidanurakṣyaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati / sāreyamānanda parṣadapagataparpaṭaśarkatakaṭhalyā bahubuddhaśatasahasraparyupāsitā sāre pratiṣṭhitā / śarkarakaṭhalyamityānanda bālapṛthagjanānāmetadadhivacanam, yeṣāmeṣu dharmeṣu nāstyavakāśaḥ / parpaṭamityānanda ādhimānikānāṃ pudgalānāmetadadhivacanam / nirabhimāneyamānanda parṣad mahadbhiḥ kuśalamūlairabhyudgatā //
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One spoke to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Just so, <s>Ānanda</s>, as <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> teaches. This is not the ground, <s>Ānanda</s>, for the conceited in this <s>Dharma</s> teaching; it is beyond the range of those who would enter this <s>Buddha-bodhi</s>. This <s>Buddha-bodhi</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, is in conformity [with reality]. For the minds of beings with inferior convictions do not penetrate these sublime <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>. Those with inferior convictions, <s>Ānanda</s>, are conceited and stand in opposition to <s>Buddha-bodhi</s>. They go under the power of conceit. This assembly, <s>Ānanda</s>, is pure — they have performed meritorious deeds under former <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), have planted roots of merit, have attended upon many <s>Buddhas</s>, have conviction in profound <s>dharmas</s>, and practice profound <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, teaches the <s>Dharma</s> boldly in this assembly with full confidence, and does not guard any part of the teaching. This assembly, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the essence — free of chaff, gravel, and pebbles, having attended upon many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, established in the essence. "Gravel and pebbles," <s>Ānanda</s>, is a designation for foolish ordinary people who have no room in these <s>dharmas</s>. "Chaff," <s>Ānanda</s>, is a designation for conceited individuals. This assembly, <s>Ānanda</s>, is free from conceit, having risen by great roots of merit.'

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma ānanda yadā anavatapto nāgarājaḥ pramudito bhavati prītisaumanasyajātaḥ, tadā svabhavane pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ paricārayati, svabhavane 'bhipramudito mahāvṛṣṭimutsṛjati aṣṭāṅgopetasya pānīyasya / tadā ye 'pi tasya putrā bhavanti, te 'pi pramuditāḥ sveṣu sveṣu bhavaneṣu pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitāḥ samanvaṅgībhūtāḥ krīḍanto mahāvṛṣṭimutsṛjanti, evameva ānanda tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya mahādharmavṛṣṭimutsṛjato ya ime jyeṣṭhaputrā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ, te 'pi iha lokadhātau svakasvakāni ca buddhakṣetrāṇi gatvā imaṃ dharmasamudayamārabhya teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ purastānmahādharmavṛṣṭimutsṛjanti, mahādharmavarṣaṃ cābhivarṣanti / tadyathāpi nāma ānanda sāgaro nāgarājo yadā pramudito bhavati, tadā svabhavane mahāvarṣadhārāḥ pramuñcati / ye ca tatra bhavane naivāsikā nāgā bhavanti, te tā varṣadhārāḥ saṃpratīcchanti, tuṣṭāśca bhavanti, tābhiśca te varṣadhārābhiḥ sukhaṃ ca saṃjānante / ye 'pi tasya putrā bhavanti, te 'pi tā varṣadhārāḥ sahante, tābhiśca varṣadhārābhiḥ prāmodyaṃ pratilabhante / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? asahyā hi ānanda tā varṣadhārā anyairnāgaiḥ / nāpyanye nāgāḥ sukhaṃ saṃjānīraṃstābhirvarṣadhārābhiḥ, na ca tuṣṭā bhaveyuḥ / evamevānanda ye tathāgatasya dharmaratnamadhyāvasanti, ye ca tathāgatasya jyeṣṭhaputrā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ kṛtakuśalamūlā udārāśayā gambhīradharmanayanirjātāḥ, te imāṃ mahādharmanayavṛṣṭiṃ tathāgatasya prasahante, śrutvā udagrāḥ prītāḥ praharṣitāḥ sukhaṃ saṃjānante / idamānanda tathāgato 'rthavaśaṃ saṃpratītya śuddhāyāṃ parṣadi mahāsiṃhanādaṃ nadati, mahādharmavṛṣṭimutsṛjati //
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Ānanda</s>, when the <s>Nāga</s> king <s>Anavatapta</s> becomes delighted and filled with joy and gladness, he revels in his own palace with the five strands of sensual pleasure, and delighting in his own palace, he releases a great rain of water endowed with eight qualities. Then his sons too, delighted, endowed and furnished with the five strands of sensual pleasure in their own respective palaces, sporting about, release a great rain — just so, <s>Ānanda</s>, when the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One releases a great rain of <s>Dharma</s>, these eldest sons, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, also go to this world-system and to their own respective <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) and, beginning with this gathering of the <s>Dharma</s>, release a great rain of <s>Dharma</s> before those <s>Tathāgatas</s> and shower down a great rain of <s>Dharma</s>. Just as, <s>Ānanda</s>, when the <s>Nāga</s> king <s>Sāgara</s> becomes delighted, he releases great torrents of rain in his own palace. And those <s>Nāgas</s> who dwell in that palace receive those torrents of rain and are satisfied, and by those torrents of rain they experience happiness. And his sons too endure those torrents of rain and through those torrents of rain obtain joy. For what reason? Those torrents of rain, <s>Ānanda</s>, cannot be endured by other <s>Nāgas</s>. Nor would other <s>Nāgas</s> experience happiness from those torrents of rain, nor would they be satisfied. Just so, <s>Ānanda</s>, those who abide in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-jewel, and those who are the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s eldest sons, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who have cultivated roots of merit, whose aspirations are noble, who have arisen from the profound <s>Dharma</s>-method — they endure this great rain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-method, and hearing it they are elated, joyful, delighted, and experience happiness. It is perceiving this purpose, <s>Ānanda</s>, that the <s>Tathāgata</s> roars the great lion's roar in the pure assembly and releases the great rain of <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: tadyathā ānanda rājā cakravartī bahuratnakośasaṃnicayaḥ / bahavaścāsya putrā bhaveyurjātimanto mātṛśuddhāḥ / tān sarvānānayitvā ratnagañjaṃ samaṃ saṃvibhajedanuprayacchet, na ca kaṃcitputraṃ vañcayet / te khalu evaṃ saṃvibhaktāstasya rājñaścakravartino 'ntike bhūyasyā mātrayā adhikaṃ prema ca prasādaṃ ca saṃjanayeyuḥ, samānārthatāṃ ca rājñaścakravartinaḥ ātmasu saṃjānīran / (
Vaidya 14
children.translated_text: [Vaidya 14]

children.text: ) evameva ānanda tathāgato 'pi dharmarājā dharmasvāmī svayaṃbhūrimān putrān saṃnipātya imaṃ dharmaratnagañjaṃ saṃvibhajati ebhyaḥ putrebhyaḥ, na kaṃcidvañcayati, te mamāntike bhūyasyā mātrayā prema ca prasādaṃ ca gauravaṃ cotpādayanti, samānārthatāyāṃ ca buddhavaṃśasyānucchedāya tiṣṭhanti //
children.translated_text: ) Just so, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> too, the <s>Dharma</s>-king, the Lord of <s>Dharma</s>, the Self-Arisen One, having assembled his sons, distributes this <s>Dharma</s>-jewel treasury to these sons, and does not cheat anyone. They generate even greater love, devotion, and reverence toward me, and they remain for the continuation of the <s>Buddha</s>'s lineage in sharing the same purpose.

Just as, <s>Ānanda</s>, a <s>Cakravartin</s> king possessing a great treasure-storehouse of gems — and suppose he has many sons, of noble birth and pure on the mother's side. Having summoned all of them, he would equally divide and bestow the jewel-treasury, and he would not cheat any son. Those who are thus given their share would generate even greater love and devotion toward that <s>Cakravartin</s> king, and they would recognize themselves as sharing the same purpose as the <s>Cakravartin</s> king. (

children.text: na śakyamānanda anyaiḥ sattvairidaṃ dharmaratnaṃ hīnādhimuktikairadhimānikairdṛṣṭicaritairnimittacaritairupalambhadṛṣṭicaritairasmimānahatai rāgadveṣamohābhibhūtairutpathaprayātaiḥ / na hi ānanda hīnādhimuktikānāṃ sattvānāṃ cakravartidhanaṃ rocate / ye eva ānanda cakravartiputrā bhavanti, teṣāmeva cakravartidhanaṃ rocate / kimānanda daridrasattvānāṃ cakraratnena vā hastiratnena vā aśvaratnena vā maṇiratnena vā strīratnena vā gṛhapatiratnena vā pariṇāyakaratnena vā udārairvā vastraiḥ, udārairvā suvarṇamuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajataistaiḥ prayojanam, yāni labdhvāpi prītā na śaknuvanti paribhoktum / samarghaṃ vā vikrīṇanti, akauśalyācca ujjhanti / tatkasmāt? na hi te ratnakovidāḥ / nāpyānanda daridrasattvā ratnānyapi prajānanti - asya ratnasyedaṃ nāmeti / evameva ānanda ye tathāgatasya putrā dṛṣṭasatyā bodhisattvāśca mahāsattvāḥ, te khalvasya dharmaratnakośasya pratyeṣakāḥ / tebhyaścedaṃ dharmaratnamanupalambhaśūnyatāpratisaṃyuktaṃ buddhadharmapratisaṃyuktaṃrocate kṣamate ca / te eva anena kāryaṃ kurvanti / kimānanda daridrasattvāḥ śrutavihīnāḥ śrutavipratipannā bālā acakṣuṣmantaḥ anena dharmaratnakośena kariṣyanti? labdhvā cojjhiṣyanti anyebhyo 'pi vā dātavyaṃ maṃsyante / na hi ānanda caṇḍālā vā pukkasā vā veṇukārā vā, ye vā kecidanye daridrajīvinaḥ sattvāḥ udāraṃ ratnaṃ labdhvā svayaṃ paribhuñjate / te samardhaṃ vā vikrīṇanti ujjhanti vā / daridrasattvā ityānanda sarvatīrthyakarāṇāmetadadhivacanam, ye cānyatīrthikāḥ śrāvakāḥ / daridrasattvā ityānanda sarvabālapṛthagjanānāmetadadhivacanaṃ dṛṣṭipaṅkanimagnānāmaupalambhikānāṃ bandhābhiniviṣṭānāṃ nimittacaritānāmutpathaprayātānām, ye khalu ānanda idaṃ dharmaratnaṃ labdhvā na śaknuvanti paribhoktum, ujjhanti vā, mudhā vā anyebhyaḥ prayacchanti / ye punarānanda dharmaratnaṃ prāpnuvanti buddhaputrā buddhagocaracāriṇastathāgatavaṃśānucchedasthitāḥ, te khalvimaṃ (daṃ?) dharmaratnaṃ paribhuñjate / te labdhvā ca na vipraṇāśayanti, ratnasaṃjñinaścātra bhavanti / na hi ānanda śṛgālaḥ siṃhanādaṃ paribhuṅkte / ye punarānanda siṃhapotakā bhavanti mahāsiṃhenotpāditāḥ, te taṃ mahāsiṃhanādaṃ paribhuñjate / evameva ānanda śṛgālopamāḥ sarvabālapṛthagjanā mithyādṛṣṭayaḥ / te na samarthā tathāgatamahāsiṃhanādaṃ paribhoktum, mahāsiṃhasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya dharmam / ye punarānanda samyaksaṃbuddhasya potakāḥ mahābuddhasiṃhena svayaṃ bhuñjānenotpāditāḥ, te imaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhamahāsiṃhanādaṃ paribhuñjate, paribhokṣyante iti //
children.translated_text: It is not possible, <s>Ānanda</s>, for other beings — those of inferior aspiration, the conceited, those who follow views, those who follow signs, those who follow the view of apprehension, those struck by the conceit of 'I am,' those overcome by passion, hatred, and delusion, those who have gone on the wrong path — to receive this <s>Dharma</s>-jewel. For, <s>Ānanda</s>, the wealth of a <s>Cakravartin</s> does not please beings of inferior aspiration. Only those who are the sons of a <s>Cakravartin</s> are pleased by the <s>Cakravartin</s>'s wealth. What use, <s>Ānanda</s>, have impoverished beings for the jewel-wheel, the jewel-elephant, the jewel-horse, the jewel-gem, the jewel-woman, the jewel-householder, the jewel-minister, or for fine garments, or for fine gold, pearls, <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), conch, crystal, coral, gold, and silver? Even if they obtain them, they cannot enjoy them, being not pleased. They sell them for a trifle, or through inexperience discard them. For what reason? They are not connoisseurs of jewels. Nor, <s>Ānanda</s>, do impoverished beings even recognize jewels — 'This jewel has this name.' Just so, <s>Ānanda</s>, those who are the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s sons, who have seen the truth, and <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> — they are the seekers of this <s>Dharma</s>-jewel treasury. It is this <s>Dharma</s>-jewel, connected with non-apprehension and emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), connected with the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, that pleases them and is acceptable to them. They alone put it to use. What, <s>Ānanda</s>, will impoverished beings, devoid of learning, gone astray from learning, foolish, and without eyes, do with this <s>Dharma</s>-jewel treasury? Having obtained it, they will discard it, or they will think it should be given to others. For, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>caṇḍālas</s>, <s>pukkasas</s>, bamboo-workers, and whatever other beings of impoverished livelihood — if they obtain a fine jewel, they do not enjoy it themselves. They sell it for a trifle or discard it. 'Impoverished beings,' <s>Ānanda</s>, is a designation for all followers of other paths and for <s>Śrāvakas</s> of other sects. 'Impoverished beings,' <s>Ānanda</s>, is a designation for all foolish ordinary persons — those sunk in the mire of wrong views, those who follow apprehension, those attached to bonds, those who follow signs, those who have gone on the wrong path. They, <s>Ānanda</s>, having obtained this <s>Dharma</s>-jewel, are unable to enjoy it, or they discard it, or they give it vainly to others. But those, <s>Ānanda</s>, who obtain the <s>Dharma</s>-jewel, being sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, ranging in the <s>Buddha</s>'s domain, established in the continuation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lineage — they enjoy this <s>Dharma</s>-jewel. And having obtained it, they do not lose it, and they perceive it as a jewel. For, <s>Ānanda</s>, a jackal does not enjoy the lion's roar. But those who are the lion's cubs, produced by the great lion, enjoy that great lion's roar. Just so, <s>Ānanda</s>, all foolish ordinary persons of wrong views are like jackals. They are not able to enjoy the great lion's roar of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> of the great lion, the Perfectly Awakened One. But those who are the cubs of the Perfectly Awakened One, produced by the great <s>Buddha</s>-lion who himself partakes — they enjoy this great lion's roar of the Perfectly Awakened One, and they shall enjoy it.

children.text: Vaidya 15

atha khalvāyuṣmān śāradvatīputro bhagavantametadavocat - āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvatpariśuddheyaṃ tathāgatasya parṣat saṃnipatitā / paramāścaryaṃ bhagavan pariśuddheyaṃ tathāgatasya parṣat, svayaṃbhūparṣadanavamṛdyaparṣad vajropamaparṣad acalākampyākṣobhyaparṣadiyaṃ bhagavan / evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputrametadavocat - guṇāṃstvaṃ śāradvatīputra parṣadaḥ parikīrtayasi / āha - na hyasyā bhagavan parṣado mayā śakyā guṇāḥ parikīrtayitum / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? sumerukalpeyaṃ bhagavan parṣadanantaguṇasamanvāgatā / bhagavānāha - evameva śāradvatīputra anantaguṇasamanvāgateyaṃ parṣat / na hyasyāḥ parṣado guṇānāmantaḥ śakyo 'dhigantuṃ samyaksaṃbuddhairapi, prāgeva anyaiḥ satvaiḥ / neyaṃ śāradvatīputra parṣattathāgatena saṃnipatitā, nāpyasyāṃ tathāgatasya kiṃcidautsukyamāsīdvā / svenaiva kuśalamūlena iyaṃ mama nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā parṣat saṃnipatitā / nāsyāṃ parṣadi tathāgatena kaścidvyāpārito nāpyadhīṣṭaḥ / svenaiva kuśalamūlenaite saṃcoditāḥ yadasyāṃ parṣadyāgatāḥ / dharmataiṣā / avaśyaṃ hi evaṃrūpāyāṃ dharmadeśanāyāmevaṃrūpāṇāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ saṃnipāto bhavati / ye 'pyanye śāradvatīputra buddhā bhagavantaḥ imaṃ sarvasaṃśayocchedanaṃ bodhisattvapiṭakaṃ saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, teṣāmapyevaṃrūpaḥ parṣatsaṃnipāto bhaviṣyati, evaṃrūpameva parṣanmaṇḍalamavaśyaṃ bhāvanīyamasyāṃ dharmadeśanāyām / eṣā dharmateti //
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'It is wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>, how pure this assembly of the <s>Tathāgata</s> has gathered! Most wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>, how pure this assembly of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is — a self-arisen assembly, an unwavering assembly, a vajra-like assembly, an immovable, unshakable, imperturbable assembly, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: 'You are proclaiming the virtues of the assembly, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>.' He said: 'Indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>, I am not able to fully proclaim the virtues of this assembly. For what reason? This assembly, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is like Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, endowed with infinite virtues.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Just so, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, this assembly is endowed with infinite virtues. The end of the virtues of this assembly cannot be reached even by Perfectly Awakened Ones, much less by other beings. This assembly, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, was not assembled by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor did the <s>Tathāgata</s> have any eagerness about it. By their own roots of merit, this assembly gathered upon hearing my name. No one in this assembly was urged by the <s>Tathāgata</s> or commanded. By their own roots of merit they were impelled to come to this assembly. This is the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>). Inevitably, in a <s>Dharma</s> teaching of this kind, there is a gathering of such great beings. Whatever other <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, will illuminate this <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s> (Collection of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>) which cuts off all doubts — for them too there will be a gathering of this kind of assembly. Such an assembly-circle must inevitably be present for this <s>Dharma</s> teaching. This is the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>).'

children.text: āryaprajñāpāramitāyāmānandaparivarto nāma dvitīyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter, named the <s>Ānanda</s> Chapter, in the Noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: Vaidya 16
3 tathatāparivartastṛtīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 3. The third chapter: the <s>Tathatā</s> (Suchness) Chapter.

children.text: atha khalu bhagavān suvikrāntavikrāmiṇaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayate sma - prajñāpāramitā prajñāpāramiteti suvikrāntavikrāmin katamā bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitā? yā pāramitā sarvadharmāṇām, na sā śakyā nirdeṣṭum / yathā punaryuṣmākamājānanā bhaviṣyati, tathā nirdekṣyāmi, yathā prajñāpāramitāyāṃ vyavahārapadānyāgamiṣyanti / na rūpaṃ prajñāpāramitā / peyālam / evaṃ na vedanā, na saṃjñā, na saṃskārāḥ, na vijñānaṃ prajñāpāramitā / nāpyanyatra rūpātprajñāpāramitā, yāvat nānyatra vijñānātprajñāpāramitā / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? yaddhi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpasya pāram, na tadrūpam / peyālam / evaṃ yadvedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām, yadvijñānasya pāram, na tadvijñānam / yathā va rūpasya pāram, tathā rūpam / evaṃ yathā vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇām, yathā ca vijñānasya pāram, tathā vijñānam / yathā ca vijñānasya pāram, tathā sarvadharmāṇāṃ pāram / yacca sarvadharmāṇāṃ pāram, na te sarvadharmāḥ / yathā ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ pāram, tathā sarvadharmāḥ / tatra suvikrāntavikrāmin "yadrūpasya pāraṃ na tadrūpam" iti rūpavisaṃyogo hyeṣa nirdiṣṭaḥ / "yathā rūpasya pāraṃ tathā rūpam" iti rūpasvabhāvanirdeśo hyeṣa nirdiṣṭaḥ / rūpayathāvattaiṣā nirdiṣṭā, rūpaprakṛtireṣā nirdiṣṭā, rūpānupalabdhireṣā nirdiṣṭā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / "yadvijñānasya pāraṃ na tadvijñānam" iti vijñānavisaṃyogo hyeṣa nirdiṣṭaḥ / "yathā vijñānasya pāraṃ tathā vijñānam" iti vijñānasvabhāvanirdeśa eṣa nirdiṣṭaḥ, vijñānayathāvattā vijñānaprakṛtirvijñānānupalabdhireṣā nirdiṣṭā / "yacca sarvadharmāṇāṃ pāraṃ na te sarvadharmāḥ" iti sarvadharmāṇāmeṣa visaṃyogo nirdiṣṭaḥ / "yathā ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ pāraṃ tathā sarvadharmāḥ" iti sarvadharmasvabhāvanirdeśa eṣa nirdiṣṭaḥ, sarvadharmayathāvattā sarvadharmaprakṛtiḥ sarvadharmānupalabdhireṣā nirdiṣṭā / yathā ca sarvadharmayathāvattā sarvadharmaprakṛtiḥ sarvadharmānupalabdhiḥ, tathā prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>: '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, it is said, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> — what is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>? That which is the <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection/transcendence) of all <s>dharmas</s> cannot be pointed out. But in the way that understanding will arise for you, so I shall point it out, in the way that conventional terms will apply to <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Form (<s>rūpa</s>) is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; [abbreviation]; likewise neither feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), nor perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), nor formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), nor consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Nor is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> apart from form, and so on up to: nor apart from consciousness. For what reason? Because, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, that which is the transcendence (<s>pāra</s>) of form is not form; [abbreviation]; likewise that which is the transcendence of feeling, perception, formations — that which is the transcendence of consciousness is not consciousness. And as the transcendence of form is, so is form; likewise as the transcendence of feeling, perception, formations — as the transcendence of consciousness is, so is consciousness. As the transcendence of consciousness is, so is the transcendence of all <s>dharmas</s>. And that which is the transcendence of all <s>dharmas</s> — those are not all <s>dharmas</s>. And as the transcendence of all <s>dharmas</s> is, so are all <s>dharmas</s>. Therein, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>: "That which is the transcendence of form is not form" — this indicates the disjunction from form. "As the transcendence of form is, so is form" — this indicates the own-nature of form. This indicates the suchness of form, the nature of form, the non-apprehension of form. Likewise for feeling, perception, formations. "That which is the transcendence of consciousness is not consciousness" — this indicates the disjunction from consciousness. "As the transcendence of consciousness is, so is consciousness" — this indicates the own-nature of consciousness, the suchness of consciousness, the nature of consciousness, the non-apprehension of consciousness. "That which is the transcendence of all <s>dharmas</s> — those are not all <s>dharmas</s>" — this indicates the disjunction from all <s>dharmas</s>. "As the transcendence of all <s>dharmas</s> is, so are all <s>dharmas</s>" — this indicates the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, the suchness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. As the suchness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s> — so is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā rūpaniśritā, na vedanāniśritā, na saṃjñāniśritā, na saṃskāraniśritā, na vijñānaniśritā / nāpi prajñāpāramitā rūpasyādhyātmaṃ vā bahirdhā vā ubhayamantareṇa vā viprakṛṣṭā sthitā / na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārāṇām / na vijñānasyādhyātmaṃ vā bahirdhā vā ubhayamantareṇa vā viprakṛṣṭā sthitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not depend on form, does not depend on feeling, does not depend on perception, does not depend on formations, does not depend on consciousness. Nor does <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> stand removed from form — internally, externally, or in between. Nor from feeling, nor from perception, nor from formations. Nor does it stand removed from consciousness — internally, externally, or in between.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpasaṃyuktā prajñāpāramitā, nāpi rūpavisaṃyuktā / na vedanāsaṃyuktā na saṃskārasaṃyuktā, na vijñānasaṃyuktā prajñāpāramitā / nāpi vijñānavisaṃyuktā prajñāpāramitā / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā kenaciddharmeṇa saṃyuktā vā visaṃyuktā vā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not conjoined with form, nor is it disjoined from form. It is not conjoined with feeling, nor with formations, nor is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> conjoined with consciousness, nor is it disjoined from consciousness. For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is neither conjoined with nor disjoined from any <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: yā punā rūpasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yathāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ yā vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānatathatā avitathathā ananyatathatā yathāvattathātā, sā prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: That which is the suchness (<s>tathatā</s>) of form, the non-distorted suchness, the non-other suchness, the suchness-as-it-is — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise, that which is the suchness of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — the non-distorted suchness, the non-other suchness, the suchness-as-it-is — that is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: Vaidya 17

rūpamiti suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpāpagatametat / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi rūpe rūpaṃ saṃvidyate / yā ca asaṃvidyamānatā, seyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānamiti suvikrāntavikrāmin vijñānāpagatametat / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi vijñāne vijñānaṃ saṃvidyate / yā ca asaṃvidyamānatā, seyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: 'Form,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> — this is gone beyond form. For what reason? Because form is not found in form. That which is the state of not-being-found — that is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise for feeling, perception, formations. 'Consciousness,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> — this is gone beyond consciousness. For what reason? Because consciousness is not found in consciousness. That which is the state of not-being-found — that is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: rūpasvabhāvāpagataṃ hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānasvabhāvāpagataṃ hi vijñānam / yā ca apagatasvabhāvatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / rūpāsvabhāvaṃ hi rūpam / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / vijñānāsvabhāvaṃ hi vijñānam / yā ca asvabhāvatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: Form is gone beyond the own-nature of form, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>. Likewise feeling, perception, formations. Consciousness is gone beyond the own-nature of consciousness. That which is the state of being gone beyond own-nature — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For form is without own-nature. Likewise feeling, perception, formations. Consciousness is without own-nature. That which is the state of being without own-nature — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpasya rūpaṃ gocaraḥ / na vedanā na saṃjñā na saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānasya vijñānaṃ gocaraḥ / agocara iti suvikrāntavikrāmin na rūpaṃ rūpaṃ saṃjānīte vā paśyati vā / yā ca rūpasya ajānanā apaśyanā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ na vijñānaṃ (vijñānaṃ) saṃjānīte vā paśyati vā / yā ca vijñānasya ajānanā apaśyanā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is not the domain of form. Nor feeling, nor perception, nor formations. Consciousness is not the domain of consciousness. 'Without domain' — <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form does not cognize or see form. That which is the non-cognizing, the non-seeing of form — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, neither feeling, nor perception, nor formations — consciousness does not cognize or see consciousness. That which is the non-cognizing, the non-seeing of consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ rūpasvabhāvaṃ jahāti / na vedanā, na saṃjñā, na saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ vijñānasvabhāvaṃ jahāti / yā ca asvabhāvaparijñā, iyamucyate prajñāpāramitā / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ rūpaṃ saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānā(nā)masaṃyojanā, avisaṃyojanā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form does not abandon the own-nature of form. Nor feeling, nor perception, nor formations. Consciousness does not abandon the own-nature of consciousness. That which is the full understanding of non-own-nature — this is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form does not bind or unbind form. That which is the non-binding, non-unbinding of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ hīyate vā vardhate vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ hīyate vā vardhate vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmahāniravṛddhiḥ, iyaṃ sā prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form neither decreases nor increases. Likewise feeling, perception, formations. Consciousness neither decreases nor increases. That which is the non-decrease and non-increase of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — that is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ saṃkliśyate vā vyavadāyate vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ saṃkliśyate vā vyavadāyate vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmasaṃkleśatā avyavadānatā, iyamucyate prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither defiled nor purified. Likewise feeling, perception, formations. Consciousness is neither defiled nor purified. That which is the non-defilement and non-purification of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ viśuddhadharmi nāviśuddhadharmi / evaṃ na vedanā na saṃjñā na saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ viśuddhadharmi nāviśuddhadharmi / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na viśuddhadharmatā nāviśuddhadharmatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither of the nature of purity nor of the nature of impurity. Likewise neither feeling, nor perception, nor formations. Consciousness is neither of the nature of purity nor of the nature of impurity. That which is the non-nature-of-purity and non-nature-of-impurity of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ saṃkrāmati vā avakrāmati vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ saṃkrāmati vā avakrāmati vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃskāravijñānānāmasaṃkrāntiranavakrāntiḥ, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form neither transmigrates nor descends. Likewise feeling, perception, formations. Consciousness neither transmigrates nor descends. That which is the non-transmigration and non-descent of form, feeling, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: Vaidya 18

na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ saṃyujyate vā visaṃyujyate vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ saṃyujyate vā visaṃyujyate vā / yaśca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmasaṃyogo 'visaṃyogaḥ, iyaṃ sā prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither conjoined nor disjoined. Likewise feeling, perception, formations. Consciousness is neither conjoined nor disjoined. That which is the non-conjunction and non-disjunction of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — that is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ cyavate vā upapadyate vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ cyavate vā upapadyate vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmacyutiranupapattiḥ, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form neither passes away nor is reborn. Likewise feeling, perception, formations. Consciousness neither passes away nor is reborn. That which is the non-passing-away and non-rebirth of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ jāyate vā mriyate vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñāna jāyate vā mriyate vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravedanāvijñānānāmajātiramaraṇam, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither born nor does it die. Likewise feeling, perception, formations. Consciousness is neither born nor does it die. That which is the non-birth and non-death of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ saṃsarati vā saṃsaraṇadharmi vā / evaṃ na vedanā na saṃjñā na saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ saṃsarati vā saṃsaraṇadharmi vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmasaṃsaraṇatā asaṃsaraṇadharmatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form neither transmigrates nor is of the nature of transmigration. Likewise neither feeling, nor perception, nor formations. Consciousness neither transmigrates nor is of the nature of transmigration. That which is the non-transmigration and non-nature-of-transmigration of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ kṣīyate vā kṣayadharmi vā / evaṃ na vedanā na saṃjñā na saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ kṣīyate vā kṣayadharmi vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmakṣayatā akṣayadharmatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form neither perishes nor is it of a nature to perish. Likewise feeling, perception, formations — consciousness neither perishes nor is it of a nature to perish. That which is the non-perishing and imperishable nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ samudayadharmi na nirodhadharmi / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ samudayadharmi na nirodhadharmi / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃskāravijñānānāmasamudayadharmatā anirodhadharmatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither of the nature of arising nor of the nature of cessation. Likewise feeling, perception, formations — consciousness is neither of the nature of arising nor of the nature of cessation. That which is the non-arising and non-ceasing nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpamutpādadharmi vā vyayadharmi vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānamutpādadharmi vā vyayadharmi vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmanutpādadharmatā avyayadharmatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither of the nature of origination nor of the nature of decay. Likewise feeling, perception, formations — consciousness is neither of the nature of origination nor of the nature of decay. That which is the non-origination and non-decay nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ vipariṇāmadharmi na avipariṇāmadharmi / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ vipariṇāmadharmi na avipariṇāmadharmi / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na vipariṇāmadharmatā na avipariṇāmadharmatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither of the nature of transformation nor of the nature of non-transformation. Likewise feeling, perception, formations — consciousness is neither of the nature of transformation nor of the nature of non-transformation. That which is neither the transforming nor the non-transforming nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ nityaṃ vā anityaṃ vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ nityaṃ vā anityaṃ vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na nityatā nāpyanityatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither permanent nor impermanent. Likewise feeling, perception, formations — consciousness is neither permanent nor impermanent. That which is neither the permanence nor the impermanence of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpi sukhatā nāpyasukhatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither pleasant nor painful. Likewise feeling, perception, formations — consciousness is neither pleasant nor painful. That which is neither the pleasantness nor the unpleasantness of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpamātmā vā anātmā vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānamātmā vā anātmā vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpyātmatā nāpyanātmatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither self nor non-self. Likewise feeling, perception, formations — consciousness is neither self nor non-self. That which is neither the selfhood nor the non-selfhood of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: Vaidya 19

na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ rāgadharmi vā virāgadharmi vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ rāgadharmi vā virāgadharmi vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na rāgadharmatā nāpi virāgadharmatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither of the nature of passion nor of the nature of dispassion. Likewise feeling, perception, formations — consciousness is neither of the nature of passion nor of the nature of dispassion. That which is neither the passionate nature nor the dispassionate nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ dveṣadharmi vā adveṣadharmi vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ dveṣadharmi vā adveṣadharmi vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na dveṣadharmatā nāpi vigatadveṣadharmatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither of the nature of hatred nor of the nature of non-hatred. Likewise feeling, perception, formations — consciousness is neither of the nature of hatred nor of the nature of non-hatred. That which is neither the hateful nature nor the non-hateful nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ mohadharmi vā vigatamohadharmi vā / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ mohadharmi vā vigatamohadharmi vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na mohadharmatā nāpi vigatamohadharmatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither of the nature of delusion nor of the nature of freedom from delusion. Likewise feeling, perception, formations — consciousness is neither of the nature of delusion nor of the nature of freedom from delusion. That which is neither the deluded nature nor the non-deluded nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpasya kaścitkartā vā kārayitā vā / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāṇām / na vijñānasya kaścitkartā vā kārayitā vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmakartṛtā akārayitṛtā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is no doer or causer of form. Likewise of feeling, perception, and formations — there is no doer or causer of consciousness. That which is the non-doership and non-causership of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpasya kaścidutthāpako vā samutthāpako vā / evaṃ na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārāṇām / na vijñānasya kaścidutthāpako vā samutthāpako vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ notthāpanā va samutthāpanā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is no one who raises up or produces form. Likewise not of feeling, not of perception, not of formations — there is no one who raises up or produces consciousness. That which is the non-raising and non-producing of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpasya kaścijjñātā vā jñāpako vā / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāṇām / na vijñānasya kaścijjñātā vā jñāpako vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmajñātṛtā ajñāpakatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is no knower or informer of form. Likewise not of feeling, perception, and formations — there is no knower or informer of consciousness. That which is the non-knowing and non-informing of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpasya kaścidvedako vā vedayitā vā / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāṇām / na vijñānasya kaścidvedako vā vedayitā vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmavettṛtā avedanatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is no experiencer or one who causes experience of form. Likewise not of feeling, perception, and formations — there is no experiencer or one who causes experience of consciousness. That which is the non-experiencing and non-causing-of-experience of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpasya kaścijjānako vā paśyako vā / evaṃ na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārāṇām / na vijñānasya kaścijjānako vā paśyako vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmajānanāṃ apaśyanā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is no one who cognizes or sees form. Likewise not of feeling, not of perception, not of formations — there is no one who cognizes or sees consciousness. That which is the non-cognizing and non-seeing of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpasyocchedatā vā śāśvatatā vā / evaṃ na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārāṇām / na vijñānasyocchedatā vā śāśvatatā vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmanucchedatā aśāśvatatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither subject to annihilation nor to eternalism. Likewise not feeling, not perception, not formations — consciousness is neither subject to annihilation nor to eternalism. That which is the non-annihilation and non-eternalism of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpasya anto vā ananto vā / evaṃ na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārāṇām / na vijñānasya anto(vā) ananto vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmantatā nāpyanantatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither finite nor infinite. Likewise not feeling, not perception, not formations — consciousness is neither finite nor infinite. That which is neither the finiteness nor the infiniteness of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ dṛṣṭigataṃ na dṛṣṭigataprahāṇam / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ dṛṣṭigataṃ na dṛṣṭigataprahāṇam / yacca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na dṛṣṭigataṃ na dṛṣṭigataprahāṇam, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither a [wrong] view nor the abandonment of views. Likewise not feeling, perception, formations — consciousness is neither a view nor the abandonment of views. That which is neither the being-a-view nor the abandonment-of-views of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: Vaidya 20

na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ tṛṣṇā na tṛṣṇāprahāṇam / evaṃ na vedanā na saṃjñā na saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ tṛṣṇā na tṛṣṇāprahāṇam / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na tṛṣṇā na tṛṣṇāprahāṇatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) nor the abandonment of craving. Likewise not feeling, not perception, not formations — consciousness is neither craving nor the abandonment of craving. That which is neither the craving nor the abandonment of craving with regard to form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ kuśalaṃ vā akuśalaṃ vā / evaṃ na vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ kuśalaṃ vā akuśalaṃ vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na kuśalatā nākuśalatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither wholesome nor unwholesome. Likewise not feeling, perception, formations — consciousness is neither wholesome nor unwholesome. That which is neither the wholesomeness nor the unwholesomeness of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpasya gamanaṃ vā āgamanaṃ vā prajñāyate / evaṃ na vedanāyā na saṃjñāyā na saṃskārāṇām / na vijñānasya gamanaṃ vā āgamanaṃ vā prajñāyate / yatra ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na gatirnāgatiḥ prajñāyate, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, no going or coming of form is discerned. Likewise not of feeling, not of perception, not of formations — no going or coming of consciousness is discerned. Wherein no going or coming of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness is discerned — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ sthitirvā asthitirvā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravedanānāṃ na sthitirnāpyasthitiḥ, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is neither abiding nor non-abiding of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. That which is neither the abiding nor the non-abiding of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmāraṃ vā pāraṃ vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpyāratā na pāratā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is neither a near shore nor a far shore of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. That which is neither the near-shore-ness nor the far-shore-ness of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni śīlaṃ vā dauḥśīlyaṃ vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmaśīlatā adauḥśīlyatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) nor immorality (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>). That which is the non-moral-conduct and non-immorality of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni anunayo vā pratigho vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmananunayatā apratighatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither attachment (<s>anunaya</s>) nor aversion (<s>pratigha</s>). That which is the non-attachment and non-aversion of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni dadati vā pratigṛhṇāti vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃskāravijñānānāmadānatā apratigrahatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness neither give nor receive. That which is the non-giving and non-receiving of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni kṣāntirvā akṣāntirvā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpi kṣāntirnāpyakṣāntiḥ, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) nor impatience. That which is neither the patience nor the impatience of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni vīryaṃ vā kausīdyaṃ vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmavīryatā akausīdyatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither vigor nor indolence. That which is the non-vigor and non-indolence of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ samādhirna vikṣiptacittatā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na samādhirna vikṣiptacittatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) nor distracted mind. That which is neither the concentration nor the distracted-mindedness of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni prajñā vā dauṣprajñyaṃ vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpi prajñatā nāpi dauṣprajñatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither wisdom nor lack of wisdom. That which is neither the wisdom-nature nor the lack-of-wisdom-nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāni viparyāsā vā aviparyāsā vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpi viparyāsatā nāpyaviparyāsatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither perversions nor non-perversions. That which is neither the perversion-nature nor the non-perversion-nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: Vaidya 21
na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni smṛtyupasthānāni vā asmṛtyupasthānāni vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpi smṛtirnāpyasmṛtiḥ, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) nor non-foundations of mindfulness. That which is neither mindfulness nor non-mindfulness of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni samyakprahāṇāni vā asamyakprahāṇāni vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpi samyakprahāṇatā nāpyasamyakprahāṇatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>) nor wrong exertions. That which is neither the right-exertion-nature nor the wrong-exertion-nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni ṛddhipādā vā apramāṇāni vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpi ṛddhipādatā nāpyapramāṇatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) nor immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>). That which is neither the supernatural-power-nature nor the immeasurable-nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni indriyāṇi vā balabodhyaṅgamārgaṃ vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nendriyatā na balabodhyaṅgamārgatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither faculties (<s>indriya</s>) nor powers, factors of awakening, or the path (<s>bala-bodhyāṅga-mārga</s>). That which is neither the faculty-nature nor the power-awakening-factor-path-nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni vidyā vā vimuktirvā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na vidyatā na vimuktitā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) nor liberation (<s>vimukti</s>). That which is neither the knowledge-nature nor the liberation-nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattyabhijñā vā nāpyanabhijñā vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattitā nāpyabhijñatā nāpyanabhijñatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither meditations, liberations, concentrations, attainments, and superknowledges (<s>dhyāna-vimokṣa-samādhi-samāpatti-abhijñā</s>), nor non-superknowledges. That which is neither the meditation-liberation-concentration-attainment-nature, nor superknowledge-nature, nor non-superknowledge-nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni śūnyatā vā animittaṃ vā apraṇihitaṃ vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na śūnyatā nānimittatā nāpraṇihitatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), nor signlessness (<s>animitta</s>), nor wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>). That which is neither the emptiness-nature, nor signlessness-nature, nor wishlessness-nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni saṃskṛtāni vā asaṃskṛtāni vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpi saṃskṛtatā nāpyasaṃskṛtatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) nor unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). That which is neither the conditioned-nature nor the unconditioned-nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni saṅgo vā asaṅgo vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpi saṅgatā nāpyasaṅgatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither attachment (<s>saṅga</s>) nor non-attachment (<s>asaṅga</s>). That which is neither the attachment-nature nor the non-attachment-nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni jñānaṃ vā ajñānaṃ vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpi jñānatā nāpyajñānatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) nor ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>). That which is neither the knowledge-nature nor the ignorance-nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni manyanā vā spandanā vā prapañcanā vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmanyanatā aspandanatā aprapañcatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither conceiving (<s>mayanā</s>), nor stirring (<s>spandana</s>), nor proliferation (<s>prapañcana</s>). That which is the non-conceiving, non-stirring, and non-proliferating nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: Vaidya 22
na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni saṃjñā nāsaṃjñā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpi saṃjñatā nāpyasaṃjñatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) nor non-perception. That which is neither the perception-nature nor the non-perception-nature of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni upaśāntāni vā anupaśāntāni vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpyupaśāntirnāpyanupaśāntiḥ, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are neither pacified (<s>upaśānta</s>) nor unpacified. That which is neither the pacification nor the non-pacification of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nirvṛttirna anirvṛttiḥ / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nāpi nirvṛttirnāpyanirvṛttiḥ, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness have neither accomplishment (<s>nirvṛtti</s>) nor non-accomplishment. That which is neither the accomplishment nor the non-accomplishment of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yaḥ pañcānāṃ skandhānāmabhinirvṛttiparyāpannanirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punaḥ pañcaskandhānāmabhinirvṛttiparyāpannanirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the exposition pertaining to the production of the five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>s) — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), the <s>avitathatā</s> (non-falseness), the <s>ananyatathatā</s> (non-otherness of suchness), the <s>yāvattathatā</s> (suchness in all respects) of the exposition pertaining to the production of the five aggregates — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yo dhātvāyatanapratītyasamutpādābhinirvṛttiparyāpannanirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punardhātvāyatanapratītyasamutpādābhinirvṛttiparyāpannanirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the exposition pertaining to the production of elements (<s>dhātu</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), and dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But the <s>tathatā</s>, the <s>avitathatā</s>, the <s>ananyatathatā</s>, the <s>yāvattathatā</s> of that exposition — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yo viparyāsanīvaraṇābhinirvṛttiparyāpannanirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punarviparyāsanīvaraṇābhinirvṛttiparyāpannanirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the exposition pertaining to the production of perversions (<s>viparyāsa</s>) and hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>) — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But the <s>tathatā</s>, the <s>avitathatā</s>, the <s>ananyatathatā</s>, the <s>yāvattathatā</s> of that exposition — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśattṛṣṇācaritābhinirvṛttiparyāpannanirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśattṛṣṇācaritābhinirvṛttiparyāpannanirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the exposition pertaining to the production of the thirty-six modes of craving (<s>tṛṣṇācarita</s>) — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But the <s>tathatā</s>, the <s>avitathatā</s>, the <s>ananyatathatā</s>, the <s>yāvattathatā</s> of that exposition — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yo dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattinirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punardhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattinirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the exposition of meditations (<s>dhyāna</s>), liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), and attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>) — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But the <s>tathatā</s>, the <s>avitathatā</s>, the <s>ananyatathatā</s>, the <s>yāvattathatā</s> of that exposition — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yaḥ pañcānāmabhijñānāṃ nirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punaḥ pañcānāmabhijñānāṃ nirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the exposition of the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But the <s>tathatā</s>, the <s>avitathatā</s>, the <s>ananyatathatā</s>, the <s>yāvattathatā</s> of that exposition — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yaḥ saṃskṛtaparyāpannānāṃ laukikānāṃ sarveṣāṃ kuśalākuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmabhinirvṛttiparyāpannanirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punasteṣāṃ nirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the exposition pertaining to the production of all wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharma</s>s that belong to the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and mundane (<s>laukika</s>) realm — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But the <s>tathatā</s>, the <s>avitathatā</s>, the <s>ananyatathatā</s>, the <s>yāvattathatā</s> of that exposition — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yaḥ smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgābhinirvṛttiparyāpannanirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punaḥ smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgābhinirvṛttiparyāpannanirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the exposition pertaining to the production of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), faculties (<s>indriya</s>), powers (<s>bala</s>), factors of awakening (<s>bodhyāṅga</s>), and the path (<s>mārga</s>) — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But the <s>tathatā</s>, the <s>avitathatā</s>, the <s>ananyatathatā</s>, the <s>yāvattathatā</s> of that exposition — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: Vaidya 23
na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yaścaturāryasatyanirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punaścaturāryasatyanirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the exposition of the four noble truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>) — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But the <s>tathatā</s>, the <s>avitathatā</s>, the <s>ananyatathatā</s>, the <s>yāvattathatā</s> of that exposition — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yaḥ śīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktivimuktijñānadarśanaviśuddhinirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punaḥ śīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktijñānadarśanaviśuddhinirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the exposition of the purity of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), liberation (<s>vimukti</s>), and the knowledge and vision of liberation (<s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s>) — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But the <s>tathatā</s>, the <s>avitathatā</s>, the <s>ananyatathatā</s>, the <s>yāvattathatā</s> of that exposition — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yo 'saṃskṛtaparyāpannānāṃ lokottarāṇāmaniśritānāmanāsravānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punarasaṃskṛtaparyāpannānāṃ lokottarāṇāmaniśritānāmanāsravāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the exposition of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>), independent (<s>aniśrita</s>), uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>) <s>dharma</s>s — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But the <s>tathatā</s>, the <s>avitathatā</s>, the <s>ananyatathatā</s>, the <s>yāvattathatā</s> of that exposition — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yaḥ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitānutpādānabhisaṃskṛtadharmasya nirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punaḥ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitānutpādānabhisaṃskṛtadharmanirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For it is not the teaching of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), signlessness (<s>animitta</s>), wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), non-arising, and unconditioned <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, that is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Rather, the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the teaching of emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, non-arising, and unconditioned <s>dharmas</s> — its non-falsity, its non-otherness, its ultimate suchness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yo vidyāvimuktivirāganirodhanirvāṇanirdeśaḥ, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā punarvidyāvimuktivirāganirodhanirvāṇanirdeśasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For it is not the teaching of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), liberation (<s>vimukti</s>), dispassion (<s>virāga</s>), cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), and <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, that is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Rather, the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the teaching of knowledge, liberation, dispassion, cessation, and <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — its non-falsity, its non-otherness, its ultimate suchness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaparyāpannā prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ na vedanā na saṃjñā na saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaparyāpannā prajñāpāramitā / na pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśaparyāpannā prajñāpāramitā / na kāmadhātu - na rūpadhātu - nārūpadhātuparyāpannā prajñāpāramitā / na saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtadharmaparyāpannā prajñāpāramitā / na laukikalokottarasāsravānāsravadharmaparyāpannā prajñāpāramitā / na kuśalākuśaladharmaparyāpannā prajñāpāramitā / na sattvadhātuparyāpannānāsattvadhātuparyāpannā prajñāpāramitā / nāpyebhirdharmairvinirmuktā prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: Why? For <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is not included in form (<s>rūpa</s>). Likewise not in feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), not in perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), not in formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not included in consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not included in earth, water, fire, wind, or space. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not included in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), or the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not included in conditioned or unconditioned <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not included in worldly, supramundane, defiled, or undefiled <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not included in wholesome or unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not included in the realm of beings, nor is it not included in the realm of beings. Nor is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> free from these <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā kasmiṃściddharme paryāpannā nāpyaparyāpannā / yā ca paryāpannāparyāpannānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: For <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is neither included nor not included in any <s>dharma</s>. The <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of <s>dharmas</s> that are included and not included — its non-falsity, its non-otherness, its ultimate suchness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: tathateti suvikrāntavikrāmin kasyaitadadhivacanam? na hyete suvikrāntavikrāmin tathā dharmā yathā bālapṛthagjanairupalabdhāḥ, na cānyathā / yathā dharmāstathāgataistathāgataśrāvakairbodhisattvaiśca dṛṣṭāḥ, tathaiva te sarvadharmāḥ, tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, tenocyate tathateti / ayaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaḥ //
children.translated_text: '<s>Tathatā</s>' (suchness), <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> — of what is this a designation? These <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, are not as they are apprehended by foolish ordinary people, nor are they otherwise. As <s>dharmas</s> have been seen by <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by the disciples of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and by <s>bodhisattvas</s> — just so are all <s>dharmas</s>: <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), non-falsity, non-otherness, ultimate suchness — therefore it is called '<s>tathatā</s>.' This, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the teaching of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for the <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>.
