children.translated_text: 4. The Simile Chapter (<s>Aupamyaparivarta</s>), the fourth.

children.text: atha khalu bhagavān suvikrāntavikrāmiṇaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin svapnadarśī puruṣaḥ svapnasvabhāvanirdeśaṃ ca nirdiśati, na ca svapnasvabhāvanirdeśaḥ kaścitsaṃvidyate / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? svapna eva na saṃvidyate, kutaḥ punaḥ svapnasvabhāvanirdeśo bhaviṣyati? evameva suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitāyāḥ svabhāvaśca nirdiśyate, na ca prajñāpāramitāyāḥ svabhāvaḥ kaścitsaṃvidyate / tadyathāpiu nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin svapno na kasyaciddharmasya nidarśanena pratyupasthitaḥ / evameva prajñāpāramitā na kasyaciddharmasya nidarśanena pratyupasthitā //
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One spoke to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>: 'Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a person seeing a dream describes the nature of the dream, yet no description of the nature of the dream exists. Why? The dream itself does not exist — how then would a description of the nature of the dream exist? Just so, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the own-nature of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is described, yet no own-nature of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> exists. Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a dream is not directed toward the demonstration of any <s>dharma</s>, just so <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not directed toward the demonstration of any <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin māyādarśī puruṣo māyāsvabhāvanirdeśaṃ ca nirdiśati, na ca māyāyāḥ svabhāvanirdeśaḥ kaścitsaṃvidyate, kutaḥ punarmāyāsvabhāvanirdeśasya svabhāvo bhaviṣyati? evameva prajñāpāramitā ca nirdiśyate, na ca prajñāpāramitāyāḥ svabhāvanirdeśaḥ kaścitsaṃvidyate / tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin māyā na kasyaciddharmasya abhinirvṛttaye pratyupasthitā, evameva prajñāpāramitā na kasyaciddharmasya abhinirvṛttaye pratyupasthitā //
children.translated_text: 'Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a person seeing an illusion (<s>māyā</s>) describes the nature of the illusion, yet no description of the nature of the illusion exists — how then would the own-nature of the description of the illusion's nature exist? Just so, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is described, yet no description of the own-nature of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> exists. Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, an illusion is not directed toward the production of any <s>dharma</s>, just so <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not directed toward the production of any <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin pratibhāsadarśī puruṣaḥ pratibhāsasvabhāvanirdeśaṃ ca nirdiśati, na ca kaścitpratibhāsasvabhāvaḥ saṃvidyate, kutaḥ punaḥ pratibhāsasvabhāvanirdeśo bhaviṣyati? evameva suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā ca nirdiśyate, na ca kaścitprajñāpāramitāsvabhāvaḥ saṃvidyate, kutaḥ punaḥ prajñāpāramitāsvabhāvanirdeśo bhaviṣyati? tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin pratibhāso na kasyaciddharmasya nirdaśanena pratyupasthitaḥ, evameva prajñāpāramitā na kasyaciddharmasya nidarśanena pratyupasthitā //
children.translated_text: 'Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a person seeing a reflection describes the nature of the reflection, yet no own-nature of the reflection exists — how then would a description of the nature of the reflection exist? Just so, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is described, yet no own-nature of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> exists — how then would a description of the own-nature of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> exist? Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a reflection is not directed toward the demonstration of any <s>dharma</s>, just so <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not directed toward the demonstration of any <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin marīcidarśī puruṣo marīcidarśanaṃ ca nirdiśati, na ca marīcidarśana (svabhāvaḥ kaścit) saṃvidyate, kutaḥ punarmarīcidarśanasvabhāvo bhaviṣyati? evameva suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā na nirdiśyate, na ca punaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ svabhāvanirdeśaḥ kaścitsaṃvidyate / tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin marīcirna kasyaciddharmasya nidarśanena pratyupasthitā, evameva prajñāpāramitā na kasyaciddharmasya nidarśanena pratyupasthitā //
children.translated_text: 'Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a person seeing a mirage describes the vision of the mirage, yet no own-nature of the vision of the mirage exists — how then would the own-nature of the vision of the mirage exist? Just so, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is described, yet no description of the own-nature of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> exists. Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a mirage is not directed toward the demonstration of any <s>dharma</s>, just so <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not directed toward the demonstration of any <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin pratiśrutkāgocarasthaḥ puruṣaḥ pratiśrutkāyāśca śabdaṃ śṛṇoti, na ca taṃ samanupaśyati / yadā punaḥ svayamevānubhāṣate, tadā taṃ śabdaṃ śṛṇoti / evameva prajñāpāramitānirdeśapadaṃ cādhigacchati śravaṇāya, na ca kasyaciddharmasya nirdeśaśravaṇāya gacchati anyatra yadābhibhāṣyate tadā ājñāyate, śravaṇapathaṃ cādhigacchati //
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a man standing within the range of an echo hears the sound of the echo but does not see it — yet when he himself speaks, then he hears that sound — even so one reaches the word of the exposition of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for hearing, yet one does not reach the exposition-hearing of any <s>dharma</s>; only when it is spoken is it known, and it reaches the path of hearing.

children.text: Vaidya 26

tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin phenapiṇḍadarśī puruṣaḥ phenapiṇḍasvabhāvaṃ ca nirdiśati, na ca phenapiṇḍasvabhāva upalabhyate adhyātmaṃ vā bahirdhā vā, kutaḥ punastannirdeśasvabhāvopalabdhirbhaviṣyati? evameva suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā ca nirdiśyate, na ca prajñāpāramitāsvabhāva upalabhyate / tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin phenapiṇḍo na kasyaciddharmasya abhinirvṛttisvabhāvamupaiti, evameva prajñāpāramitā na kasyaciddharmasya abhinirvṛttasvabhāvamupaiti //
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a man who sees a mass of foam points out the own-nature of the foam, yet the own-nature of the foam is not apprehended either internally or externally — how then could the apprehension of the own-nature of its exposition exist? Even so, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is expounded, yet the own-nature of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not apprehended. Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a mass of foam does not approach the own-nature of accomplishment of any <s>dharma</s>, even so <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not approach the own-nature of accomplishment of any <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin budbudadarśī puruṣo budbudasvabhāvaṃ ca nirdiśati, na ca budbudasvabhāvaḥ saṃvidyate, kutaḥ punarbudbudasvabhāvanirdeśo bhaviṣyati? evameva suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā ca nirdiśyate, na ca prajñāpāramitāyāḥ svabhāvaḥ saṃvidyate / tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin budbudo na kasyaciddharmasya abhinirvṛttisvabhāvena pratyupasthitaḥ, evameva suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā na kasyaciddharmasya abhinirvṛttisvabhāvena pratyupasthitā //
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a man who sees a bubble points out the own-nature of the bubble, yet the own-nature of the bubble is not found — how then could the exposition of the own-nature of the bubble exist? Even so, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is expounded, yet the own-nature of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not found. Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a bubble is not present with the own-nature of accomplishment of any <s>dharma</s>, even so, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not present with the own-nature of accomplishment of any <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin puruṣaḥ kadalyāḥ sāraṃ paryeṣamāṇo nopalabhate, atha ca tasyāḥ patraiḥ kāryaṃ karoti, evameva suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāraṃ na saṃvidyate, prajñāpāramitāyā nirdeśaḥ kāryaṃ ca karoti //
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a man searching for the core of a plantain tree does not find it, yet he makes use of its leaves — even so, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the core of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not found, yet the exposition of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> accomplishes its purpose.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin puruṣa ākāśanidarśanena vyavahārati, na cākāśasya kiṃcinnidarśanam saṃvidyate / evameva suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramiteti vyavahāraḥ kriyate, na ca kasyacinnidarśanena vyavahriyate / tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin nākāśaṃ na vyavahriyate, na ca kasyaciddharmasya nidarśanena vā pariniṣpattyā vā vyavahriyate / evameva suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā ca vyavahriyate, na ca kasyaciddharmasya nidarśanena vā pariniṣpattyā vā vyavahriyate //
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a man uses the illustration of space, yet no illustration of space is found — even so, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the conventional term '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' is used, yet it is not used by way of illustrating any [<s>dharma</s>]. Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, space is not unused, yet it is not used by way of illustrating or accomplishing any <s>dharma</s> — even so, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is used [conventionally], yet it is not used by way of illustrating or accomplishing any <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin chāyeti cātapaśceti vyavahriyate, na ca tau kasyaciddharmasya pariniṣpattaye pratyupasthitau, avabhāsaśca vijñāyate / etameva suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā vyavahārapadaṃ gacchati, na ca kasyaciddharmasya nidarśanena vyavahārapadamāgacchati, avabhāsaṃ ca karoti sarvadharmāṇām //
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the terms 'shadow' and 'sunlight' are used, yet those two are not present for the accomplishment of any <s>dharma</s>, and yet illumination is known — even so, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> enters the conventional term, yet it does not enter the conventional term by way of illustrating any <s>dharma</s>, and yet it illuminates all <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin maṇiratnamuttaptaṃ mahatāvabhāsena pratyupasthitaṃ bhavati, na ca so 'vabhāso 'dhyātmaṃ vā bahirdhā vā darśanamupaiti / evameva suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitā avabhāsakṛtyena pratyupasthitā, na ca so 'vabhāso 'adhyātmaṃ vā bahirdhā vā darśanamupaiti //
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a heated jewel is present with a great radiance, yet that radiance is not seen to appear internally or externally — even so, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is present with the function of radiance, yet that radiance is not seen to appear internally or externally.

children.text: tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin tailapradyotasya dhmāyato nāsyārciṣo muhūrtamapi saṃtiṣṭhante, avabhāsaṃ ca kurvanti, tenāvabhāsena rūpāṇi darśanamāgacchanti / evameva suvikrāntavikrāmin (

children.text: ) prajñāpāramitā na kasmiṃściddharme 'vatiṣṭhate, dharmāṇāṃ cāvabhāsaṃ karoti, tena cāvabhāsena sarvadharmā yathābhūtadarśanamāgacchantyāryāṇām //

children.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (<s>Śāriputra</s>) said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'It is wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s> — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has been expounded, and the non-accomplishment of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has been expounded.' Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: 'So it is, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, so it is. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished because of the non-accomplishment of form; unaccomplished because of the non-accomplishment of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness; unaccomplished because of the non-accomplishment of ignorance; likewise unaccomplished because of the non-accomplishment of formations; unaccomplished because of the non-accomplishment of consciousness; because of the non-accomplishment of name-and-form, the six sense-bases, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished. Because of the non-accomplishment of the elements, sense-bases, impermanence, suffering, non-self, peace, the perversions, the hindrances, views, mental wanderings, accumulation and diminution — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished. Because of the non-accomplishment of pleasure, suffering, neither-suffering-nor-pleasure — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished. Because of the non-accomplishment of arising, ceasing, persisting, and changing — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished. Because of the non-accomplishment of origination, cessation, self, being, life-force, nourisher, person, individual, human, youth, agent, causer, instigator, one who causes to instigate, experiencer, one who causes to experience, knower, one who causes to know — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished. Because of the non-accomplishment of truth, falsehood, conditioned, unconditioned, going, coming, with-indication, without-indication, internal, external — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished. Because of the non-accomplishment of earth, water, fire, wind, desire-realm, form-realm, formless-realm, space, consciousness, and the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (dharma-element) — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished. Because of the non-accomplishment of <s>karma</s>, ripening, cause, condition, annihilationism, eternalism, past, future, present, prior end, later end, middle end, morality, immorality, patience, impatience, vigor, laziness, <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), distraction, wisdom, foolishness, mind, mental faculty, consciousness, obstruction, passing away, rebirth, defilement, purification, the foundations of mindfulness, right exertions, bases of power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, path, Noble Truths, the immeasurables, <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, concentrations, attainments, superknowledges, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, wholesome, unwholesome, with defilements, without defilements, worldly, supramundane, with fault, faultless, conditioned, unconditioned, determined, undetermined, dark, bright, neither-dark-nor-bright, included, not-included, inferior, excellent, middling, desire, hatred, delusion, seen, heard, thought, cognized, thinking, established, thought-construction, investigation, object, illusion, jealousy, miserliness, conjunction, duality, characteristic, non-arising, non-fabrication, tranquility, insight, ignorance, liberation, destruction, dispassion, cessation, the abandoning of all substrata, conventional truth, ultimate truth, <s>Śrāvaka</s>-stage, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-stage, omniscient knowledge, unknowing, unattached knowledge, self-born knowledge, unequaled knowledge, <s>Bodhisattva</s> vow, <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> accomplishment, immeasurable, included, unequaled omniscient knowledge, the suchness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the without-illustration of all <s>dharmas</s>, the knowledge and vision of all <s>dharmas</s> — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished. Because of the non-accomplishment of the maturing of beings — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished. Because of the non-accomplishment of the marks of perfection, the purification of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, the <s>Buddha</s>'s powers, fearlessnesses, and the eighteen special qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished. Because of the non-accomplishment of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished; and so on up to: because of the non-accomplishment of all <s>dharmas</s>, wholesome and unwholesome — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unaccomplished. All this should be elaborated in full.'

children.text: āha - gambhīreyaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitā / āha - rūpagambhīratayā śāradvatīputra gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānagambhīratayā śāradvatīputra gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / avidyāgambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / saṃskāravijñānanāmarūpaṣaḍāyatanasparśavedanātṛṣṇopādānabhavajātijarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsagambhīratayā (

children.text: ) gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / viparyāsagambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / pañcanīvaraṇagambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / dṛṣṭigambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / ātmagambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / sattvagambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / prapañcagambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / aprapañcagambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / śīladauḥśīlyagambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / kṣāntivyāpādavīryakausīdyadhyānavikṣepaprajñādauṣprajñyendriyabalabodhyaṅgasmṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇarddhipādāviparyāsāryāṣṭāṅgamārgaduḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgavimuktajñānadarśanātītānāgatapratyutpannatryadhvasamatāgambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / caturvaiśāradyarddhipādābhijñāgambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / atītānāgatapratyutpannāsaṅgajñānagambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / buddhadharmagambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / kṣayajñānānutpādajñānanirodhajñānābhisaṃskārajñānavirāgajñānagambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā / nīvaraṇagambhīratayā gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā //
children.translated_text: ) <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of perversions (<s>viparyāsa</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of the five hindrances (<s>pañcanīvaraṇa</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of self (<s>ātma</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of beings (<s>sattva</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of non-proliferation (<s>aprapañca</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of morality and immorality. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of patience and ill-will, vigor and indolence, meditation and distraction, wisdom and lack of wisdom, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, foundations of mindfulness, right exertions, bases of supernatural power, non-perversions, the noble eightfold path, suffering, its origin, its cessation, the path, liberated knowledge and vision, the past, future, and present, and the equality of the three times. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), bases of supernatural power, and superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of unattached knowledge of past, future, and present. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of the knowledge of extinction, the knowledge of non-arising, the knowledge of cessation, the knowledge of conditioning, and the knowledge of dispassion. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound through the profundity of hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>).

He said: 'This <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, O Blessed One, is profound.' He [the Buddha] said: 'By the profundity of form, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound. Likewise by the profundity of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is profound. By [the profundity of] ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>)

children.translated_text: <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is purified through the purification of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity (<s>maitrī</s>, <s>karuṇā</s>, <s>muditā</s>, <s>upekṣā</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is purified through the purification of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) and the right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is purified through the purification of non-perversion. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is purified through the purification of suffering, its origin, cessation, and the path. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is purified through the purification of superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is purified through the purification of the path. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is purified through the purification of the <s>śrāvaka</s> stage. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is purified through the purification of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stage. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is purified through the purification of the <s>Buddha</s> stage. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is purified through the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>.

He said: '<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of form (<s>rūpa</s>). Likewise, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), through the purity of formations, through the purity of consciousness, through the purity of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>), through the purity of the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of contact (<s>sparśa</s>), feeling, craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), clinging (<s>upādāna</s>), becoming (<s>bhava</s>), birth (<s>jāti</s>), old age and death (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental anguish, and distress. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of perversions (<s>viparyāsa</s>), hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>), and wrong views (<s>dṛṣṭigata</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of passion, hatred, and delusion. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of self, being, life-force, nourisher, person, individual, human, man, doer, causer, experiencer, raiser, producer, knower, and seer. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of annihilationism and eternalism. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of the finite and the infinite. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of morality (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is pure through the purity of faculties (<s>indriya</s>), powers (<s>bala</s>), factors of awakening (<s>bodhyāṅga</s>), meditations (<s>dhyāna</s>), liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), concentrations (<s>samādhi</s>), and attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>) (

children.text: ) anantapāramiteyam / dṛṣṭigatānantatayā rāgadveṣamohānantatayā ucchedaśāśvatānantatayā pūrvāntakoṭyanantatayā anantapāramiteyam / aparāntakoṭyanantatayā anantapāramiteyam / dānānantatayā śīlānantatayā kṣāntyanantatayā vīryānantatayā dhyānānantatayā prajñānantatayā anantapāramiteyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / smṛtyupasthānānantatayā samyakprahāṇarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgānantatayā aviparyāsānantatayā anantapāramiteyam / dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattyanantatayā anantapāramiteyam / ārambaṇānantatayā anantapāramiteyam / vidyāvimuktijñānadarśanānantatayā anantapāramiteyam / śrāvakabhūmipratyekabuddhabhūmibuddhabhūmyanantatayā anantapāramiteyam / śrāvakadharmapratyekabuddhadharmabuddhadharmānantatayā anantapāramiteyam / ātmasattvānantatayā anantapāramiteyam / kāmadhātvanantatayā anantapāramiteyam / rūpadhātvanantatayā anantapāramiteyam / ārūpyadhātvanantatayā anantapāramiteyam / abhijñānantatayā anantapāramiteyam / nīvaraṇānantatayā anantapāramiteyam / atītānāgatapratyutpannajñānadarśanānantatayā anantapāramiteyam / asaṅgānantatayā ākāśānantatayā dharmadhātvanantatayā anantapāramiteyam //
children.translated_text: This is a boundless perfection! Through the boundlessness of speculative views, through the boundlessness of passion, hatred, and delusion, through the boundlessness of annihilationism and eternalism, through the boundlessness of the limit of the past — this is a boundless perfection. Through the boundlessness of the limit of the future — this is a boundless perfection. Through the boundlessness of giving (<s>dāna</s>), moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) — this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is a boundless perfection. Through the boundlessness of the foundations of mindfulness, right exertions, bases of supernatural power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, and the path — this is a boundless perfection. Through the boundlessness of meditations, liberations, concentrations, and attainments — this is a boundless perfection. Through the boundlessness of objects — this is a boundless perfection. Through the boundlessness of knowledge, liberation, knowledge and vision — this is a boundless perfection. Through [the boundlessness of] the <s>śrāvaka</s> stage and the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stage

When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'It is wonderful, Blessed One, how <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is purified by its very nature!' He said: '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, O <s>ŚāradvatIputra</s>, is [purified] through the purity of space.' He said: 'Blessed One, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is formless and without indication!' He said: 'Indeed, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not present through the material accomplishment or indication of any <s>dharma</s>.' He said: 'Blessed One, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unobstructed!' He said: 'Indeed, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not perceive any <s>dharma</s> against which it could be obstructed.' He said: 'Blessed One, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is uncreated!' He said: 'Because a creator is not apprehended, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>.' He said: 'Blessed One, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has no meeting point!'

children.text: na hyasyāḥ śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāyā anto vā madhyaṃ vā paryavasānaṃ vā upalabhyate, nāpi kenacidupalabdhāḥ / anantāparyantapāramiteyaṃ śāradvatīputra yaduta prajñāpāramitā / tadyathāpi nāma śāradvatīputra ākāśasyānto nopalabhyate, evameva prajñāpāramitāyā anto nopalabhyate / pṛthivīdhātvanantatayā śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitānantatā draṣṭavyā / abdhātvanantatayā tejodhātvanantatayā vāyudhātvanantatayā vijñānadhātvanantatayā prajñāpāramitānantatā anugantavyā / anantamadhyaparyantatā hi śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā anuboddhavyā / na hi śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā deśasthā na pradeśasthā / rūpāparyantatayā śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / peyālam / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāparyantatayā śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / avidyāparyantatayā saṃskārāparyantatayā vijñānāparyantatayā nāmarūpaṣaḍāyatanāparyantatayā yāvat jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāparyantatayā śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / viparyāsāparyantatayā śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / nīvaraṇāparyantatayā dṛṣṭigatāparyantatayā śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / ātmānantatayā sattvānantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / dānānantatayā śīlānantatayā kṣāntyanantatayā vīryānantatayā dhyānānantatayā prajñānantatayā śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitānantatā anugantavyā / smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇarddhipādāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitānantatā anugantavyā / indriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattyaparyantatayā śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgāparyantatayā śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / abhijñāparyantatayā (
Vaidya 34
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 34)

children.text: ) vimuktyaparyantatayā vimuktijñānadarśanāparyantatayā śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / pṛthagjanadharmāparyantatayā śrāvakadharmāparyantatayā pratyekabuddhadharmāparyantatayā buddhadharmāparyantatayā śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / vidyāparyantatayā vimuktyaparyantatayā vimuktijñā[nadarśa]nāparyantatayā śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāparyantatā anugantavyā / paryantānupalabdhitaḥ śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāparyantatetyucyate, antānupalabdhito 'nantetyucyate / ananteti śāradvatīputra aparyantavacanametat / ātmānupādānataḥ śāradvatīputra sarvadharmānantatā anugantavyā / ākāśānantatayā śāradvatīputra sarvadharmānantāparyantā anugantavyā /
children.translated_text: ) through the boundlessness of liberation, through the boundlessness of the knowledge and vision of liberation, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the boundlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be understood. Through the boundlessness of the <s>dharmas</s> of ordinary people, through the boundlessness of the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, through the boundlessness of the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, through the boundlessness of the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the boundlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be understood. Through the boundlessness of knowledge, through the boundlessness of liberation, through the boundlessness of the knowledge and vision of liberation, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the boundlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be understood. From the non-apprehension of a limit, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is called 'the limit of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>'; from the non-apprehension of an end, it is called 'endless.' 'Endless,' <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is a term for 'boundless.' From the non-grasping of a self, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the endlessness of all <s>dharmas</s> is to be understood. Through the endlessness of space, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the endless and boundless nature of all <s>dharmas</s> is to be understood.

For, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, neither the end, middle, nor conclusion of this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is apprehended, nor is it apprehended by anyone. This, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is a perfection without end and without limit — namely, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Just as, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the end of space is not apprehended, even so the end of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not apprehended. Through the boundlessness of the earth element, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the boundlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be seen. Through the boundlessness of the water element, the fire element, the wind element, and the consciousness element, the boundlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be understood. For, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be understood as without end, middle, or limit. For, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not located in any place or region.

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān śāradvatīputro bhagavantametadavocat - kīdṛśānāṃ bhagavan bodhisattvānāmeṣu dharmeṣu viṣayaḥ? bhagavānāha - ye te śāradvatīputra bodhisattvā dharmamapi nopalabhante prāgevādharmam, mārgamapi nopalabhante prāgevāmārgam, śīlamapi nopalabhante na manyante prāgeva dauḥśīlyam, aparyāpannāśca sarvatraidhātuke, aparyāpannāśca sarvabhavagaticyutyupapattiṣu, anadhyavasitāśca kāye jīvite ca prāgeva bāhyeṣu vastuṣu, kṛtaparyantāśca saṃsārasrotasaḥ, uttīrṇāśca mahābhavārṇavāt, samuttīrṇāśca mahāsaṃgrāmāt, teṣāṃ śāriputra bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmeṣu dharmeṣu viṣayaśca gatiśca, sarvaviṣayā aviṣayā iti ca yeṣāṃ parijānante (parijñānam?), te tathārūpāḥ satpuruṣāḥ sarvaviṣayeṣvanadhyavasitāḥ, te mahāsiṃhāḥ / te sarvaviṣayeṣvanadhyāpannāḥ, te tadrūpāḥ satpuruṣāḥ / sarvaviṣayanirupaliptāste, te 'saṃsṛṣṭāḥ / sarvaviṣayasamatikrāntāste, te mahāsārthavāhāḥ / yeṣāṃ śāradvatīputra eṣu dharmeṣu viṣayo gatiśca / nāhaṃ śāradvatīputra asyāṃ parṣadi samanupaśyāmi ekamapi bodhisattvam, yasya naiṣu dharmeṣu viṣayo vā adhimuktirvā, yo vā eṣu dharmeṣu sākāṅkṣo vā savicikitso vā / niṣkāṅkṣeyaṃ śāradvatīputra parṣadeṣu dharmeṣu nirvicikitsā nirvaimatikā / nāsti śāradvatīputra eṣāṃ bodhisatvānāmeṣu dharmeṣu vimatiḥ / vimatisamuddhātāya śāradvatīputra ete satpuruṣāḥ sarvasattvānāṃ sthitāḥ / niḥsaṃśayā hyete śāradvatīputra eṣvevaṃrūpeṣu dharmeṣu saṃśayasamatikrāntāḥ //
children.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> spoke to the Blessed One: 'What kind of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, Blessed One, have these <s>dharmas</s> as their domain?' The Blessed One said: 'Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, who do not apprehend even <s>Dharma</s>, much less non-<s>Dharma</s>; who do not apprehend even the path, much less the non-path; who do not apprehend or conceive of even morality, much less immorality; who are not included in the entire triple world; who are not included in all states of existence, destinies, deaths, and rebirths; who are not attached to the body or life, much less to external things; who have reached the end of the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s>; who have crossed the great ocean of existence; who have emerged from the great battle — for those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, these <s>dharmas</s> are their domain and their course. Those who comprehend that all domains are non-domains — such true persons are not attached to any domain; they are great lions. They are not caught in any domain; they are such true persons. They are untouched by all domains; they are unentangled. They have transcended all domains; they are great caravan leaders. For them, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, these <s>dharmas</s> are their domain and course. I do not see, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, in this assembly even a single <s>bodhisattva</s> for whom these <s>dharmas</s> are not a domain or conviction, or who has doubt or uncertainty regarding these <s>dharmas</s>. This assembly, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is free from doubt regarding these <s>dharmas</s>, free from uncertainty, free from disagreement. There is no hesitation, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, among these <s>bodhisattvas</s> regarding these <s>dharmas</s>. These true persons stand for the uprooting of hesitation in all beings. For they are, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, without doubt regarding such <s>dharmas</s>, having transcended doubt.'

children.text: ye 'pi te śāradvatīputra paścime kāle paścime samaye imāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ śroṣyanti, te 'pi niḥsaṃśayā bhaviṣyanti sarvadharmeṣu, sarvasattvānāṃ ca saṃśayacchedanāya pratipannā bhaviṣyanti, niḥsaṃśayāśca te dharmaṃ deśayiṣyanti / nāhaṃ śāradvatīputra parīttakuśalamūlānāṃ sattvānāmeṣu dharmeṣvadhimuktiṃ vadāmi / nāpi teṣāmeṣu dharmeṣvavakāśaḥ, nāpi teṣāmidaṃ dhanam / nāpi te śāradvatīputra sattvāḥ parīttakuśalamūlasamanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti, yeṣāmiyaṃ dharmadeśanāṃ śrotrapathamapyāgamiṣyati kimaṅga punarye udgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti / niyatāste buddhadharmeṣu, vyākṛtāste buddhairbhagavadbhiḥ / evaṃ ca te siṃhanādaṃ nadiṣyanti yathāhametarhi siṃhanādaṃ nadāmi astambhitanādaṃ mahāpuruṣanādaṃ svayaṃbhūnādam / ye eṣu dharmeṣvatyantaśaḥ śraddhāṃ janayitvā chandaṃ janayiṣyanti anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, (
Vaidya 35
children.translated_text: [<s>Vaidya</s> 35]

children.text: ) teṣāmapi ta eeva vyākaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyanti / tatkamāddhetoḥ? durlabhā hi śāradvatīputra te sattvāḥ, ya imān gambhīrān dharmān śrutvā prītiṃ ca vindanti, prāmodyaṃ ca janayanti, adhimuñcante ca / ataḥ śāradvatīputra durlabhatamāste sattvāḥ, ye gambhīrān dharmān śrutvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayanti, chandaṃ ca janayanti mahākuśalamūlasamanvāgatāḥ / nāhaṃ śāradvatīputra tān sattvān mahāsaṃsārasaṃprasthitāniti vadāmi yeṣāmayaṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśaḥ śravaṇapathamapyāgamiṣyati, śrutvā ca (ye) paṭhiṣyanti adhimokṣyanti udāraṃ ca prītisaumanasyaṃ janayiṣyanti, eṣu dharmeṣu chandaṃ janayiṣyanti punaḥ punaḥ śravaṇāyāpi, kaḥ punarvādaḥ uddeṣṭuṃ vā svādhyātuṃ vā parebhyo deśayituṃ vā / vyākaromyahaṃ śāradvatīputra anavakrāntaniyāmān aniyatān śrāvakapratyekabuddhayāne anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhauḥ / nāhaṃ śāradvatīputra hīnadharmasamanvāgatānāṃ sattvānāmagrato dharmeṣvavakāśaṃ samanupaśyāmi / udāreyaṃ śāradvatīputra buddhabodhiḥ / yadbhūyasā ca sattvā hīnādhimuktikā hīnadharmasamanvāgatā akṛtakalyāṇāḥ / akuśalā eṣvevaṃrūpeṣu gambhīreṣu dharmeṣu nirupalepeṣu / ye punaste śāradvatīputra udārāḥ sattvā udāradharmādhimuktā mahāyānasaṃprasthitāḥ supariprāptakāryāḥ susaṃnāhasaṃnaddhāḥ suvicitrārthā mahāmārgeṇa saṃprasthitā aviṣameṇa ṛjunā, agahanena samena apagatakhāṇukaṇṭakena apagataśvabhraprapātena śucinā apagatakilbiṣeṇa akuṭilena avaṅkena, ye lokahitāya saṃprasthitā lokasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya va devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca, avabhāsakarāstīrthabhūtāḥ sattvānām, mahākāruṇikā hitānukampakā hitakāmāḥ sukhakāmā yogakṣemakāmāḥ, sarvasattvānāṃ sukhopadhānāya pratyupasthitāḥ, teṣāṃ śāradvatīputra tathārūpāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmidaṃ mahādhanam / ta eva ca śāradvatīputra mahāsattvā asya dharmaratnasya pratyeṣakāḥ / teṣāṃ caitaddhanamudāradhanam / tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi śāradvatīputra akṛtapuṇyānāṃ sattvānāmakṛtakalyāṇānāṃ hīnādhimuktikānāṃ śraddhāvihīnānāmasminnudāre dhane 'dhimuktirjāyate / etacca me śāradvatīputra saṃdhāya bhāṣitam - dhātuśaḥ satvāḥ saṃsyandanti hīnādhimuktikā hīnādhimuktikaiḥ, udārādhimuktikā udārādhimuktikairiti //
children.translated_text: ) — for them too there will be that same prediction. Why? Rare indeed, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are those beings who, hearing these profound <s>dharmas</s>, find joy, generate gladness, and have conviction. Even rarer, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are those beings who, hearing the profound <s>dharmas</s>, generate the mind [set on] unsurpassed perfect awakening and generate aspiration, endowed with great roots of merit. I do not say, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that those beings have set forth on the great <s>saṃsāra</s> for whom this teaching of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> will even reach their ears, and who, having heard it, will recite it, have conviction in it, generate exalted joy and gladness, generate aspiration in these <s>dharmas</s>, and seek to hear it again and again — what need to mention reciting, studying, or teaching it to others? I give prediction, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, to those who have not yet entered upon the certainty of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles, for unsurpassed perfect awakening. I do not see, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, any room in these <s>dharmas</s> for beings endowed with inferior <s>dharmas</s>. This <s>Buddha-bodhi</s>, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is sublime. But for the most part, beings have inferior convictions and are endowed with inferior <s>dharmas</s>, having done no meritorious deeds. They are unskilled in such profound <s>dharmas</s> that are free from defilement. But those beings, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, who are sublime, who have conviction in sublime <s>dharmas</s>, who have set forth on the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, who have well accomplished their task, who are well girded with the armor [of resolve], who have diverse purposes, who have set forth on the great path — the even, straight, unentangled, level path, free of stumps and thorns, free of chasms and precipices, pure, free of defilement, uncrooked, unbent — who have set forth for the welfare of the world, for the happiness of the world, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the great multitude of beings, of gods and humans, who are light-bearers, who are fords for beings, who are greatly compassionate, who are beneficent and sympathetic, who desire welfare, happiness, and security for all beings, who stand ready to provide happiness for all beings — for those beings, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, for those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>, this is the great treasure. They, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are the seekers of this <s>Dharma</s>-jewel. This is their treasure, their sublime treasure. Why? For beings who have not made merit, who have done no good, who have inferior convictions, who are devoid of faith — conviction does not arise in them regarding this sublime treasure. And it is with this meaning in mind, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that I have said: "Beings flow together according to their element — those with inferior convictions with those of inferior convictions, those with sublime convictions with those of sublime convictions."'

'Those too, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, who in the last time, in the last age, will hear this <s>Dharma</s> teaching — they too will be without doubt regarding all <s>dharmas</s> and will be engaged in cutting through the doubts of all beings, and they will teach the <s>Dharma</s> without doubt. I do not speak, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, of conviction in these <s>dharmas</s> for beings with meager roots of merit. Nor do they have room in these <s>dharmas</s>, nor is this their treasure. Nor, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, will those beings be endowed with meager roots of merit for whom this <s>Dharma</s> teaching will even reach their ears — how much more those who will take it up, retain it, recite it, and master it! They are determined in the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>; they have been given prediction by the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. And they will roar the lion's roar just as I now roar the lion's roar — the unshakable roar, the great person's roar, the self-born roar. Those who, having generated supreme faith in these <s>dharmas</s>, will generate aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening (

children.text: āha - kiṃlakṣaṇeya bhagavan prajñāpāramitā? bhagavānāha - alakṣaṇeyaṃ śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramtiā / tadyathāpi nāma śāradvatīputra ākāśadhātuśca vāyudhātuśca na kasyaciddharmasya pariciṣpattilakṣaṇenopagacchataḥ, evameva śāradavtīputra prajñāpāramitā na kasyaciddharmasya pariniṣpattilakṣaṇenopaiti / āha - kiṃlakṣaṇeyaṃ bahgavan prajñāpāramitā? children.translated_text: This <s>Dharma</s> discourse will come into the hands of beings whose wholesome roots have been thoroughly purified. Moreover, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, I declare to you and make known to you: that son of good family or daughter of good family, whether of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle or the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle, having obtained these <s>dharmas</s>, should not be of little enthusiasm, nor lazy, nor drowsy, nor lacking in clear comprehension, nor with unestablished mindfulness, nor with a distracted mind, nor greedy for material things, nor fickle, nor garrulous, nor gluttonous, nor presumptuous, nor with unrefined faculties. Although, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, wholesome roots once created do not deceive, nevertheless, having obtained these <s>dharmas</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should cultivate to an even greater degree: diligence, vigor, enthusiasm, aspiration, non-laziness, restraint of the faculties, and non-garrulousness; and exertion should be made in the foundations of mindfulness and in extensive learning. With aroused vigor, one should strive for the fulfillment of such qualities. This is not the fruit of hearing such <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that a <s>Bodhisattva</s> or one of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle, having heard such <s>dharmas</s>, should fall into negligence, or become complacent, or lose aspiration, or diminish vigor, or display laxity, or become prone to ill-will. That would not be fruitful, nor would such <s>dharmas</s> truly have been heard by such a one. 'Hearing,' <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is a designation for true practice, not for wrong practice. For, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, this <s>Dharma</s> is not heard by one who practices wrongly. You should be skilled in the meaning of what is heard, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, and established in practice. There is no conforming patience (<s>ānulomikī kṣānti</s>) for those who practice wrongly, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>. Practice in this <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is said to be this: that one practices in accordance with the <s>dharmas</s> as they have been taught. For a person endowed with patience and established in practice, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, there is no further going to the lower realms, and he quickly succeeds in these <s>dharmas</s>. One should not become complacent with merely minor wholesome roots. Even one who has not laid down the burden should not become complacent until he is fully accomplished in these <s>dharmas</s>. One who, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is accomplished in these <s>dharmas</s>, trained, and has attained patience, would not further commit <s>karma</s> tending toward the lower realms. Nor would there be laziness or decline for him. Nor would he have fear of falling back. Nor would he become lax. For what reason? Because, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, he has fully understood defilement and purification, and he has seen as it truly is: 'All <s>dharmas</s> arise from perversion; they are unreal.' One who sees rightly thus, endowed with patience, is gentle, energetic, established in the purity of morality, accomplished in conduct, range, behavior, and restraint. Even the gods, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, aspire toward such beings, how much more so humans! Such beings are objects of aspiration even for the gods, how much more for humans! They are worthy of worship even by the gods, how much more by humans! They should be protected even by the gods, how much more by humans! They should be protected by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, who become eager for their protection, shelter, and safety.

In such <s>dharmas</s> as these, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, not many companions are to be found. This is an exposition within the domain of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge — namely, the indication, illumination, and analysis of <s>dharmas</s> in this way. For in these <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, no one

children.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Why, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, do you pass the time in silence? This assembly is pure, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, and it longs to hear the profound <s>Dharma</s>.'

children.text: evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputramevamāha - nāhaṃ tamāyuṣman dharmaṃ samanupaśyāmi yaṃ me ārabhya pratibhāyāt - na cāhamāyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāṃ samanupaśyāmi, na ca bodhisattvaṃ nāpi pratibhānam, nāpi yatpratibhāyāt, nāpi yena pratibhāyāt, nāpi yataḥ pratibhāyāt / evaṃ samanupaśyan nāhamāyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ yacca pratibhāyāt, yena ca pratibhāyāt, yataśca pratibhāyāt, yasya ca pratibhāyāt, kimiti nirdekṣyāmi, kiṃ me ārabhya pratibhāsyati / eṣaivātra āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā yo 'vyāhāraḥ, anudāhāraḥ, anabhihāraḥ, anabhilāpaḥ / na hi āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā śakyodāhārtuṃ vā, pravyāhartuṃ vā, abhilapituṃ vā / yaivaṃ visarjanā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / na hi āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā atītā vā anāgatā vā pratyutpannā vā / na hi āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā atītalakṣaṇā vā śakyā nirdeṣṭum, anāgatalakṣaṇā vā pratyutpannalakṣaṇā vā / alakṣaṇā avyavahārā eṣā āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā / nāhamāyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitāyā lakṣaṇaṃ samanupaśyāmi, yena lakṣaṇena prajñāpāramitā nirdiśyeta / na hi āyuṣman śāradvatīputra yadrūpasya atītalakṣaṇaṃ vā anāgatalakṣaṇaṃ vā pratyutpannalakṣaṇaṃ vā, sā prajñāpāramitā / nāpi yadvedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāmatītalakṣaṇaṃ vā anāgatalakṣaṇaṃ vā pratyutpannalakṣaṇaṃ vā sā prajñāpāramitā / yacca āyuṣman śāradvatīputra atītānāgatapratyutpannarūpalakṣaṇasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, sā prajñāpāramitā / yā ca atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / yā ca āyuṣman śāradvatīputra atītānāgatapratyutpannasya rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānalakṣaṇasya tathatā avitathatā ananyatathatā yāvattathatā, sā na śakyā prajñapayituṃ vā udāhartuṃ vā abhilapituṃ vā vākkarmaṇā vā visarjayitum / ya āyuṣman śāradvatīputra evaṃ prajñāpāramitānirdeśamavatarati, sa prajñāpāramitāṃ budhyate / na hi āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā kasyaciddharmasya nirdeśalakṣaṇena pratyupasthitā, na rūpanidarśanalakṣaṇena pratyupasthitā, na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānanirdeśalakṣaṇena pratyupasthitā, na saṃskāranirdeśalakṣaṇena, na pratītyasamutpādanirdeśalakṣaṇena, na nāmarūpalakṣaṇena, nātmalakṣaṇena, na sattvalakṣaṇena, na dharmadhātulakṣaṇena, na saṃyogalakṣaṇena, na visaṃyogalakṣaṇena, na hetulakṣaṇena, na pratyayalakṣaṇena, na duḥkhalakṣaṇena, (
Vaidya 40
children.translated_text: [Vaidya p. 40]

children.text: ) na sukhalakṣaṇena, na vyavasthānalakṣaṇena nāvyavasthānalakṣaṇena, notpādalakṣaṇena na vyayalakṣaṇena, na saṃkleśalakṣaṇena na vyavadānalakṣaṇena, na prakṛtilakṣaṇena, (na) saṃvṛtilakṣaṇena na paramārthalakṣaṇena, na satyalakṣaṇena na mṛṣālakṣaṇena, na saṃkrāntilakṣaṇena nāvakrāntilakṣaṇena pratyupasthitā / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvalakṣaṇavigatā hi āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā / sā na kasyaciddarśanamupaiti - iyaṃ vā prajñāpāramitā, iha vā prajñāpāramitā, anena vā prajñāpāramitā, asya vā prajñāpāramiteti //
children.translated_text: — not by the mark of pleasure; not by the mark of stability nor instability; not by the mark of arising nor cessation; not by the mark of defilement nor purification; not by the mark of nature; not by the mark of conventional [truth] nor ultimate [truth]; not by the mark of truth nor falsehood; not by the mark of transmigration nor descent. For what reason? Because, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is free from all marks. It does not come within the range of any perception: 'This is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,' or 'Here is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,' or 'By this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,' or 'This one's is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

Thus addressed, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'I do not perceive, Venerable, any <s>dharma</s> regarding which something might occur to my mind. Nor do I, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, perceive <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, nor a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, nor the occurrence of thought, nor that about which thought might occur, nor that by which it might occur, nor that from which it might occur. Perceiving thus, I do not perceive, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> — that about which, by which, from which, or for whom thought might occur — what shall I expound? What will occur to my mind? This itself, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>: that which is non-utterance, non-declaration, non-assertion, non-expression. For, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> cannot be declared, or uttered, or expressed. That which is thus a letting-go — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is neither past, nor future, nor present. Nor can <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, be pointed out by the mark of the past, or the future, or the present. This <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is without mark and without conventional designation. I do not perceive, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, any mark of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> by which <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> could be pointed out. For, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that which is the mark of the past, future, or present of form — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Nor is that which is the mark of the past, future, or present of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — that is not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But that, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, which is the suchness (<s>tathatā</s>) of the mark of past, future, and present form — the non-distorted suchness, the non-other suchness, the suchness-as-it-is — that is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And that which is the suchness of past, future, and present feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — the non-distorted suchness, the non-other suchness, the suchness-as-it-is — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And that, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, which is the suchness of the mark of past, future, and present form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — the non-distorted suchness, the non-other suchness, the suchness-as-it-is — that cannot be conceptualized, declared, expressed, or communicated through verbal action. One who, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, thus enters the exposition of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, understands <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not present by way of the mark of exposition of any <s>dharma</s>; not present by way of the mark of illustrating form; not present by way of the mark of exposition of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness; not by the mark of exposition of formations; not by the mark of exposition of dependent origination; not by the mark of name-and-form; not by the mark of self; not by the mark of being; not by the mark of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>; not by the mark of conjunction; not by the mark of disjunction; not by the mark of cause; not by the mark of condition; not by the mark of suffering —

children.text: nāhamāyuṣman śāradvatīputra taṃ dharmaṃ samanupaśyāmi yena dharmeṇa prajñāpāramitā nirdiśyeta / na hi āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā kasyaciddharmasya nidarśanamupaiti vā utpaśyati vā / na hi āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā rūpasya nidarśanamupaiti, na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ nidarśanamupaiti, na cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanasāṃ nidarśanamupaiti / nāpi dhātvāyatanānāṃ nidarśanamupaiti, na pratītyasamutpādasya nidarśanamupaiti, nāpi vidyāvimuktyornidarśanamupaiti / yāpi sā āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñā lokottarā nirvedhagāminī, tasyā api prajñāpāramitā nidarśanaṃ nopaiti / tadyathā āyuṣman śāradvatīputra dharmo nidarśanaṃ nopaiti kasyaciddharmasya, kathaṃ tasyā eva udāhāranirdeśo bhaviṣyati? api tu khalu āyuṣman śāradvatīputra ya evaṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmanayaṃ prajānanti, te prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ prajānanti //
children.translated_text: I do not, O venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, perceive any <s>dharma</s> by which <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> could be expounded. For, O venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not approach or observe the indication of any <s>dharma</s>. For, O venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not approach the indication of form, nor of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness; nor of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind. Nor does it approach the indication of elements or sense-bases; nor of dependent origination; nor of knowledge or liberation. Even that wisdom, O venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, which is supramundane and leads to penetration — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not approach even its indication.

children.text: na hi āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā kasyaciddharmasya saṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, nāpi nidarśanen / na hi āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā rūpasya saṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanen / na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ saṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanena / na nāmarūpasya saṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanena / na saṃkleśasya na vyavadānasya saṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanena / na pratītyasamutpādasya saṃdarśanen pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanena / na viparyāsānāṃ saṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanena / na sattvadhātoḥ, nātmadhātoḥ saṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanena / na pṛthivīdhātoḥ, na aptejovāyudhātoḥ saṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanena / na kāmadhātoḥ, na rūpadhātoḥ, na ārūpyadhātoḥ saṃdarśanena pratyutpasthitā, na nidarśanena / na dānamātsaryaśīladauḥśīlyasaṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā na nidarśanena / na kṣāntivyāpādavīryakausīdyadhyānavikṣepaprajñādauṣprajñyasaṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanena / na smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇarddhipādāpramāṇendriyabalabodhyaṅgavimokṣasamādhisamāpattyabhijñāsaṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanena / na satyamārgaphalasaṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanena / na śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvabhūmisaṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanena / na śrāvakadharma na pratyekabuddhadharma, na bodhisattvadharma, (
Vaidya 41
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 41)

children.text: ) na buddhadharmasaṃdarśanena pratyupasthitā, na nidarśanena / nāpi kasyaciddharmasya jñānena vā ajñānena vā saṃdarśanena vā nidarśanena vā pratyupasthitā / nāpyanutpādajñānasya vā kṣayajñānasya vā nirodhajñānasya vā saṃdarśanena vā nidarśanena vā pratyupasthitā / nāpi nirvāṇasya saṃdarśanena vā nidarśanena vā pratyupasthitā / tadyathā āyuṣman śāradvatīputra na kasyaciddharmasya saṃdarśanena vā pratyupasthitā nidarśanena vā, kathaṃ tasyā vyavahāraṃ nirdekṣyāmi? api tu khalu āyuṣman śāradvatīputra ya evaṃ nirdeśamavabudhyate - na prajñāpāramitā kasyaciddharmasya saṃdarśanena vā nidarśanena vā pratyupasthiteti, sa prajñāpāramitāṃ jānīte, prajñāpāramitānirdeśaṃ ca prajānīte / na hi āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā kasyaciddharmasya yogāya vā viyogāya vā pratyupasthitā / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi āyuṣman śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā rūpaṃ saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / na pratītyasamutpādaṃ saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / na kāmadhātuṃ na rūpadhātuṃ nārūpyadhātuṃ saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / na pṛthivīdhātuṃ nābdhātuṃ na tejodhātuṃ na vāyudhātuṃ saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / na sattvadhātuṃ nātmadhātuṃ na dharmadhātuṃ nākāśadhātuṃ saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / na dānaṃ na mātsaryaṃ na śīlaṃ na dauḥśīlyaṃ na kṣāntiṃ na vyāpādaṃ na vīryaṃ na kausīdyaṃ na dhyānaṃ na vikṣepaṃ na prajñāṃ na dauṣprajñyaṃ saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / na smṛtyupasthānāni na samyakprahāṇāni na ṛddhipādāpramāṇāni nendriyabalabodhyaṅgadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattyabhijñāḥ saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / na mārgaṃ na mārgaphalaṃ na duḥkhaṃ na duḥkhasamudayaṃ na nirodhaṃ saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / na śrāvakabhūmiṃ na pratyekabuddhabhūmiṃ na bodhisattvabhūmiṃ na buddhabhūmiṃ saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / na śrāvakadharmān na pratyekabuddhadharmān na bodhisattvadharmān na buddhadharmān saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / nātītānāgatapratyutpannatryadhvasamatāṃ saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / nāsaṅgatānutpādajñānaṃ na kṣayajñānaṃ na nirvāṇaṃ saṃyojayati na visaṃyojayati / tadyathā āyuṣman śāradvatīputra dharmo na kasyaciddharmasya saṃyogāya vā visaṃyogāya vā pratyupasthitaḥ, kathaṃ tasya nirdeśo bhaviṣyati? idamāyuṣman śāradvatīputra arthavaśaṃ saṃpaśyannahamevaṃ vadāmi - nāhaṃ taṃ dharmaṃ samanupaśyāmi yo me dharmaḥ pratibhāyāt, yena me pratibhāyāt, yato me pratibhāyāt, yaṃ me ārabhya pratibhāyāditi //
children.translated_text: Nor is it present through the demonstration or indication of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s. Nor is it present through the knowledge or ignorance, demonstration or indication of any <s>dharma</s>. Nor is it present through the demonstration or indication of the knowledge of non-arising, the knowledge of exhaustion, or the knowledge of cessation. Nor is it present through the demonstration or indication of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Since, O venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is not present through the demonstration or indication of any <s>dharma</s>, how shall I expound its conventional usage? But indeed, O venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, whoever understands this exposition — that <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not present through the demonstration or indication of any <s>dharma</s> —

For, O venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not present through the demonstration or indication of any <s>dharma</s>. For, O venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not present through the demonstration or indication of form; nor of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness; nor of name-and-form; nor of defilement or purification; nor of dependent origination; nor of perversions; nor of the being-element or the self-element.

children.text: āryaprajñāpāramitāyāṃ subhūtiparivartaḥ pañcamaḥ //
children.translated_text: The <s>Subhūti</s> Chapter, the Fifth, in the Noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: START Svp 6
children.translated_text: [Start of Section 6]

children.text: Vaidya 42
6 caryāparivartaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 6. The Sixth Chapter on Conduct (<s>Caryāparivarta</s>).

children.text: atha khalu bhagavān suvikrāntavikrāmiṇaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - iha khalu suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caranna kvaciddharme carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? sarvadharmā hi suvikrāntavikrāmin viparyāsasamutthitāḥ, abhūtā asanto mithyā vitathāḥ / tadyathā suvikrāntavikrāmin kasmiṃściddharme carati, viparyāse sa carati / viparyāse caran na bhūte carati / na ca suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo viparyāsacaryāprabhāvitaḥ, abhūtacaryāprabhāvito vā / nāpi viparyāse vā abhūte vā caran bodhisattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati / yaśca viparyāsaḥ, so 'bhūtaḥ / na tatra kāciccaryā, tena tatra bodhisattvo na carati / viparyāsa iti suvikrāntavikrāmin vitathaḥ / eṣa bālapṛthagjanairgṛhītaḥ / na tathā yaiste te dharmāḥ / ye ca na tathā yathā gṛhītāḥ, sa ucyate 'viparyāso 'tra bhūta iti / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo mahāsattvo viparyāse vā abhūte vā carati / bhūtavādīti suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo 'viparyāsacārī / yatra ca bhūtamaviparyāsaḥ, tatra ca na kāciccaryā / tenocyate - acaryā bodhisattvacaryeti / sarvacaryāsamucchinnā hi suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvacaryā / sā na śakyā ādarśayitum - iyaṃ vā bodhisattvacaryā, anena vā bodhisattvacaryā, iha vā bodhisattvacaryā, ito vā bodhisattvacaryeti / naivaṃ bodhisattvacaryā prabhāvitā / sarvacaryāvinivṛttaye hi bodhisattvā bodhisattvacaryāṃ caranti pṛthagjanacaryāvinivṛttaye śrāvakacaryāvinivṛtaye pratyekabuddhacaryāvinivṛttaye / ye 'pi te suvikrāntavikrāmin buddhadharmāḥ, teṣvapi bodhisattvā na caranti nābhiniviśante - ime vā te bodhisattvadharmāḥ, iha vā te bodhisattvadharmāḥ, anena vā te bodhisattvadharmāḥ, asya vā te bodhisattvadharmā iti / evamapi suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na carati / sarvā eṣāṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin vikalpacaryā / na bodhisattvo vikalpe carati nāvikalpe / sarvavikalpaprahīṇā hi bodhisattvacaryā / kalpa iti suvikrāntavikrāmin vikalpanaiṣā sarvadharmāṇām / na hi śakyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ kalpayitum / akalpitā hi sarvadharmāḥ / tadyo dharmaṃ kalpayati, sa vikalpayati / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin dharmaḥ kalpo vā vikalpo vā / kalpa iti suvikrāntavikrāmin eṣa eko 'ntaḥ, vikalpa iti dvitīyo 'ntaḥ / na ca suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo 'nte carati, nāpyanante / yo naiva ante na anante carati, sa madhyaṃ na samanupaśyati / madhyamapi suvikrāntavikrāmin samanupaśyan madhye caran anta eva carati / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin madhyasya kāciccaryā (vā kiṃci)ddarśanaṃ vā(nidarśanaṃ vā) / madhyamiti suvikrāntavikrāmin (
Vaidya 43
children.translated_text: [Vaidya 43]

children.text: ) nāpi āryāṣṭāṅgamārgasyaitadadhivacanam / na ca suvikrāntavikrāmin āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ kasyaciddharmasyopalambhena pratyupasthitaḥ, nāpi kasyaciddharmasya samanupaśyanatayā //
children.translated_text: ) nor is this a designation of the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>). And, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the noble eightfold path does not serve through the apprehension of any <s>dharma</s>, nor through perceiving any <s>dharma</s>.

Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>: 'Here, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, when a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he does not practice in any <s>dharma</s>. For what reason? All <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, have arisen from perversion (<s>viparyāsa</s>); they are unreal, non-existent, false, and untrue. Insofar as one practices in some <s>dharma</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, one practices in perversion. Practicing in perversion, one does not practice in the real. And, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is not dominated by the practice of perversion, nor by the practice of the unreal. Nor does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who practices in perversion or the unreal practice <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. What is perversion is unreal. There is no practice therein; therefore the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not practice therein. "Perversion," <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, means what is untrue. It is grasped by foolish ordinary persons. Those <s>dharmas</s> are not as they are grasped. And what is not as it is grasped is called "perversion here being real." Indeed, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> does not practice in perversion or in the unreal. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> is called a speaker of truth, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, because he practices without perversion. And where there is the real and non-perversion, there is no practice. Therefore it is said: "The practice of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is non-practice." For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the practice of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> cuts off all practices. It cannot be shown: "this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice," or "by this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice," or "here is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice," or "from here is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice." The <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice is not thus constituted. For <s>Bodhisattvas</s> practice the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice for the cessation of all practices — for the cessation of the practice of ordinary persons, for the cessation of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> practice, for the cessation of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> practice. Even in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> do not practice or become attached — "these are the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharmas</s>," "here are the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharmas</s>," "by this are the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharmas</s>," "his are the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharmas</s>." Even thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not practice. All of this, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is practice of conceptual discrimination (<s>vikalpa</s>). A <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not practice in discrimination nor in non-discrimination. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice has abandoned all discrimination. "Imagining" (<s>kalpa</s>), <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the discrimination of all <s>dharmas</s>. All <s>dharmas</s> cannot be imagined. All <s>dharmas</s> are unimagined. Whoever imagines a <s>dharma</s>, discriminates. Indeed, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a <s>dharma</s> is neither imagination nor discrimination. "Imagination," <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is one extreme; "discrimination" is the second extreme. A <s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, does not practice in extremes, nor in non-extremes. One who practices in neither extreme nor non-extreme does not perceive a middle. Even perceiving the middle, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, and practicing in the middle, one actually practices in an extreme. children.text: api tu yasmin samaye suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na kaṃciddharmaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati, tadā pratiprasrabdhamārga ityucyate / sa sarvadharmān na bhāvayanna vibhāvayan bhāvanāsamatikrānto dharmasamatāmanuprāpnoti, yayā dharmasamatayā mārgasaṃjñāpyasya na pravartate, kutaḥ punarmārgaṃ drakṣyati? pratiprasrabdhamārga iti suvikrāntavikrāmin arhataḥ kṣīṇāsravasyaitadbhikṣoradhivacanam / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? vibhāvito hi sa mārgo na bhāvito na vibhāvitaḥ / tenocyate vibhāvita iti / vibhāvanāpi tatra nāsti, tenocyate vibhāvita iti / vigatā tasya bhāvanā, tenocyate vibhāvaneti / sacetkhalu punaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin bhāvanā syādvibhāvanā vā, sā punarupalabhyate, nāsyā vibhāvanā syāt / vibhāvaneti suvikrāntavikrāmin vigatā asyāṃ bhāvaneti vibhāvanā, bhāvo 'syā vigata iti, tenocyate vibhāvaneti, na punaryathocyate / tatkasmāt? avyāhārā hi vibhāvanā, vigama eṣa vibhāvanā / katamo vigamaḥ? yato viparyāsasya asamutthānaṃ yadabhūtasyāsamutthānam / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin viparyāso viparyāsaṃ samutthāpayati / asamutthita eṣa viparyāsaḥ / na hi tatra kiṃcitsamutthānam / yadi tatra kiṃcitsamutthānamabhaviṣyat, nocyeta / yasmādabhūtasamutthitaḥ, tasmāducyate viparyāsa iti / aviparyāstā hi suvikrāntavikrāmin sarvadharmā bodhisattvenānubuddhāḥ / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? jñāto hi tena viparyāso 'bhūta iti / na viparyāse viparyāsaḥ saṃvidyate / yena viparyāso 'bhūto jñātaḥ, na viparyāse viparyāsaḥ saṃvidyate, tena aviparyastāḥ sarvadharmāḥ samanubuddhāḥ / yaśca aviparyāsasyānubodhaḥ, na tatra bhūyo viparyāsaḥ / yatra (na) kaścidviparyāsaḥ, tatra na kāciccaryā / sarvā hi suvikrāntavikrāmin caryā sā caryāsamutthānā / caryāvikalpādviparyāsaḥ / bodhisattvastu caryāyāṃ na vikalpayati / tena sārdhamaviparyāsaḥ sthita ityucyate / yaśca aviparyastaḥ, sa na kvacidbhūyaścarati / tenocyate acaryā bodhisattvacareti / acaryeti suvikrāntavikrāmin yanna kvaciddharme carati na vicarati na caryālakṣaṇaṃ saṃdarśayati, iyamucyate bodhisattvacaryeti / ya evaṃ carati, sa carati prajñāpāramitāyām //
children.translated_text: However, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, at the time when a <s>Bodhisattva</s> neither cultivates nor de-cultivates any <s>dharma</s>, then it is called 'the path that has subsided' (<s>pratiprasrabdhamārga</s>). He, neither cultivating nor de-cultivating all <s>dharmas</s>, having transcended cultivation, attains the equality of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasamatā</s>). Through that equality of <s>dharmas</s>, not even the notion of 'path' operates for him — how then would he see a path? 'The path that has subsided,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is a designation for the <s>Arhat</s>, the monk (<s>bhikṣu</s>) whose defilements are destroyed. For what reason? Because that path has been de-cultivated (<s>vibhāvita</s>) — neither cultivated nor de-cultivated. Therefore it is called 'de-cultivated.' And even de-cultivation does not exist therein; therefore it is called 'de-cultivated.' His cultivation has departed; therefore it is called 'de-cultivation.' If, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there were cultivation or de-cultivation, it would again be apprehended, and there would be no de-cultivation of it. 'De-cultivation,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, means 'cultivation has departed therein' — that is de-cultivation; 'the existence thereof has departed' — therefore it is called de-cultivation, but not as it is literally said. For what reason? De-cultivation is beyond verbal expression; it is departure. What departure? The non-arising of perversion, the non-arising of the unreal. For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, perversion does not produce perversion. This perversion is unarisen. There is no arising therein. If there were any arising therein, it would not be so called. Because it has arisen from the unreal, it is called 'perversion.' Indeed, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> have been understood by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> as non-perverted. For what reason? Because he has known perversion to be unreal. Perversion is not found in perversion. By one who has known perversion to be unreal, and for whom perversion is not found in perversion — by him all <s>dharmas</s> are understood as non-perverted. And in the understanding of non-perversion, there is no further perversion. Where there is no perversion, there is no practice. For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, all practice arises from that practice-arising. From the discrimination of practice comes perversion. But a <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not discriminate regarding practice. Therefore he is said to 'stand together with non-perversion.' And one who is non-perverted does not practice anywhere further. Therefore it is said: 'Non-practice is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s practice.' 'Non-practice,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, means that one does not practice in any <s>dharma</s>, does not engage, does not display the mark of practice — this is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice. One who thus practices, practices in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

But the discernment [itself] — therein there is no practice. Therefore it is called 'the non-practice that is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice.' Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s> practice in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? Because all objects have been discerned by him as isolated and known. And where there is isolation (<s>viveka</s>), there is no practice. Therefore it is said: 'Non-practice is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s practice.' children.text: evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo rūpārambaṇapariśuddhāvapi na carati / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānārambaṇapariśuddhāvapi na carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prakṛtipariśuddhaṃ hi tena rūpārambaṇaṃ parijñātam / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānārambaṇaṃ parijñātam / yā evaṃ caryā, iyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na cakṣurārambaṇaviśuddhau carati, na śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanaārambaṇaviśuddhau carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prakṛtipariśuddhaṃ hi tena yāvanmanaārambaṇaṃ parijñātam / yā evaṃ caryā, iyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmārambaṇaviśuddhāvapi carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prakṛtipariśuddhaṃ hi tena yāvaddharmārambaṇaṃ parijñātam / yā evaṃ caryā, iyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na nāmarūpārambaṇaviśuddhāvapi carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prakṛtipariśuddhaṃ hi tena nāmarūpārambaṇaṃ parijñātam / yā evaṃ caryā, iyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo nātmasattvārambaṇaviśuddhāvapi carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? parijñātā hi tena ātmasattvārambaṇaprakṛtiparijñā / yā evaṃ caryā, iyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na jīvabhavapudgalakārakakārayitrutthāpakasamutthāpakavedakavedayitṛdraṣṭrārambaṇapariśuddhāvapi carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prakṛtipariśuddhaṃ hi tena jīvabhavapudgalakārakakārayitrutthāpakasamutthāpakavedakavedayitṛdraṣṭrārambaṇaṃ parijñātam / yā evaṃ caryā, bodhisattvasyeyaṃ prajñāpāramitācaryā / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na viparyāsadṛṣṭigatārambaṇapariśuddhāvapi carati / tatkasya hetoḥ?
