children.text: ) parijñātam / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na kṣāntivyāpādavīryakausīdyadhyānavikṣepaprajñādauṣprajñyārambaṇaviśuddhāvapi carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prakṛtipariśuddhaṃ hi tena kṣāntivyāpādavīryakausīdyadhyānavikṣepaprajñādauṣprajñyārambaṇaṃ parijñātam / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo nātītānāgatapratyutpannārambaṇaviśuddhapi carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prakṛtipariśuddhāni hi tena atītānāgatapratyutpannārambaṇāni parijñātāni / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo nāsaṅgāvaraṇaviśuddhāvapi carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prakṛtipariśuddhaṃ hi tena asaṅgārambaṇaṃ parijñātam / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo nābhijñārambaṇaviśuddhāvapi carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prakṛtipariśuddhaṃ hi tenābhijñārambaṇaṃ parijñātam / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na sarvajñatārambaṇaviśuddhāvapi carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prakṛtipariśuddhaṃ hi tena sarvajñatārambaṇaṃ parijñātam / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām, yanna kasyāṃcidārambaṇaviśuddhau carati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prakṛtipariśuddhatvātsarvārambaṇānām / iyaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya sarvārambaṇaprakṛtipariśuddhiḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ //
children.translated_text: ) Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of patience and ill-will, vigor and laziness, meditation and distraction, wisdom and lack of wisdom. Why? Because the objects of patience and ill-will, vigor and laziness, meditation and distraction, wisdom and lack of wisdom have been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of past, future, and present. Why? Because the objects of past, future, and present have been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of non-attachment and non-obstruction. Why? Because the object of non-attachment has been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of the superknowledges (<s>abhijñās</s>). Why? Because the objects of the superknowledges have been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the object of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>). Why? Because the object of omniscience has been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, in that he does not practice in the purification of any object. Why? Because all objects are inherently pure by nature. This, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the inherent natural purity of all objects for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice even in the purification of the object of form (<s>rūpa</s>). Likewise, he does not practice in the purification of the objects of feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>), or consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). Why? Because the object of form has been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Likewise, the objects of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness have been comprehended. Such practice is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind. Why? Because up to the object of mind, it has been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Such practice is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or mental objects (<s>dharmas</s>). Why? Because up to the object of mental objects, it has been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Such practice is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>). Why? Because the object of name-and-form has been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Such practice is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of self (<s>ātman</s>) and being (<s>sattva</s>). Why? Because the comprehension of the natural purity of the objects of self and being has been accomplished by him. Such practice is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of life-principle, existence, person, doer, causer, raiser, co-raiser, experiencer, one who causes experience, and seer. Why? Because the objects of life-principle, existence, person, doer, causer, raiser, co-raiser, experiencer, one who causes experience, and seer have been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Such practice is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of error (<s>viparyāsa</s>) and wrong views (<s>dṛṣṭigata</s>). Why? Because the objects of error and wrong views have been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Such practice is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of the hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇas</s>). Why? Because the objects of the hindrances have been comprehended as inherently pure by nature. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). Why? Because the objects of dependent origination have been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm. Why? Because the objects of the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm have been comprehended by him as inherently pure by nature. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice in the purification of the objects of generosity and miserliness, morality and immorality. Why? children.text: evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaḥ idaṃ rūpamiti na samanupaśyati, anena rūpamiti na samanupaśyati, asya rūpamiti na samanupaśyati, asmādrūpamiti na samanupaśyati / sa evaṃ rūpamasamanupaśyan na rūpamutkṣipati na nikṣipati, na rūpamutpādayati na nirodhayati, na rūpe carati na vicarati, na rūpārambaṇe carati na vicarati / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām / evamime vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ, idaṃ vijñānamiti na samanupaśyati, anena vijñānamiti na samanupaśyati, asya vijñānamiti na samanupaśyati, asmādvijñānamiti na samanupaśyati / sa evaṃ vijñānamasamanupaśyan na vijñānamutkṣipati na nikṣipati, na vijñānamutpādayati na nirodhayati, na vijñāne carati na vicarati, na vijñānārambaṇe carati na vicarati / evaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām //
children.translated_text: Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not perceive 'this is form,' does not perceive 'form is by this,' does not perceive 'form is of this,' does not perceive 'form is from this.' Thus not perceiving form, he neither picks it up nor puts it down; he neither produces form nor ceases it; he neither engages in form nor investigates it; he neither engages in the object of form nor investigates it. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise with feeling, perception, and formations. He does not perceive 'this is consciousness,' does not perceive 'consciousness is by this,' does not perceive 'consciousness is of this,' does not perceive 'consciousness is from this.' Thus not perceiving consciousness, he neither picks it up nor puts it down; he neither produces consciousness nor ceases it; he neither engages in consciousness nor investigates it; he neither engages in the object of consciousness nor investigates it. Thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin evaṃ caran bodhisattvo na rūpamatītamiti carati, na rūpamanāgatamiti carati, na rūpaṃ pratyutpannamiti carati / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / na vijñānamatītamiti carati, na anāgatam, na pratyutpannam //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, practicing thus, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice 'form is past,' does not practice 'form is future,' does not practice 'form is present.' Likewise with feeling, perception, and formations. He does not practice 'consciousness is past,' nor 'future,' nor 'present.'

children.text: na rūpamātmeti carati, na rūpamātmīyamiti carati / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / na vijñānamātmeti carati, na vijñānamātmīyamiti carati / na rūpaṃ duḥkhamiti carati / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ duḥkhamiti carati / na rūpaṃ mama nānyeṣāmiti carati / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ mama nānyeṣāmiti carati / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām //
children.translated_text: He does not practice 'form is self,' does not practice 'form is mine.' Likewise with feeling, perception, and formations. He does not practice 'consciousness is self,' does not practice 'consciousness is mine.' He does not practice 'form is suffering.' Likewise with feeling, perception, and formations. He does not practice 'consciousness is suffering.' He does not practice 'form is mine or others'.' Likewise with feeling, perception, and formations. He does not practice 'consciousness is mine or others'.' Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text: punaraparaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaḥ evaṃ prajñāpāramitāyaṃ caran na rūpaṃ nityaṃ nānityamiti carati, na rūpaṃ śūnyaṃ nāśūnyamiti carati, na rūpaṃ māyopamamiti carati, na rūpaṃ svapnopamamiti carati, na rūpaṃ pratibhāsopamamiti carati, na rūpaṃ pratiśrutkopamamiti carati / evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ nityaṃ nānityamiti carati, na vijñānaṃ śūnyaṃ nāśūnyamiti carati, na vijñānaṃ māyopamamiti carati, na vijñānaṃ svapnopamamiti carati, na vijñānaṃ pratibhāsopamamiti carati, na vijñānaṃ pratiśrutkopamamiti carati / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvāṇyetāni suvikrāntavikrāmin vitarkitāni vicaritāni caritavicaritāni / tatra suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaḥ etāni sarvāṇi vitarkitāni vicaritāni caritavicaritāni jñātvā sarvacaryāsamuddhātāya sarvacaryāparijñāyai prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati / ayaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya sarvacaryānirdeśaḥ //

children.text: evamukte suvikrāntavikrāmī bodhisattvo bhagavantometadavocat - acintyeyaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / bhagavānāha - evametat suvikrāntavikrāmin / rūpācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / nāmarūpācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / pratītyasamutpādācintyatayā saṃkleśācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya (
Vaidya 49

children.text: ) prajñāpāramitācaryā / karmavipākācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / sārācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhi(sattva)sya prajñāpāramitācaryā / viparyāsācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā, dṛṣṭigatācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / kāmadhātvacintyatayā, rūpadhātvacintyatayā, ārūpyadhātvacintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / ātmācintyatayā, sattvācintyatayā, dānācintyatayā, mātsaryācintyatayā, śīlācintyatayā, dauḥśīlyācintyatayā, kṣāntyacintyatayā, vyāpādācintyatayā, vīryācintyatayā, kausīdyācintyatayā, dhyānācintyatayā vikṣepācintyatayā, prajñācintyatayā, dauṣprajñyācintyatayā acintyā bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / rāgadveṣamohācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / smṛtyupasthānācintyatayā samyakprahāṇāviparyāsarddhipādācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / indriyabalabodhyaṅgasamādhisamāpattyacintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / gatyacintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / vidyāvimuktyacintyatayā, kṣayajñānānutpādajñānābhisaṃskārajñānācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / śrāvakabhūmipratyekabuddhabhūmyacintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / śrāvakapratyekabuddhadharmācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / abhijñācintyatayā, atītānāgatapratyutpannajñānācintyatayā acintyā bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / asaṅgajñānācintyatayā, nirvāṇācintyatayā, buddhadharmācintyatayā acintyeyaṃ bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitācaryā cittajanikā, tenocyate acintyeti //
children.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is inconceivable. By the inconceivability of <s>karma</s>-ripening (<s>karmavipāka</s>), the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is inconceivable. By the inconceivability of essence (<s>sāra</s>), the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is inconceivable. By the inconceivability of inversion (<s>viparyāsa</s>), the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is inconceivable.

When this was said, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Inconceivable (<s>acintya</s>), O Blessed One, is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>. By the inconceivability of form, the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s practice of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is inconceivable.

children.text: cittasyotpāda iti suvikrāntavikrāmin viparyāsa eṣaḥ / cittaṃ cittajamiti suvikrāntavikrāmiṃścetasaḥ pratiṣedha eṣaḥ / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin yā cittasya prakṛtiḥ sā utpadyate jā jāyate vā / viparyāsasaṃprayuktaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmiṃścittamutpadyate / tatra cittamapi vivṛtam, yena viparyāsenotpadyate tadati vivṛtam / na punaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin bālapṛthagjanā jānanti vivṛtaṃ cittamiti / yatrāpyutpadyeta tadapi vivṛtam, yenāpyutpadyeta tadapi vivṛtamiti / te cittavivekamajānantaḥ, ārambaṇavivekamajānantaḥ abhiniviśante - ahaṃ cittam, mama cittam, asya cittam, asmāccittamiti / te cittamabhiniviśya kuśalamiti vā abhiniviśante, akuśalamiti vā abhiniviśante / sukhamiti vā abhiniviśante, duḥkhamiti vā abhiniviśante / uccheda ityabhiniviśante, śāścata ityabhiniviśante, dṛṣṭigata ityabhiniviśante, nīvaraṇa ityabhiniviniśante / dānamātsaryaśīladauḥśīlyamityabhiniviśante / dharmadhātukāmadhāturūpadhātvārūpyadhātumityabhiniviniśante, pratītyasamutpādamityabhiniviśante, nāmarūpamityabhiniviśante, (
Vaidya 50
children.translated_text: [Vaidya p. 50]

children.text: ) rāgadveṣamohamityabhiniviśante / īrṣyāmātsaryamityabhiniviśante / asmimānamityabhiniviśante / duḥkhamityabhiniviśante / samudayamityabhiniviśante / nirodhamityabhiniviśante / mārgamityabhiniviśante / smṛtyupasthānamityabhiniviśante / samyakprahāṇāviparyāsarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgānītyabhiniviśante / dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattīnapyabhiniviśante / anutpādakṣayānabhisaṃskāramityabhiniviśante / śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmimabhiniviśante / śrāvakapratyekabuddhadharmānapyabhiniviśante / mārgamityabhiniviśante / abhijñāmapyabhiniviśante / nirvāṇamapyabhiniviśante / buddhajñānamapyabhiniviśante / lakṣaṇānyapyabhiniviśante / pratyekabuddhasaṃpadamapyabhiniviśante / bodhisattvasaṃpadamapyabhiniviśante //
children.translated_text: They cling to passion, hatred, and delusion. They cling to jealousy and miserliness. They cling to the conceit "I am." They cling to suffering. They cling to its origin. They cling to cessation. They cling to the path. They cling to the foundations of mindfulness. They cling to right exertions, non-perversions, bases of supernatural power, faculties, powers, and factors of awakening. They cling to meditations, liberations, concentrations, and attainments. They cling to non-arising, exhaustion, and non-conditioning. They cling to the <s>śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stages. They cling to the <s>dharma</s>s of <s>śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s. They cling to the path. They cling to superknowledges. They cling to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. They cling to the <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.

'The arising of mind' — this, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is an inversion (<s>viparyāsa</s>). 'Mind is mind-born' — this, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the negation of mind. For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, that which is the inherent nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) of mind neither arises nor is born. Inversion

children.text: tatra suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaḥ imānevaṃrūpānabhiniveśān sattvānāṃ viparyāsacittajān samanupaśyan na kvacidviparyāse cittamutpādayati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? cittāpagatā hi prajñāpāramitā / yā ca cittasya prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā prakṛtipariśuddhatā, tatra na kāciccittasyotpattiḥ / ārambaṇe sati suvikrāntavikrāmin bālapṛthagjanāścittamutpādayanti / tatra bodhisattvo 'pyārambaṇaṃ prajānannapi cittasyotpattiṃ prajānāti - kutaścittamutpadyate? sa evaṃ pratyavekṣate - prakṛtiprabhāsvaramidaṃ cittam / tasyaivaṃ bhavati - ārambaṇaṃ pratītya cittamutpadyate iti / sa ārambaṇaṃ parijñāya na cittamutpādayati nāpi nirodhayati / tasya taccittaṃ prabhāsvaraṃ bhavati asaṃkliṣṭaṃ kamanīyaṃ pariśuddham / sa cittānutpādasthito na kaṃciddharmamutpādayati na nirodhayati / iyaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin cittānutpādaparijñā prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ / ya evaṃ carati bodhisattvaḥ, sa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati / tasyaivaṃ carato naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ carāmi prajñāpāramitāyām, asyāṃ carāmi prajñāpāramitāyām, anena carāmi prajñāpāramitāyām, asmāccarāmi prajñāpāramitāyāmiti / sacetpunaḥ saṃjānīte - iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā, anena prajñāpāramitā, asya vā prajñāpāramiteti, na carati prajñāpāramitāyām / atha tāmapi prajñāpāramitāṃ na samanupaśyati nopalabhate - ahaṃ carāmi prajñāpāramitāyāmiti na carati, carati prajñāpāramitāyām //
children.translated_text: Therein, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, perceiving these clinging-tendencies of beings born from perversion of mind, does not give rise to mind anywhere in perversion. Why is that? Because <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is free from mind. And that which is the natural luminosity and natural purity of mind — therein there is no arising of mind. When there is an object, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, foolish ordinary beings give rise to mind. Therein the <s>bodhisattva</s>, while knowing the object, also knows the arising of mind — "From where does mind arise?" He reflects thus: "This mind is naturally luminous." It occurs to him: "Mind arises dependent on an object." Having fully comprehended the object, he does not give rise to mind.

children.text: evamukte suvikrāntavikrāmī bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - anuttareyaṃ caryā bhagavan bodhisattvasya yaduta prajñāpāramitācaryā / prabhāsvareyaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvasya caryā yaduta prajñāpāramitācaryā / niruttareyaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvasya caryā yaduta prajñāpāramitācaryā / atyadbhuteyaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvasya caryā yaduta prajñāpāramitācaryā / anavakrānteyaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvasya caryā māreṇa vā māraparṣadbhirvā anyairvā punaḥ kaiścinnimittacaritairupalambhacaritairātmadṛṣṭibhiḥ sattvadṛṣṭibhirjīvadṛṣṭibhiḥ pudgaladṛṣṭibhirbhavadṛṣṭibhirvibhavadṛṣṭibhirucchedadṛṣṭibhiḥ śāścatadṛṣṭibhiḥ satkāyadṛṣṭibhiḥ skandhadṛṣṭibhirdhātudṛṣṭibhirāyatanadṛṣṭibhirbuddhadṛṣṭibhirdharmadṛṣṭibhiḥ saṃghadṛṣṭibhirnirvāṇadṛṣṭibhiḥ prāptasaṃprajñairvā adhimānikairvā rāgadveṣamohacaritairvā (
Vaidya 51
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 51)

children.text: ) viparyāsacaritairvā utpathonmārgaprasthitairvā anākramaṇīyā / sarvalokābhyudayacaryeyaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvasya caryā yaduta prajñāpāramitācaryā //
children.translated_text: or who operate through perversions, or who have set out on wrong paths and byways — it is unassailable. This, Blessed One, is the conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s> that leads to the welfare of all the world — namely, the conduct of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

When this was said, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> said this to the Blessed One: "This is an unsurpassed conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, Blessed One — namely, the conduct of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is a luminous conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, Blessed One — namely, the conduct of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is a conduct without superior of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, Blessed One — namely, the conduct of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is a most wondrous conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, Blessed One. This is a conduct that cannot be encroached upon, Blessed One — neither by <s>Māra</s>, nor by <s>Māra</s>'s retinue, nor by any others who operate through signs, who operate through apprehension, through views of self, views of beings, views of life, views of persons, views of existence, views of non-existence, views of annihilation, views of eternalism

children.text: evamukte bhagavān suvikrāntavikrāmiṇaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - evametat suvikrāntavikrāmin, evametat / anavakrāntacaryeyaṃ bodhisattvasya māreṇa vā mārakāyikairvā devaputrairmāraparṣadā vā, antaśo nirvāṇadṛṣṭikairapi nirvāṇābhiniviṣṭairvā anākramaṇīyā sarvabālapṛthagjanairvā / yā bodhisattvānāmiyaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmiṃścaryā, neyaṃ caryā bālapṛthagjanānām / nāpīyaṃ caryā śaikṣāśaikṣāṇāṃ śrāvakayānīyānām, nāpi pratyekabuddhayānīyānām / sacet suvikrāntavikrāmin iyaṃ caryā śrāvakayānīyānāṃ vā pratyekabuddhayānīyānāṃ vā abhaviṣyat, na teṣāṃ kaścidvyavahāro 'bhaviṣyat - śrāvakayānīyā vā pratyekabuddhayānīyā veti / bodhisattvā evābhaviṣyan, te 'pi tathāgatā vā caturvaiśāradyaprāptā abhaviṣyan / yasmāttarhi suvikrāntavikrāmin na śrāvakayānīyānāṃ va pratyekabuddhayānīyānāmiyaṃ caryā, tasmātte na bodhisattvā iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchanti, na ca tathāgatā bhavanti caturvaiśāradyaprāptāḥ / vaiśāradyabhūmiriyaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin dharme, neyaṃ prajñāpāramitācaryā / evaṃ carantaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvāḥ kṣipraṃ caturvaiśāradyatāmanuprāpnuvanti, anabhisaṃbuddhā eva yāvadanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ praṇidhānavaśena ca buddhānāṃ ca bhagavatāmadhiṣṭhānavaśena / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin śrāvakayānikānāṃ vā pratyekabuddhayānikānāṃ vā caturvaiśāradyaṃ bhavati, nāpi tathāgatasteṣāṃ caturvaiśāradyamadhitiṣṭhati / bodhisattvabhūmireṣā suvikrāntavikrāmin yasyāṃ caturvaiśāradyamanuprāpyate praṇidhānavaśena / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? prajñāpāramitāyāṃ suvikrāntavikrāmiṃścaranto bodhisattvāḥ catasraḥ pratisaṃvido 'nuprāpnuvanti / katamāścatasraḥ? yaduta arthapratisaṃvidaṃ dharmapratisaṃvidaṃ niruktipratisaṃvidaṃ pratibhānapratisaṃvidam / ābhiścatasṛbhiḥ pratisaṃvidbhiḥ samanvāgatā anabhisaṃbuddhā eva praṇidhānavaśena vaiśāradyāni pratigṛhṇanti / tathāgatā api tān kuśalamūlasamanvāgatāniti viditvā prajñāpāramitābhūmyanuprāptāniti viditvā adhitiṣṭhanti caturvaiśāradyena / tasmāttarhi suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvena catasraḥ pratisaṃvido 'nuprāptukāmena kṣipraṃ caturvaiśāradyakuśalena bhavitukāmena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyaṃ caritavyam //
children.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One said to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>: "So it is, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, so it is. This conduct of the <s>bodhisattva</s> cannot be encroached upon by <s>Māra</s>, or by divine sons of <s>Māra</s>'s realm, or by <s>Māra</s>'s retinue, or even by those who hold the view of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> or who cling to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, or by any foolish ordinary beings — it is unassailable. This conduct of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is not the conduct of foolish ordinary beings. Nor is it the conduct of those in the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle, whether learners or adepts, nor of those in the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle. If, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, this conduct had belonged to those in the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle or the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, there would have been no conventional distinction — 'those of the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle' or

children.text: punaraparaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran sarvadharmāṇāṃ hetuṃ ca samudayaṃ ca astaṃgamaṃ ca nirodhaṃ ca pravidhyati na kaṃciddharmam, yatprajñāpāramitāyāṃ na yojayati / sarvadharmāṇāṃ hetusamudayanirodhamārgalakṣaṇaṃ prajānāti / teṣāṃ hetusamudayanirodhamārgalakṣaṇaṃ prajānan na rūpaṃ prabhāvayati na vibhāvayati / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārān / na vijñānaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na nāmarūpaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na saṃkleśavyavadānaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na viparyāsadṛṣṭigatanīvaraṇāni bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / (
Vaidya 52
children.translated_text: (Vaidya 52)

children.text: ) na rāgadveṣamohān bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na kāmadhātuṃ na rūpadhātuṃ nārūpyadhātuṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na sattvadhātuṃ nātmadhātuṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / nocchedadṛṣṭiṃ na śāśvatadṛṣṭiṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na dānamātsaryaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na śīladauḥśīlyaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na kṣāntivyāpādaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / va vīryakausīdyaṃ na dhyānavikṣepaṃ na prajñādauṣprajñyaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇāviparyāsarddhipādāpramāṇāni bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / nendriyabalabodhyaṅgasamādhisamāpattīrbhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na pratītyasamutpādaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgān bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / nānutpādajñānaṃ na kṣayajñānaṃ nābhisaṃskārajñānaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na pṛthagjanabhūmiṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na śrāvakabhūmiṃ na pratyekabuddhabhūmiṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na pṛthagjanadharmān na śrāvakadharmān na pratyekabuddhadharmān (na bodhisattvadharmabuddhadharmān) bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na śamathaṃ na vidarśanāṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na nirvāṇaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / nātītānāgatapratyutpannajñānadarśanaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na saṅgatāṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / nāsaṅgatāṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na buddhajñānaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / na buddhavaiśāradyāni bhāvayati na vibhāvayati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? abhāvyāni hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpavedanāsajñāsaṃskāravijñānāni / abhāvyāni nāmarūpaviparyāsadṛṣṭigatasmṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇarddhipādāviparyāsāpramāṇendriyabalabodhyaṅgasamādhisamāpattyabhijñākṣayajñānābhisaṃskārajñānāni / abhāvyā pṛthagjanabhūmiḥ, abhāvyāḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvabhūmayaḥ, abhāvyāḥ pṛthagjanaśrāvakapratyekabuddhadharmāḥ, abhāvyaṃ nirvāṇam, abhāvyamatītānāgatapratyutpannajñānadarśanam, abhāvyamasaṅgajñānadarśanam, abhāvyamanāsaṅgajñānadarśanam, abhāvyaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhajñānam / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin kācidasti bhāvapariniṣpattiḥ / abhūtā hyete sarva eva vyavahārāḥ / nātra kaścitsvabhāvaḥ / abhāvasvabhāvā hi suvikrāntavikrāmin sarvadharmāḥ, abhūtā asaṃbhūtāḥ / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? yo hi viparyāsaḥ so 'bhūtaḥ / viparyāsasamutthitāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / yo hi viparyāsaḥ, so 'bhāvaḥ / bhāvāpagatā hi suvikrāntavikrāmin sarvadharmāḥ / bhāvo nopalabhyate 'svabhāvatvāt / abhāva iti suvikrāntavikrāmin abhūtaḥ / so 'saṃbhūtaḥ, tenocyate abhāva iti / asatparidīpanaiṣā suvikrāntavikrāmin abhāva iti / yaśca abhāva, tatra na bhāvanā na vibhāvanā / viparyāsasamutthitatayā hi suvikrāntavikrāmin sattvā bhāvayanti ca vibhāvayanti ca / na tatra kiṃcidbhāvyam / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? abhāvasvabhāvā hi suvikrāntavikrāmin sarvadharmāḥ, bhāvāpagatā vastvasattvāt / na tatra kiṃcidbhāvyam / yasmin samaye suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattva evaṃ dharmeṣu dharmānudarśī viharan prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran na kaṃciddharmaṃ bhāvayati na vibhāvayati, iyamucyate prajñāpāramitābhāvaneti / evaṃ carata evaṃ viharataḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāpāramitābhāvanā paripūriṃ gacchati //
children.translated_text: He neither cultivates nor un-cultivates desire, hatred, or delusion; neither cultivates nor un-cultivates the desire realm, the form realm, or the formless realm; neither cultivates nor un-cultivates the realm of beings or the realm of self; neither cultivates nor un-cultivates the annihilationist view or the eternalist view; neither cultivates nor un-cultivates generosity and miserliness; neither cultivates nor un-cultivates morality and immorality; neither cultivates nor un-cultivates patience and ill-will; neither vigor and laziness, nor <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and distraction, nor wisdom and foolishness does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither the foundations of mindfulness, right exertions, non-perversions, bases of power, nor the immeasurables does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither the faculties, powers, factors of awakening, concentrations, nor attainments does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither dependent origination does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither suffering, origination, cessation, nor the path does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither the knowledge of non-arising, the knowledge of destruction, nor the knowledge of non-fabrication does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither the stage of the ordinary person does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither the <s>Śrāvaka</s> stage nor the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stage does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither the <s>dharmas</s> of ordinary persons, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, nor <s>Bodhisattva</s>-and-<s>Buddha</s> <s>dharmas</s> does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>) nor insight (<s>vidarśanā</s>) does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither <s>Nirvāṇa</s> does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither the knowledge and vision of past, future, and present does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither attachment does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither non-attachment does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge does he cultivate or un-cultivate; neither the <s>Buddha</s>'s fearlessnesses does he cultivate or un-cultivate. For what reason? Because, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are not to be cultivated. Name-and-form, perversions, views, foundations of mindfulness, right exertions, bases of power, non-perversions, immeasurables, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, concentrations, attainments, superknowledges, knowledge of destruction, and knowledge of non-fabrication are not to be cultivated. The stage of the ordinary person is not to be cultivated; the stages of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are not to be cultivated; the <s>dharmas</s> of ordinary persons, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> are not to be cultivated; <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not to be cultivated; knowledge and vision of past, future, and present is not to be cultivated; unattached knowledge and vision is not to be cultivated; non-unattached knowledge and vision is not to be cultivated; the knowledge of a Perfectly Awakened One is not to be cultivated. For what reason? Because, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is no accomplishment of existence whatsoever. All these are entirely unreal conventions. There is no own-nature here. All <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, are of the nature of non-existence, unreal, unarisen. For what reason? Because that which is perversion is unreal. All <s>dharmas</s> arise from perversion. That which is perversion is non-existence. All <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, are gone beyond existence. Existence is not apprehended, due to the absence of own-nature. 'Non-existence,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is unreal. It is unarisen; therefore it is called non-existence. This illumination of the unreal, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is 'non-existence.' And where there is non-existence, there is neither cultivation nor un-cultivation. Because of arising from perversion, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, beings cultivate and un-cultivate. There is nothing to be cultivated there. For what reason? Because all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, are of the nature of non-existence, gone beyond existence, due to the non-reality of things. There is nothing to be cultivated there. At the time when, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> thus dwells contemplating <s>dharmas</s> in <s>dharmas</s>, practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and neither cultivates nor un-cultivates any <s>dharma</s> — this is called the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who thus practices and thus dwells, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> reaches fulfillment.

Furthermore, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> penetrates the cause, origin, cessation, and cessation of all <s>dharma</s>s; there is no <s>dharma</s> that he does not connect with <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. He knows the characteristic of cause, origin, cessation, and path of all <s>dharma</s>s. Knowing their characteristic of cause, origin, cessation, and path, he neither cultivates nor decultivates form. Likewise with feeling, perception, and formations. He neither cultivates nor decultivates consciousness. He neither cultivates nor decultivates name-and-form. He neither cultivates nor decultivates defilement or purification. He neither cultivates nor decultivates perversions, speculative views, or hindrances.

pṛthagjanaśrāvakapratyekabuddhasamyaksaṃbuddhabhūmimupaiti, nopādatte / na pṛthagjanadharmān, na śrāvakadharmān na pratyekabuddhadharmānupaiti, nopādatte / nātītānāgatapratyutpannajñānadarśanamupaiti, Vaidya 54
children.translated_text: [Vaidya p. 54]

children.text: ) nopādānīyaṃ vā / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? asārakā hi suvikrāntavikrāmin sarvadharmā māyopamatayā / vaśitā hi sarvadharmāḥ sārānupalabdhitaḥ / pratibhāsasamā hi sarvadharmā agrāhyatāmupādāya / riktakā hi sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvāsattvāt / phenapiṇḍopamā hi sarvadharmā avimardanakṣamatvāt / budbudopamā hi sarvadharmā utpannabhaṅgavilīnatāmupādāya / marīcyupamā hi sarvadharmā viparyāsasamutthānatāmupādāya / kadalīgarbhopamā hi sarvadharmāḥ sārāsattāmupādāya / udakacandrasadṛśā hi sarvadharmā agrāhyatāmupādāya indrāyudharaṅgasadṛśā hi sarvadharmā asatparikalpanatāmupādāya / nirīhakā hi sarvadharmā asamutthāpanatāmupādāya / riktamuṣṭisamā hi sarvadharmā vaśikasvabhāvalakṣaṇatayā / tatra suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaḥ evaṃ sarvadharmān samanupaśyan na kaṃciddharmamupaiti nopādatte, nādhitiṣṭhati, nādhyavasāya tiṣṭhati / iyaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya sarvadharmaśraddadhānatā anadhiṣṭhānatā anadhyavasānatā anabhiṣvaṅgatā prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ / evaṃ carataḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitābhāvanā paripūriṃ gacchati //
children.translated_text: nor to be grasped at. For what reason? Because all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, are without essence, being like an illusion. All <s>dharmas</s> are mastered by the non-apprehension of essence. All <s>dharmas</s> are like reflections, being ungraspable. All <s>dharmas</s> are empty,

Furthermore, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, for the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, no mind arises with the sign of conjunction with form; nor with feeling, nor perception, nor formations; no mind arises with the sign of conjunction with consciousness; no mind arises accompanied by mental rigidity; no mind arises accompanied by ill-will; no mind arises accompanied by miserliness; no mind arises accompanied by defilement; no mind arises accompanied by laziness; no mind arises accompanied by distraction; no mind arises accompanied by foolishness; no mind arises accompanied by desire; no mind arises accompanied by attachment to form-objects; no mind arises accompanied by covetousness; no mind arises accompanied by slander; no mind arises accompanied by wrong view; no mind arises accompanied by attachment to wealth; no mind arises accompanied by clinging to sovereignty; no mind arises accompanied by clinging to rebirth in a great family; no mind arises accompanied by clinging to rebirth among the gods; no mind arises accompanied by clinging to the desire realm; no mind arises accompanied by clinging to the form or formless realm; no mind arises toward the <s>Śrāvaka</s> stage; no mind arises toward the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stage; no mind arises accompanied by attachment and clinging to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice; not even a mind accompanied by the hindrances and views arises. Endowed with this purity of mind, he pervades beings with loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). The perception of 'being' has been dispelled by him, yet he does not abide in the perception of 'being,' nor does he cling to the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abidings); and he becomes wise, endowed with skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>). For him who is endowed with these <s>dharmas</s> and practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> quickly reaches fulfillment. Cultivating <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> thus, he neither approaches nor grasps form; neither feeling, nor perception, nor formations; he neither approaches nor grasps consciousness; he neither approaches nor grasps the perversions, hindrances, or views; he neither approaches nor grasps the desire realm, the form realm, or the formless realm; he neither approaches nor grasps annihilationism or eternalism; he neither approaches nor grasps dependent origination; he neither approaches nor grasps the elements of earth, water, fire, or wind; he neither approaches nor grasps desire, hatred, or delusion; he neither approaches nor grasps generosity and miserliness, morality and immorality; he neither approaches nor grasps patience and ill-will, vigor and laziness, <s>dhyāna</s> and distraction, wisdom and foolishness; he neither approaches nor grasps the foundations of mindfulness, right exertions, non-perversions, immeasurables, or bases of power; he neither approaches nor grasps the faculties, powers, factors of awakening, <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, or attainments; he neither approaches nor grasps the superknowledges; he neither approaches nor grasps suffering, origination, cessation, or the path; he neither approaches nor grasps the knowledge of non-arising, the knowledge of destruction, or the knowledge of non-fabrication; he neither approaches nor grasps the realm of self, the realm of beings, or the <s>dharmadhātu</s>; he neither approaches nor grasps the stage of ordinary persons, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, or Perfectly Awakened Ones; he neither approaches nor grasps the <s>dharmas</s> of ordinary persons, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, or <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; he neither approaches nor grasps the knowledge and vision of past, future, and present; he neither approaches nor grasps unattached knowledge and vision; he neither approaches nor grasps <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, powers, and fearlessnesses; he neither approaches nor grasps the hindrances. For what reason? Because all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, are unapproached and ungrasped, not approached by anyone. For, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is to be grasped, nor has any been grasped by anyone. For what reason? Because there is nothing here to be grasped —

children.text: punaraparaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin evaṃ śikṣamāṇo bodhisattvo na rūpe śikṣate, na rūpasamatikramāya śikṣate / na vedanāyāṃ na saṃjñāyāṃ na saṃskāreṣu / na vijñāne śikṣate na vijñānasamatikramāya śikṣate / na rūpotpattau śikṣate, na rūpanirodhe śikṣate / evaṃ na vedanā na saṃjñā na saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānotpattau śikṣate, na vijñānanirodhe śikṣate / na rūpavinayāya śikṣate nāvinayāya / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānavinayāya śikṣate nāvinayāya / na rūpasya saṃkrāntaye śikṣate nāvakrāntaye / na sthitaye śikṣate nāsthitaye / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ saṃkrāntaye śikṣate nāvakrāntaye, na sthitaye śikṣate nāsthitaye / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na rūpanityatāyāṃ śikṣate, na rūpasukhatāyāṃ śikṣate, na rūpaduḥkhatāyāṃ śikṣate na rūpaśubhatāyām, na rūpānātmatāyāṃ śikṣate / na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāḥ, na vijñānanityatāyāṃ śikṣate, na vijñānasukhatāyāṃ śikṣate, na vijñānaduḥkhatāyām, na vijñānaśubhatāyāṃ na vijñānātmatāyāṃ śikṣate / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na rūpātītārambaṇe carati, rūpānāgatārambaṇe carati, na rūpapratyutpannārambaṇe carati / na vedanā, na saṃjñā, na saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānātītārambaṇe carati, nānāgatārambaṇe carati, na pratyutpannārambaṇe carati / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo 'tītaṃ śūnyākāreṇa śāntākāreṇa anātmākāreṇa pratyavekṣate - yadatītaṃ tacchūnyam, evaṃ śāntamanātmeti / evamapi [na] carati / anāgataṃ śūnyākāreṇa śāntākāreṇa anātmākāreṇa pratyavekṣate - yadatītaṃ tacchūnyaṃ śāntamanātmeti / evamapi (na) carati / pratyutpannaṃ śūnyākāreṇa śāntākāreṇa anātmākāreṇa pratyavekṣate - yatpratyutpannaṃ tacchūnyaṃ śāntamanātmeti / evamapi (na) carati / atītaṃ śūnyaṃ śāntamanātmanā vā anātmīyena (
Vaidya 55
children.translated_text: [Vaidya p. 55]

children.text: ) vā anityena vā adhruveṇa vā aśāśvatena vā vipariṇāmadharmiṇā vā, evamapi na carati / anāgataṃ śūnyaṃ śāntamanātmanā vā anātmīyena vā anityena vā adhruveṇa vā aśāśvatena vā vipariṇāmadharmiṇā vā, evamapi na carati / pratyutpannaṃ śūnyaṃ śāntamanātmanā vā anātmīyena vā anityena vā adhruveṇa vā aśāśvatena vā vipariṇāmadharmiṇā veti, evamapi na carati / evaṃ carataḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitābhāvanā paripūriṃ gacchati / evaṃ carataḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya māraḥ pāpīyānavatāraṃ na labhate / evaṃ caran sarvamārakarmāṇi budhyate, na ca tairmārakarmabhiḥ saṃhriyate //
children.translated_text: or impermanent, or unstable, or non-eternal, or of a nature to change — even so he does not practice [thus]. [Thinking] the future is empty, peaceful, without self or without anything belonging to a self, or impermanent, or unstable, or non-eternal, or of a nature to change — even so he does not practice [thus].

Furthermore, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> training in this way does not train in form, nor does he train for the transcending of form. Not in feeling, not in perception, not in formations — he does not train in consciousness, nor does he train for the transcending of consciousness.

children.text: punaraparaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin evaṃ caran bodhisattvo na rūpamālambate, na vedanāṃ na saṃjñāṃ na saṃskārān, na vijñānamālambate / na nāmarūpamālambate, na viparyāsadṛṣṭigatamālambate, nātmābhiniveśamālambate, na sattvābhiniveśamālambate, nocchedaśāśvatamālambate, nāntaṃ nānantamālambate / na rūpaśabdagandharasasparśadharmānālambate / na kāmadhātuṃ na rūpadhātuṃ nārūpyadhātumālambate / na pratītyasamutpādamālambate / na pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśadhātūnālambate / na satyaṃ na mṛṣāṃ ālambate / na saṃyogaṃ na visaṃyogamālambate / na rāgadveṣamohānālambate / na rāgadveṣamohaprahāṇamālambate / na dānamātsaryaśīladauḥśīlyamālambate / na kṣāntivyāpādamālambate / na vīryakausīdyamālambate / na dhyānavikṣepamālambate / na prajñādauṣprajñyamālambate / na smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇarddhipādāviparyāsānālambate / nendriyabalabodhyaṅgasamādhisamāpattīrālambate / na maitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣā ālambate / nānutpādajñānakṣayajñānābhisaṃskārajñānānyālambate / na pṛthagjanaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmīrālambate / na pṛthagjanaśrāvakapratyekabuddhadharmānālambate / na duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgānālambate / nābhijñājñānadarśanamālambate / na vimuktimālambate / na vimuktijñānadarśanamālambate / na nirvāṇamālambate / nātītānāgatapratyutpanna(jñānadarśana)mālambate / nāsaṅgajñānamālambate / na buddhajñānamālambate / na buddhabalavaiśāradyānyālambate / na buddhakṣetrapariśuddhimālambate / na lakṣaṇapariśuddhimālambate / na śrāvakasaṃpadamālambate / na pratyekabuddhasaṃpadamālambate / na bodhisattvasaṃpadamālambate / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? nirālambanā hi suvikrāntavikrāmin sarvadharmāḥ / na hi sarvadharmāṇāṃ kiṃcidgrahaṇaṃ saṃvidyate yatraiṣāmālambanaṃ bhaveta / yāvat suvikrāntavikrāmin ālambanam, tāvadadhyavasānam, tāvadabhiniveśaḥ, tāvadupādānam / yāvadupādānam, yāvadālambanam, tāvaduḥkhadaurmanasyam, tāvadgāḍhāḥ śokaśalyopāyāsaparidevāḥ saṃbhavanti / yāvat suvikrāntavikrāmin ālambanaṃ tāvadbandhanam / yāvadālambanaṃ tāvannāsti mārgaḥ, tāvadduḥkhadaurmanasyam / yāvadālambanaṃ tāvanmanyanā spandanā prapañcanā / yāvadālambanaṃ tāvadadhikaraṇavigrahavivādāḥ / yāvadālambanaṃ tāvadavidyāndhakāramohāḥ / yāvadālambanaṃ tāvadbhayāni, (
Vaidya 56
children.translated_text: [Vaidya p. 56]

children.text: ) tāvadbhairavāṇi / yāvadālambanaṃ tāvanmārapāśamāravidhvaṃsanāni / yāvadālambanaṃ tāvadduḥkhapratipīḍanā sukhaparyeṣaṇā ca / tatra suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattva imānādīnavān saṃpaśyan na kaṃciddharmamālambate / so 'nālambamāno na kaṃciddharmaṃ parigṛhṇāti / sa nāpyudgrahāya nāgrahāya sthitaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ tāmapi nirālambanavaśikatāṃ na manyate / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na kaṃciddharmamabhiniviśate nābhivadati, na kaṃciddharmamadhyavasāya tiṣṭhati / ayaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya sarvadharmālambanavisaṃyogaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ / evaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya carataḥ prajñāpāramitābhāvanā paripūtiṃ gacchati / na cāsya māraḥ pāpīyān antarāyaṃ śaknoti kartum, na mārakāyikā devatāḥ, na māraparṣat, na mārādhiṣṭhitāḥ / na cāsya te 'vatāraṃ labhante yatrāsya viheṭhān kuryuḥ, yatrainaṃ gṛhītvā dharṣayeyuḥ / nityaṃ ca sarvāṇi mārakarmāṇyavabudhyante / na ca mārakarmavaśago bhavati / sarvāṇi ca mārabhavanāni dhyāmīkaroti / sarvānyatīrthikānāṃ ca nigrahāya sthito bhavati, sarvāścānyatīrthikāṃścarakaparivrājakānabhibhavati / anavamardanīyaśca bhavati sarvaparapravādibhiḥ //
children.translated_text: ) so long are there terrors. So long as there is an object of support, so long are there <s>Māra</s>'s snares and <s>Māra</s>'s destructions. So long as there is an object of support, so long is there the oppression of suffering and the search for happiness. Therefore, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing these dangers, does not take any <s>dharma</s> as an object of support. Not taking any object of support, he does not grasp any <s>dharma</s>. He is established neither for grasping nor for non-grasping; he does not even regard that mastery of non-support regarding all <s>dharmas</s> as something. Thus practicing, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> does not become attached to any <s>dharma</s> nor assert any, and does not stand having determined any <s>dharma</s>. This, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s disjunction from the support of all <s>dharmas</s> while practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> reaches fulfillment for the practicing <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And <s>Māra</s> the Evil One is unable to create an obstacle for him, nor can the <s>Mārakāyika</s> gods, nor <s>Māra</s>'s assembly, nor those empowered by <s>Māra</s>. They do not find an opening where they might harm him, where they might seize and assail him. He constantly sees through all the works of <s>Māra</s>. He does not fall under the power of <s>Māra</s>'s works. He renders all of <s>Māra</s>'s realms obscure. He stands ready to subdue all followers of other paths, and he overcomes all <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist ascetics), wanderers, and mendicants. He is invincible by all proponents of other doctrines.

Furthermore, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing thus does not take form as an object of support, nor feeling, nor perception, nor formations, nor consciousness. He does not take name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) as an object of support, nor inversions and wrong views (<s>viparyāsa-dṛṣṭi</s>), nor the clinging to a self (<s>ātmābhiniveśa</s>),

children.text: evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na rūpakalpanāyāṃ sthito bhavati na rūpavikalpanāyām / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānakalpanāyāṃ sthito bhavati na vikalpanāyām / nāpi rūpaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / evaṃ na vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni kalpayati na vikalpayati / na nīvaraṇadṛṣṭigatāni kalpayati na vikalpayati / nocchedaśāśvataṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na kāmadhāturūpadhātvārūpyadhātūn kalpayati na vikalpayati / na rāgadveṣamohān kalpayati na vikalpayati / na satyaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na mṛṣā kalpayati na vikalpayati / na pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśadhātuṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na saṃyogaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na visaṃyogaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na pratītyasamutpādaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / nātmasaṃjñāṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na sattvasaṃjñāṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na jīvasaṃjñāṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na pudgalasaṃjñāṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na dānamātsaryaśīladauḥśīlyaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na kṣāntivyāpādau kalpayati na vikalpayati / na vīryakausīdyaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na dhyānavikṣepau kalpayati na vikalpayati / na prajñādauṣprajñye kalpayati na vikalpayati / nāviparyāsasamyakprahāṇarddhipādasmṛtyupasthānāni kalpayati na vikalpayati / nendriyabalabodhyaṅgasamādhisamāpattīḥ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgān kalpayati na vikalpayati / na maitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣāḥ kalpayati na vikalpayati / nānutpādajñānakṣayajñānābhisaṃskārajñānāni kalpayati na vikalpayati / na pṛthagjanadharmān na śrāvakadharmān na pratyekabuddhadharmān na buddhadharmān kalpayati na vikalpayati / (
Vaidya 57

children.text: ) na pṛthagjanabhūmiṃ na śrāvakabhūmiṃ na pratyekabuddhabhūmiṃ na buddhabhūmiṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na nīvaraṇāni kalpayati na vikalpayati / nātītānāgatapratyutpannajñānadarśanaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / nāsaṅgajñānaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na vidyāvimuktiṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na muktiṃ na vimuktijñānadarśanaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na buddhajñānavaiśāradyāni kalpayati na vikalpayati / na lakṣaṇapariśuddhiṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na śrāvakasaṃpadaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na pratyekabuddhasaṃpadaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / na bodhisattvasaṃpadaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? kalpanāyāṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin satyāṃ vikalpo bhavati / yatra punaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin kalpanā nāsti, na tatra vikalpanā / sarvabālapṛthagjanā hi suvikrāntavikrāmin kalpanāsamutthitāḥ / teṣāṃ saṃjñā vikalpasamutthitāḥ / te kalpayanti vikalpayanti ca / kalpaneti suvikrāntavikrāmin eṣa eko 'ntaḥ, vikalpaneti dvitīyo 'ntaḥ / yatra nāsti kalpo vā vikalpo (vā), tatra nāsti anto vā madhyaṃ vā / madhyamiti suvikrāntavikrāmin kalpayataḥ sa evānto bhavati / yāvatkalpanā, tāvadvikalpanā / nāstyatra vikalpanāsamucchedaḥ / yatra punaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin na kalpanā na vikalpanā, tatra kalpasamucchedaḥ / kalpasamuccheda iti suvikrāntavikrāmin nātra kasyacicchedaḥ / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? anto hi suvikrāntavikrāmin kalpo vikalpo vikalpasamutthitaḥ / teṣāṃ yo vyupaśamaḥ, so 'viparyāsaḥ / yo 'viparyāsaḥ, na tatra kaścicchedaḥ / samuccheda iti suvikrāntavikrāmin duḥkhasamucchedasyaitadadhivacanam / na ca duḥkhasya kaścitsamucchedaḥ / syādduḥkhasamucchedaḥ, yadi duḥkhasya kācitpariniṣpattiḥ syāt / apariniṣpattidarśanametat duḥkhasamuccheda iti / duḥkhaparijñānametat, yadidaṃ duḥkhasamuccheda iti / yo duḥkhaṃ naiva kalpayati na vikalpayati, ayaṃ duḥkhavyupaśamaḥ, ayaṃ duḥkhasyānutpādo 'prādurbhāvaḥ / sa evaṃ paśyan suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvo na kaṃciddharmaṃ kalpayati na vikalpayati / iyaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya sarva(kalpa)vikalpaparijñā prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ / evaṃ carataḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitābhāvanā paripūriṃ gacchati / na cāsya māraḥ pāpīyānantarāyasthito bhavati, na ca māraparṣat / utpannotpannāni ca mārakarmāṇi budhyate / na cotpannotpannānāṃ mārakarmaṇāṃ vaśaṃ gacchati / mārasya ca pāpīyasaḥ parājayaṃ karoti dhyāmīkaroti ca / evamalpapakṣīkaroti vigatabhayabhairavaśca bhavati / na ca mārairākramaṇīyo bhavati / prasrabdhāni cāsya saṃbhavanti sarvāṇyapāyagamanāni / pithitāśca bhavanti kumārgāḥ / sarvaughottīrṇaśca bhavati, vigatamohāndhakāraśca bhavati, pratilabdhacakṣurālokabhūtaśca bhavati sarvasattvānām, sthitaśca bhavatyunucchedāya buddhavaṃśasya, pratilabdhamārgaśca bhavati mārgasamatāyām, anukampa(ka)śca (
children.translated_text: ) He neither imagines nor discriminates the stage of ordinary persons, the stage of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, the stage of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, or the stage of <s>Buddhas</s>. He neither imagines nor discriminates hindrances. He neither imagines nor discriminates the knowledge and vision of the past, future, and present. He neither imagines nor discriminates unattached knowledge. He neither imagines nor discriminates knowledge and liberation. He neither imagines nor discriminates release or the knowledge and vision of liberation. He neither imagines nor discriminates the <s>Buddha</s>'s knowledge and fearlessnesses. He neither imagines nor discriminates the purification of marks. He neither imagines nor discriminates the purification of <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields). He neither imagines nor discriminates the attainments of <s>Śrāvakas</s>. He neither imagines nor discriminates the attainments of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. He neither imagines nor discriminates the attainments of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, where there is imagining, there is discrimination. But where, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is no imagining, there is no discrimination. All foolish ordinary persons, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, have arisen from imagining. Their perceptions arise from discrimination. They imagine and discriminate. 'Imagining,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is one extreme; 'discriminating' is the second extreme. Where there is neither imagining nor discriminating, there is neither extreme nor middle. 'Middle,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, for one who imagines, becomes itself an extreme. So long as there is imagining, so long is there discriminating. There is no cutting off of discrimination here. But where, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, there is neither imagining nor discriminating, there is the cutting off of imagining. 'The cutting off of imagining,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, means that here there is no cutting off of anything. For what reason? Because, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the extremes of imagining and discriminating have arisen from discrimination. Their pacification is non-perversion. And in non-perversion, there is no cutting off of anything. 'Cutting off,' <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is a designation for the cutting off of suffering. And there is no cutting off whatsoever of suffering. There would be a cutting off of suffering if there were any completion of suffering. This is the perception of non-completion — called 'the cutting off of suffering.' This is the full knowledge of suffering — that which is called 'the cutting off of suffering.' One who neither imagines nor discriminates suffering — this is the pacification of suffering, this is the non-arising and non-appearance of suffering. Thus seeing, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> neither imagines nor discriminates any <s>dharma</s>. This, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s full knowledge of all imagining and discrimination while practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Thus for the practicing <s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> reaches fulfillment. <s>Māra</s> the Evil One is not established as an obstacle for him, nor is <s>Māra</s>'s assembly. He perceives the works of <s>Māra</s> as they arise. He does not fall under the power of the arising works of <s>Māra</s>. He defeats and renders obscure <s>Māra</s> the Evil One. Thus he diminishes [<s>Māra</s>'s power] and becomes free from fear and terror. He is not to be assailed by <s>Māras</s>. All his paths to lower rebirths subside. The wrong paths are blocked. He has crossed beyond all floods. He is free from the darkness of delusion. He becomes a light and eye for all beings. He stands for the non-interruption of the <s>Buddha</s>'s lineage. He has attained the path in the equality of the path. He is compassionate (

children.text: ) bhavati sarvasattvānām, viśuddhaṃ cakṣurbhavati dharmeṣu, vīryasaṃpannaśca bhavatyakusīdaḥ, kṣāntibalapratilabdhaśca bhavatyavyāpannacittaḥ, dhyāyī ca bhavatyaniśritadhyāyī, pratilabdhaprajñaśca bhavati nirvedhikaprajñāsamanvāgataḥ, vigatakaukṛtyaśca bhavati apagatanīvaraṇaḥ, visaṃyuktaśca bhavati sarvamārapāśaiḥ, chinnabandhanaśca bhavati sarvatṛṣṇājālaviyogāt, upasthitasmṛtiśca bhavatyasaṃpramoṣadharmatayā, viśuddhaśīlaśca bhavati śīlaviśuddhipāramitāprāptaḥ, paramaguṇapratiṣṭhitaśca bhavati sarvadoṣanirghātāya, prajñābalādhānaprāptaśca bhavatyaprakampyatayā, anākṣiptaśva bhavati sarvamāraparavādibhiḥ, aparihīṇadharmā ca bhavati sarvadharmaviśuddhiprāptatayā, viśāradaśca bhavati sarvadharmadeśanāyām, amaṅkuśca bhavati parṣadupasaṃkramaṇāya, anāgṛhītaśca bhavati muktatyāgo dharmadānam (?), prativiśodhitamārgaśca bhavati mārgasamatayā, vibhāvitabhāvanaśca bhavati kumārgāparijñatayā, vāsitavāsanaśca bhavati viśuddhadharmatayā, śodhitaśodhanaśca bhavati viśuddhaprajñatayā, gambhīraprajñaśca bhavati sāgaropamatayā, duravagāhaśca bhavati astambhitatayā, aprameyaśca bhavati dharmasāgarāprameyatayā / evaṃ caran suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaḥ ebhiścānyaiśca guṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati yeṣāṃ guṇānāṃ na paryantaḥ śakyo 'dhigantum //
children.translated_text: ) he becomes a light for all beings; his eye becomes pure in <s>dharmas</s>; he becomes endowed with vigor and is not lazy; he has attained the power of patience and his mind is free from ill-will; he is a meditator, meditating without reliance; he has attained wisdom and is endowed with penetrating <s>Prajñā</s>; he is free from remorse, the hindrances having departed; he is released from all the snares of <s>Māra</s>; his bonds are cut through separation from the entire net of craving; his mindfulness is established through the nature of non-forgetfulness; his morality is pure, having attained the perfection of moral purity; he is established in supreme virtues for the eradication of all faults; he has attained the power of wisdom and is unshakable; he is not led astray by any <s>Māras</s> or opponents; he is one whose <s>dharmas</s> have not declined, having attained the purity of all <s>dharmas</s>; he is confident in teaching all <s>dharmas</s>; he is without hesitation in approaching assemblies; he is unattached, having freely relinquished — [giving] the gift of <s>Dharma</s>; his path has been cleansed by the equality of the path; his cultivation has been discerned through the comprehension of wrong paths; he is perfumed with the perfume of pure <s>Dharma</s>-nature; his purification has been cleansed through the purity of wisdom; he has profound wisdom through being like the ocean; he is unfathomable through being unshakable; he is immeasurable through the immeasurability of the ocean of <s>Dharma</s>. Practicing thus, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is endowed with these and other virtues whose limit cannot be reached.

Thus practicing, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not stand in the imagining of form, nor in the discriminating of form. Likewise, he does not stand in the imagining or discriminating of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness. Nor does he imagine or discriminate form; likewise not feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness. He neither imagines nor discriminates hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>) or views (<s>dṛṣṭigata</s>). He neither imagines nor discriminates annihilationism or eternalism. He neither imagines nor discriminates the desire realm, the form realm, or the formless realm. He neither imagines nor discriminates passion, hatred, or delusion. He neither imagines nor discriminates truth. He neither imagines nor discriminates falsehood. He neither imagines nor discriminates earth, water, fire, wind, space, or consciousness-element. He neither imagines nor discriminates conjunction. He neither imagines nor discriminates disjunction. He neither imagines nor discriminates dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). He neither imagines nor discriminates the notion of self. He neither imagines nor discriminates the notion of a being. He neither imagines nor discriminates the notion of a life-force. He neither imagines nor discriminates the notion of a person. He neither imagines nor discriminates giving and miserliness, morality and immorality. He neither imagines nor discriminates patience and ill-will. He neither imagines nor discriminates vigor and indolence. He neither imagines nor discriminates meditation and distraction. He neither imagines nor discriminates wisdom and lack of wisdom. He neither imagines nor discriminates non-perversions, right exertions, bases of supernatural power, or foundations of mindfulness. He neither imagines nor discriminates faculties, powers, factors of awakening, concentrations, or attainments. He neither imagines nor discriminates suffering, its origin, cessation, or the path. He neither imagines nor discriminates loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, or equanimity. He neither imagines nor discriminates the knowledge of non-arising, the knowledge of extinction, or the knowledge of conditioning. He neither imagines nor discriminates the <s>dharmas</s> of ordinary persons, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, or <s>Buddhas</s>. (

children.text: punaraparaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaḥ evaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran nendriyavikalo bhavati / sa na rūpavikalo bhavati, na bhogavikalo bhavati, na parivāravikalo bhavati, na jātivikalo bhavati, na kulavikalo bhavati, na deśavikalo bhavati, na ca pratyunteṣu janapadeṣūpapadyate, na cākṣaṇaprāpto bhavati, na cāpariśuddhaiḥ sattvairapariśuddhakarmāntaiḥ saṃsargajāto bhavati, na ca svacittaṃ hāpayati, na ca prajñāyā hīyate / sa yān dharmān parataḥ śṛṇoti, tān sarvadharmasamatāyāṃ saṃsyandayati, sthitaśca bhavati buddhavaṃśasya sarvajñatāvaṃśasyānupacchedāya / sa ālokalabdhaśca bhavati buddhadharmeṣu, atyāsannaśca bhavati sarvajñatāyām / taṃ sacenmāraḥ pāpīyān upasaṃkrāmati viheṭhanārtham, sa tanmāraparṣadaṃ bhasmīkaroti chinnapratibhānām, sarvāṃśca mārapāśāṃśchinatti, sarvairmārakāyikairmārakoṭibhiścādhṛṣyo bhavati / tato mārā bhītāstrastāḥ palāyante / evaṃ ca mārasya pāpīyaso bhavati - atikrāntaviṣayo 'yaṃ mama, nāyaṃ mama bhūyo viṣaye carati, nāyaṃ mama bhūyo viṣaye sthitaḥ, nāyaṃ mama bhūyo viṣayamākramiṣyatīti, anyāṃśca sattvān mama viṣayānmocayiṣyatīti, uttārayiṣyatīti / tatra māraḥ pāpīyān śocati krandati paridevate - alpapakṣīkariṣyati ayaṃ bodhisattvo māmiti / daurbalyaṃ cāsya viśati, duḥkhitaśca bhavati durmanā vipratisārī / yasmiṃśca samaye suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati, prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayati, prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yogamāpadyate, sarvamārabhavanāni tasmin samaye dhyāmībhavanti alpatejaskāni, mārāśca pāpīyāṃso duḥkhitā durmanaso bhavanti śokaśalyasamarpitā mahāśokaśalyaviddhāḥ - ativāhayiṣyatyayaṃ bata sattvānasmadviṣayāt, uttārayiṣyatyayaṃ (
Vaidya 59
children.translated_text: [<s>Vaidya</s> 59]

children.text: ) sattvānasmadviṣayāt, parimocayiṣyatyayaṃ sattvānasmadviṣayāt, abhyuddhariṣyatyayaṃ bata sattvānasmadviṣayāt, chedayiṣyatyayaṃ sattvān mārapāśāt, samutkṣepsyatyayaṃ sattvān kāmapaṅkalagnān, mocayiṣyatyayaṃ sattvān dṛṣṭijālebhyaḥ, uttārayiṣyatyayaṃ sattvān nīvaraṇapathāt, pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyatyayaṃ sattvān sanmārge, uttārayiṣyatyayaṃ sattvān dṛṣṭigahanāditi / imamarthavaśaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin saṃpaśyantaste mārā duḥkhitā bhavanti durmanasaḥ śokaśalyaviddhāḥ / tadyathāpi nāma suvikrāntavikrāmin puruṣo mahatā dhanaskandhena vipannena duḥkhito vedanātta(rta)manā mahatā duḥkhadaurmanasyena samanvāgataḥ / evameva māraḥ pāpīyān duḥkhito bhavati durmanā vipratisārī śokaśalyaviddhaḥ / na ca svake āsane ramate, yasmin samaye bodhisattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati, prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayati, prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yogamāpadyate / punaraparaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin te mārāḥ pāpīyāṃsaḥ ekataḥ samāgamya cintayanti - kathaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ, kiṃ nu kariṣyāmaḥ / kathaṃkathāśokaśalyaviddhā bhavanti / te kathaṃkathāśokaśalyaviddhā bhūtvā upasaṃkrāmanti bodhisattvasyāvatāragaveṣiṇaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ / tatra bodhisattvasya romāpi na hṛṣyati, na punaḥ kāyasyānyathātvaṃ bhaviṣyati cittasyānyathātvaṃ vā / vigatabhayaromaharṣaśca māraḥ pāpīyāniti saṃbudhyate / buddhvā cādhiṣṭhānaṃ karoti / tato māraḥ pāpīyānadhiṣṭhito durbalo bhavati līnacitto bhayamāpannaḥ / na cāsya śaknotyavatāraṃ labdhum / tasyaivaṃ bhavati - ahamevāsya na śakto 'vatāraṃ labdhum, kiṃ punarmama parṣat, kiṃ punaryadanye 'dhiṣṭhāsyanti / tataste mārā(strastā utsāhapa)rihīṇāḥ svabhavanāni gatvā duḥkhadaurmanasyajātāḥ pradhyāyantastiṣṭhanti, na ca śaknuvanti bodhisattvasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carato 'cchaṭāmātramapi cittasya mohanaṃ kartum, prāgevāsyāntarāyam / iyaṃ(daṃ) suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carato (bodhisattvasya) evaṃrūpaṃ prajñābalādhiṣṭhānaṃ bhavati, evaṃrūpeṇa ca prajñābalādhiṣṭhānena samanvāgato bhavati / sacedye sarvasmiṃstrisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ, te sarve mārā bhaveyuḥ, te sarve mahatībhirmāraparṣadbhiḥ sārdhaṃ taṃ bodhisattvaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carantamupasaṃkrameyurviheṭhābhiprāyāḥ / te 'pi sarve suvikrāntavikrāmin mārāḥ pāpīyāṃso na prabhavantyantarāyaṃ kartum / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathārūpeṇa hi prajñābalādhānena prajñākhaḍgena prajñāśastreṇa tasmin samaye bodhisattvaḥ samanvāgato bhavati / acintyayā suvikrāntavikrāmin prajñayā aprameyayā asamasamayā bodhisattvastadā samanvāgato bhavati / tena taṃ na pratibalo bhavati māraḥ pāpīyānabhibhavitum / mahāśastraṃ hyetatsuvikrāntavikrāmin yaduta prajñāśastram, mahākhaḍgo hyeṣa suvikrāntavikrāmin yaduta prajñākhaḍgaḥ, yatrāgatiraviṣayo mārāṇāṃ pāpīyasām, abhūmirmārāṇāṃ pāpīyasām / ye 'pi tāvatsuvikrāntavikrāmin bāhyā ṛṣayaścaturṇāṃ dhyānānāṃ lābhinaḥ, catasṛṇāṃ vā ārūpyasamāpattīnām, ye māraviṣayaṃ kāmadhātumatikramya brahmaloke copapadyante caturṣu ca ārūpyeṣu (
children.translated_text: ) will liberate beings from our domain, will rescue beings from our domain, will cut beings free from the snares of <s>Māra</s>, will lift beings out who are stuck in the mud of sense pleasures, will free beings from the nets of wrong views, will deliver beings from the path of hindrances, will establish beings on the right path, will deliver beings from the thicket of wrong views!' Seeing this purpose, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, those <s>Māras</s> become miserable, dejected, pierced by the arrow of grief. Just as, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, a person who has lost a great mass of wealth becomes miserable, tormented by feeling, endowed with great suffering and dejection — just so <s>Māra</s> the Evil One becomes miserable, dejected, regretful, pierced by the arrow of grief. And he finds no delight upon his own seat at the time when the <s>bodhisattva</s> practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, cultivates <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and applies himself to <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, those Evil <s>Māras</s>, gathering together, think: 'What shall we do? What can we do?' They are pierced by the arrow of perplexity and grief. Pierced by the arrow of perplexity and grief, they approach the <s>bodhisattva</s> who practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, seeking an opening. But not even a hair of the <s>bodhisattva</s> bristles, much less will there be any alteration of his body or alteration of his mind. And he realizes: 'This is <s>Māra</s> the Evil One — one whose fear and bristling hair have departed.' Having realized this, he makes a firm resolve. Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, being overcome by that resolve, becomes weak, his mind sinks, and he is seized by fear. And he cannot find an opening. He thinks: 'I myself cannot find an opening — how much less my retinue, how much less those whom others would send!' Then those <s>Māras</s>, frightened and having lost all enthusiasm, return to their own abodes and sit dejected, overcome with suffering and dejection, and they are unable to cause even a snap-of-the-finger's worth of confusion to the mind of the <s>bodhisattva</s> who practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, much less an obstacle to him. This, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is the power of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s firm resolve in wisdom while practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and he is endowed with such power of the firm resolve of wisdom. Even if all beings in the entire trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>) were to become <s>Māras</s>, and all of them, together with their great retinues of <s>Māra</s>, were to approach that <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with the intention to harm — even all those Evil <s>Māras</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, would be unable to create an obstacle. Why? Because at that time the <s>bodhisattva</s> is endowed with such power of the firm resolve of wisdom, with the sword of wisdom, with the weapon of wisdom. With inconceivable, immeasurable, incomparably equal wisdom the <s>bodhisattva</s> is then endowed, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>. Therefore <s>Māra</s> the Evil One is unable to overcome him. For this is the great weapon, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> — namely, the weapon of wisdom; this is the great sword, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s> — namely, the sword of wisdom; wherein Evil <s>Māras</s> have no access, which is beyond the range of Evil <s>Māras</s>, which is not the ground of Evil <s>Māras</s>. Even those, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, who are external <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) and have attained the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), or the four formless attainments, who have transcended the domain of <s>Māra</s> — the desire realm — and are reborn in the <s>Brahma</s>-world or in the four formless states (

children.text: ) bhavati, na lakṣaṇasaṃpattiniśrito bhavati, na buddhakṣetrasaṃpanniśrito bhavati, na śrāvakavyūhasaṃpanniśrito bhavati, na bodhisattvavyūhasaṃpanniśrito bhavati / sa sarvadharmaiścāniśrito na calati na saṃcalati, niśrayāśca tena sarve vibhāvitā bhavanti / aniśritaśca sa mārgamapi nābhiniviśate, aniśrayaṃ na manyate / so 'yaṃ niśraya iti nopalabhate, iha niśraya iti nopalabhate, asya niśraya iti nopalabhate na manyate, asmānniśraya iti nopalabhate na manyate / sarvaniśrayānamanyamāno 'nupalabhamāno 'nabhiniviśamānaḥ na kvacinniśrayamupaiti nopadiśati nābhinandati nādhyavasāya tiṣṭhati / sa sarvaniśrayānupalipto 'saktaḥ sarvadharmaniśrayaviśuddhimanuprāpnoti / idaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattvasya sarvadharmaniśrayaviśuddhijñānadarśanaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ, yenāsya mārāḥ pāpīyāṃso 'vatāraṃ na labhante, anākramaṇīyaśca bhavati sarvamāraiḥ pāpīyobhiḥ, abhibhavati ca mārān pāpīyasa iti //
children.translated_text: depend [on anything]. One does not depend on the excellence of marks, does not depend on the excellence of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, does not depend on the excellence of the <s>śrāvaka</s> array, does not depend on the excellence of the <s>bodhisattva</s> array. Not depending on any <s>dharma</s>s, one neither stirs nor is shaken, and all dependencies are thereby analyzed. And being without dependence, one does not even cling to the path; one does not conceive non-dependence. One does not apprehend "this is dependence," one does not apprehend "dependence is here," one does not apprehend or conceive "this belongs to dependence," one does not apprehend or conceive "from this comes dependence." Not conceiving, not apprehending, not clinging to any dependence whatsoever, one does not approach any dependence, does not point it out, does not delight in it, does not remain established in it.

Furthermore, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who thus practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not lack sense faculties. He does not lack in physical form, nor in enjoyments, nor in retinue, nor in birth, nor in family, nor in country; he is not reborn in frontier regions; he does not encounter inopportune conditions; he does not come into contact with impure beings of impure conduct; he does not lose his own mind, nor does he decline in wisdom. Whatever <s>dharmas</s> he hears from others, he channels them all into the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, and he stands for the unbroken continuity of the <s>Buddha</s>-lineage, the lineage of omniscience. He has obtained light regarding the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, and he is very near to omniscience. If <s>Māra</s> the Evil One approaches him to cause harm, he reduces that army of <s>Māra</s> to ashes, striking them speechless, and cuts through all the snares of <s>Māra</s>, and he is invincible to all the hosts of <s>Māra</s>, to <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Māras</s>. Then the <s>Māras</s>, frightened and terrified, flee. And <s>Māra</s> the Evil One thinks: 'This one has gone beyond my domain; he no longer moves in my domain; he no longer stands in my domain; he will no longer tread upon my domain; and he will free other beings from my domain, he will deliver them!' Thereupon <s>Māra</s> the Evil One grieves, cries, and laments: 'This <s>bodhisattva</s> will diminish my following!' Weakness enters him, and he becomes miserable, dejected, and regretful. And at the time when the <s>bodhisattva</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, cultivates <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and applies himself to <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — at that time all the abodes of <s>Māra</s> become dim and lose their radiance, and the Evil <s>Māras</s> become miserable and dejected, pierced by the arrow of grief, struck by the great arrow of sorrow: 'Alas, this one will lead beings away from our domain, will deliver beings from our domain (

children.text: punaraparaṃ suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhisattva ādita eva anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāvutpanne citte bahukuśalamūlasaṃbhārasamudāgataśca bhavati, bahubuddhaparyupāsitaśca bhavati, bahubuddhaparipṛcchakaśca bhavati, kṛtādhikāraśca bhavati buddhānāṃ bhagavatām, adhyāśayasaṃpannaśca bhavati, dānasaṃvibhāgarataśca bhavati, śīlaviśuddhigurukaśca bhavati, kṣāntisauratyasaṃpannaśca bhavati, vīryavāṃśca bhavati, vīryaviśuddhigurukaḥ, dhyānaviśuddhigurukaśca bhavati, prajñāvāṃśca bhavati, prajñāviśuddhigurukaḥ / so 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādya prajñāpāramitāyāmabhiyukto mārān pāpīyaso 'dhitiṣṭhati tena prajñābalena ca - yathā me mārāḥ pāpīyāṃso 'vatāraṃ na labheran, mā ca me viheṭhāṃ kuryuḥ / tasyādhiṣṭhāne mārā avatāraṃ na labhante, na cāsyāntarāyāya pratyupasthitā bhavanti, nāpi cittamutpādayanti - kimiti vayamasya bodhisattvasya avatāraṃ gaveṣāmahe, viheṭhanāṃ kuryāmaha iti / sacetteṣāṃ cittamutpadyate 'ntarāyāya, tato mahāvyasanamātmanaḥ saṃjānate, bhayaṃ ca teṣāṃ mahatpratyupasthitaṃ bhavati, saṃvignāśca bhavanti - mā vayaṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ na bhaviṣyāma iti / te tadviheṭhanācittaṃ punarapi pratisaṃharanti / punarapi teṣāṃ te cittotpādā antardhīyante / anenāpi suvikrāntavikrāmin paryāyeṇa bodhisattvasya mārāḥ pāpīyāṃso 'ntarāyāya prayupasthitā avatāraṃ na labhante //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, from the very beginning, upon generating the mind of unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttara samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), comes to possess an accumulation of many wholesome roots; one has attended upon many <s>Buddha</s>s; one has questioned many <s>Buddha</s>s; one has performed meritorious deeds for the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>s; one is endowed with noble aspiration (<s>adhyāśaya</s>); one delights in giving and sharing; one regards the purity of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) as weighty; one is endowed with patience and gentleness; one possesses vigor and regards the purity of vigor as weighty; one regards the purity of meditation as weighty; one possesses wisdom and regards the purity of wisdom as weighty. Having generated the mind of unsurpassed perfect awakening, one devoted to <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> overcomes the evil <s>Māra</s>s.
